title: Director Menu Strategy and Innovation (U.S. & Canada)
description:
We have an exciting opportunity for a Director of Marketing, Menu Strategy & Innovation located at our corporate headquarters in Bloomington, MN. At Dairy Queen (DQ), menu strategy and product innovation marketing is the engine of our success and will play a lead role in meeting key business growth objectives in scaling the business from $7 billion today to $10 billion by 2030. The Menu Strategy & Product Innovation team fuels brand growth by staying relentlessly curious—keeping a finger on the pulse of the restaurant industry, competitive landscape, and evolving consumer behaviors. That curiosity uncovers new opportunities that fit the brand, excite guests, and drives profitable growth.

The Director of Marketing, Menu Strategy & Innovation will play a critical role in shaping the future growth of the menu at DQ by translating consumer, competitive, and marketplace insights into decisive short‑term actions and bold, long‑term strategy. This role owns the holistic performance and direction of assigned product categories—leading both day‑to‑day category management and the development of multi-year category strategies and growth plans.

This role is responsible for driving strategic growth by uncovering incremental and breakthrough opportunities across the DQ Menu including platform innovation, product line extensions, flavor strategy and menu rationalization initiatives—driving focus and prioritization on what will matter the most to grow the business.

At the hub of the wheel, the Director of Marketing, Menu Strategy & Innovation is a full‑spectrum business leader—setting direction, stewarding iconic products, and leading cross‑functional teams through complexity to deliver results and drive growth for the overall business.

This role establishes and nurtures strong partnerships through the use of strong project management skills and as a champion of the stage gate process that ensures alignment, buy‑in, and seamless execution across Product Development, Operations, Supply Chain, and Marketing.

This is a high‑impact opportunity for a dynamic, data‑driven marketer who thrives in a fast‑paced foodservice operating environment and has a proven ability to translate consumer insights into profitable business outcomes. The ideal candidate brings strong stakeholder leadership, comfort navigating ambiguity, and the ability to make and champion bold strategic choices across product innovation, pricing, and promotion.

If you’re passionate about purpose‑driven category leadership, cultural relevance, and shaping the future of an iconic brand through its products, this role puts you at the center of it all.

Strategic Planning Leadership

  • Develop short, mid and long term product and menu growth strategies to drive positive transactions, gross margin, and sales through new products and disciplined portfolio optimization grounded in business, consumer, competitive, and market insights.
  • Prioritize areas of focus for assigned categories for incremental and breakthrough prodcut innovation, line extensions, pricing and promotion opportunities, and menu rationalization to strengthen portfolio health.
  • Partner with calendar development and marketing communications to shape annual marketing plans and integrate categories into key windows and tactics that drive the business and brand growth.
  • Lead the annual learning agenda with Analytics & Insights, identifying priority questions and translating findings into strategic action to drive transactions, gross margin and sales.

Innovation & Product Development

  • Translate category strategy into clear innovation briefs and development frameworks that guide consumer-led concepts and priorities.
  • Lead innovation governance and stage-gate decisions, ensuring teams are prepared with strong learning plans, clear recommendations, and decision-ready materials.
  • Resolve critical issues across innovation and product development while protecting brand integrity and decision quality.
  • Ensure initiatives are operationally viable and scale-ready by incorporating feasibility, supply continuity, risk, and launch-readiness considerations early in development.
  • Integrate marketing and promotional considerations so launches are on-brand, consumer-ready, and commercially effective.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Franchisee Leadership

  • Build strong, two-way partnerships with franchisee leadership to ensure category and product strategies reflect operator realities and deliver in-store value.
  • Serve as a senior liaison to franchisee leadership councils, communicating product strategies and implications while incorporating feedback to strengthen outcomes.
  • Partner with Marketing, Calendar Development, Product Development, Operations, Supply Chain, and Menu Execution teams to align priorities and execution through the stage-gate process.
  • Build alignment across stakeholders by clarifying priorities, navigating trade-offs, and removing barriers to execution across the system.
  • Present category strategies, innovation direction, and performance updates to senior leadership to support informed decisions and organizational alignment.
  • Exceptional executive communication and storytelling skills, including the ability to clearly articulate strategy, build alignment, and influence senior leadership and franchise partners.

Management of Product Marketing Professionals

  • Lead and develop a high-performing Product Marketing team, setting clear expectations for strategic thinking, decision quality, and impact.
  • Coach direct reports as category and business leaders, strengthening capabilities in strategy, innovation leadership, cross-functional influence, and executive communication.
  • Establish clear operating models, roles, and ways of working that enable focus, pace, accountability, and high-quality output.
  • Build bench strength through talent development, succession planning, performance management, and ongoing feedback.
  • Foster a collaborative, curious culture that encourages constructive challenge, shared ownership, and strong enterprise leadership.

The US national base salary range for this position is $167,884 - $209,856. This position is also eligible for a bonus. The base salary range displayed reflects the targeted hiring range for positions across all US locations. Individual pay is determined by job-related skills, work location and relevant education or experience.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of significant progressive leadership experience in product marketing, brand management, product management, or category strategy, ideally within QSR, foodservice, retail, or consumer packaged goods.
  • Proven experience leading multi‑year category or portfolio strategies, translating consumer and market insights into growth‑driving product, innovation, and menu decisions.
  • Deep experience operating within cross‑functional, matrixed organizations, partnering closely with Product Development, Operations, Supply Chain, Analytics & Insights, and Marketing.
  • Experience building and leading high‑performing teams in fast‑paced environments.

Work Environment

Most positions located out of our global headquarters in Bloomington, MN will work a hybrid work schedule where you will work 3 collaboration days a week. Additional in office time may be required to support team/project needs.

Inclusion & Belonging

We are committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging for all who touch DQ. We believe in and commit to fostering a community where employees bring their authentic selves to work, and where we recruit, engage, and retain employees, franchise owners, and suppliers based on qualifications and merit. We strive to maintain an environment where everyone feels welcome.

title: Supply/Inventory Planner
description:
SUPPLY & INVENTORY PLANNER

Job Description

ABOUT MARKETLAB

Marketlab is a market-leading healthcare solutions organization specializing in the design, manufacturing, and sourcing of private-label healthcare products. Our mission is to provide healthcare partners timely, practical solutions grounded in deep understanding of their work. Every day, we strive to positively impact the lives of the people who, in turn, support the health and wellness of our communities.

Based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, Marketlab’s success is built on collaboration, accountability, and operational excellence. Strong systems, clear data, and trusted partnerships are foundational to how we operate and scale.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Marketlab is in the midst of an exciting transformation, and we are looking for an analytically driven Supply & Inventory Planner to serve as the architect of our inventory replenishment engine. In this high-impact role, you will take ownership of the quantitative models governing more than 20,000 commercial SKUs and manufacturing components across our national distribution network and internal manufacturing site. You will lead our quarterly ABC/ROP optimization, collaborate with strategic suppliers on capacity planning, orchestrate seamless product lifecycle transitions, and positively impact customer fill rates for Tier 1 healthcare distributors and health systems. Partnering cross-functionally with Data & Analytics, Product Management, and Purchasing, you will modernize planning workflows, optimize NetSuite parameters, and directly influence working capital, service levels, and EBITDA. If you are energized by turning complex datasets into proactive operational stability and want high-visibility ownership in a growing healthcare organization, this is the role for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • As the architect of inventory planning governance, you’ll take full operational ownership of the ABC classification and Reorder Point (ROP) optimization cycle across 18,000 commercial SKUs and 2,500 manufacturing components. Transform analytical models into ERP replenishment parameters to maximize service levels.

  • Bridge Commercial insights and supply chain execution through demand reviews for select strategic product lines. Partner with Product Management to capture market intelligence, sales surges, promotions and contract wins, rapidly translating commercial forecasts into off-cycle ROP updates to ensure supply continuity.

  • Proactively analyze supply requirements for strategic, growth-focused product categories and audit production capacity across key supplier partners. Model supplier constraints, minimum order quantities (MOQs), and lead-time volatility to eliminate upstream supply bottlenecks before they disrupt fulfillment.

  • Orchestrate critical product transitions by designing and executing run-out and phase-in inventory schedules for New Product Introductions (NPI), product conversions, and SKU phase-outs. Secure day-one commercial product availability while aggressively mitigating Excess & Obsolescence (E&O) write-off risk.

  • Empower our Purchasing function by serving as the chief analytical partner to the Buying team. Conduct root-cause investigations on recurring replenishment exceptions, recalibrate broken system parameters, and provide clean replenishment triggers so Buyers can execute orders with maximum speed and certainty.

  • Monitor Days Inventory on Hand (DIOH) and order fill rates to deliver actionable, data-backed trade-offs to Supply Chain leadership that efficiently utilize working capital while defending strict delivery SLAs for our Tier 1 distributor and health system partners.

  • Mature our planning architecture by maintaining planning Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and analytical workflows, supporting the broader organizational roadmap toward automated ERP replenishment.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • 3 to 5 years of experience in inventory planning, supply planning, or materials planning, ideally within a high-SKU distribution or hybrid manufacturing and distribution environment.

  • Hands-on experience managing planning parameters, item records, and replenishment triggers within NetSuite or a similar tier-one ERP system.

  • Advanced proficiency in Google Sheets and/or Microsoft Excel (data modeling, complex formulas, index/match, pivot tables) to manipulate large datasets and execute offline planning models.

  • Demonstrated mastery of statistical safety stock calculations, Reorder Point (ROP) mechanics, ABC stratification, and supplier capacity planning.

  • Experience in medical products distribution, healthcare supply chains, or light manufacturing (machining, assembly, kitting) is preferred.

  • APICS / ASCM certification (CPIM, CSCP) is a plus.






COMPETENCIES

  • Analytical Acumen & Modeling: Possesses a natural drive to interrogate large datasets, identify underlying demand patterns, and translate operational variables into mathematically sound inventory parameters.

  • Proactive Capacity Problem Solving: Anticipates supplier capacity bottlenecks, component shortages, and product lifecycle transition risks well before stockout thresholds are reached.

  • Cross-Functional Facilitation: Translates technical inventory mechanics into clear, practical business decisions when guiding Product Management and Sales on demand and inventory trade-offs.

  • Process Discipline & Data Integrity: Takes meticulous ownership of planning models and ERP parameter accuracy, understanding how small data errors cascade into major operational and financial disruptions.

  • Working Capital Stewardship: Operates with a balanced mindset that aggressively protects customer service levels and Tier 1 distributor fill rates while vigilantly mitigating inventory holding costs and E&O risk.

Benefits:

  • Paid parental leave
  • Scholarship reimbursement
  • 401k match
  • Benefits effective day one of employment
  • Paid short term disability leave
  • Generous PTO policy that starts on day one
  • Paid holidays
  • Health and wellness program
  • Employee discount program within our family of companies

title: Radiology Asst - MRI Dept
description:

title: Integration Team Lead
description:
Redefine the future of live entertainment tech

Welcome to vivenu, the global leader in event ticketing tech and one of the world’s fastest-growing live entertainment tech firms. We are transforming event ticketing for global leaders like the Grammys, the Golden Globes, Stanford University and the Hockenheimring turning what was once a simple transaction into a strategic business advantage. With six offices worldwide and growing, we deliver a customizable, intuitive solution and industry-leading support that simplify even the most complex ticketing challenges – helping organizers deliver exceptional experiences and drive real growth.

Join us and build the future of live entertainment.

With over 10 million end users and usage quadrupling annually, our infrastructure now handles over 1 billion requests per month — and counting. Our API-first platform solves complex system challenges at scale — delivering performance, flexibility, and reliability for the world’s leading live entertainment brands.

You will be leading a newly formed integration team that centralizes to build, maintain and scale critical platform integrations across distributors, insurance partners, and app marketplaces.

As an Integration Team Lead your responsibilities will include:

  • Establish, lead, mentor, and scale a newly formed engineering team focused on centralizing 3rd-party integrations and APIs.

  • Conduct regular code reviews and architectural discussions, ensuring adherence to security and coding best practices.

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable, robust RESTful endpoints, webhooks, and middleware applications.

  • Standardize integration frameworks and developer tools (SDKs, webhooks, API wrappers) to accelerate partner onboarding and third-party app builds.

  • Oversee data synchronization, schema design, and asynchronous message processing for high-volume enterprise event traffic across distribution and marketplace channels.

  • Ensure maximum uptime, error handling, rate-limiting resiliency, and end-to-end monitoring across all third-party connectors.

  • Engage with strategic technology partners (e.g., GetYourGuide, HubSpot, Salesforce, insurance carriers, payment providers) to co-design seamless integration workflows.

  • Establish clear integration standards and documentation for external developer partners building on the vivenu API ecosystem.

  • Monitor API throughput and performance during high-concurrency event launches, proactively optimizing bottlenecks.

What you will need to succeed in this role:

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a focus on web APIs, backend services, and distributed systems.

  • 2+ years in a technical leadership or team lead capacity (managing sprint planning, line management, and delivery).

  • Deep technical expertise with Go/TypeScript, Node.js or similar modern backend languages.

  • Proven track record building and consuming RESTful APIs, GraphQL, and event-driven architectures (Webhooks, Kafka, RabbitMQ, WebSockets).

  • Experience integrating major distribution channels, insurance tools, or enterprise CRMs (e.g., GetYourGuide, HubSpot, Salesforce, SAP, Stripe, Adyen).

  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (GCP/AWS) and containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).

  • Deep understanding of API authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, JWT, API Keys) and rate-limiting techniques.

  • Experience in high-throughput, latency-sensitive environments (e.g., e-commerce, ticketing, fintech, or real-time transactional platforms).

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English (ability to articulate technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders).

  • Self-starter with a founder mindset: thriving in fast-paced, high-growth environments.

  • Experience in high-growth SaaS or B2B platforms, large-scale e-commerce, AdTech/MarTech.

  • Hands-on experience building or managing a third-party developer portal/app marketplace is a plus.

Why join vivenu?

Live Entertainment Tech
Play a mission-critical role for global brands, redefining fan experiences from festivals to major sports events. Here, you’re part of the business of fun — powered by cutting-edge technology that brings moments to life for millions.

Sustainable Growth
We scale sustainably on a profitable, VC-backed foundation with true product-market fit. This means continuous investment in our people, products, and long-term vision.

Top-tier Team
Collaborate with over 160 dedicated professionals, including leaders from Google, Slack, and Salesforce. Together, we’re shaping the future of live entertainment technology, one decision at a time.

Global DNA
We’re a diverse, merit-driven team spread across six global offices. Talent and impact are what matter here — not hierarchy or background.

Fast Growing, in All Aspects
Sifted consistently ranks us among the fastest-growing scale-ups in Europe. We’re driven by daily learning, shared wins, and collective growth.

Next-Gen Leaders & Insights
Work alongside some of tech’s brightest minds — from Forbes 30 Under 30 founders to Executive of the Year award winners. At vivenu, you’ll help set the standard for the ticketing industry’s future.

vivenu Inclusion Statement
At vivenu, we believe our people define our success – and that we win with bold, diverse minds. The strongest teams are built on different perspectives, experiences, and voices. We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels empowered to contribute, grow, and thrive to shape the future of live entertainment globally.

title: Director of Counseling
description:
Director of Counseling

Position Summary:

The Director of Counseling provides strategic leadership and oversight of the district's comprehensive school counseling program, ensuring equitable access to academic, social-emotional, and mental health support for all students. The Director works with Counseling and Mental Health teams to oversee prevention, early identification, intervention, crisis response, and postvention efforts while strengthening partnerships among schools, families, and community mental health providers. This position leads the implementation of a coordinated, multi-tiered system of supports aligned with district priorities and the goals of the SAMHSA Project AWARE grant, ensuring effective grant implementation, data-driven decision-making, measurable student outcomes, and long-term sustainability of practices beyond the grant period.

Essential Duties:

  1. Great Teaching & Learning (Instructional Infrastructure):
    • Lead and monitor districtwide counseling services aligned with district priorities and Project AWARE objectives.
    • Analyze district-wide outcome data to identify and address achievement, attendance, and opportunity gaps, ensuring equitable access to college and career readiness programming.
    • Develop systems to track and monitor post-secondary success metrics, including FAFSA completion, concurrent enrollment, and graduation pathways.
    • Oversee evidence-informed prevention, early identification, and intervention strategies across Tiers I, II, and III.
    • Develop and lead professional development to support counseling strategies and initiatives.
    • Support school counselors in utilizing data to drive student support strategies.
  2. Great People (Talent Management):
    • Provide professional learning, coaching, and accountability for school counselors.
    • Coordinate counselor-teacher, counselor-parent, and other scheduled team meetings and conferences.
    • Mentor and support school counselors through monthly meetings designed to ensure the successful implementation of a school counseling program that aligns with American School Counselor Association (ASCA) standards. Facilitate monthly collaboration meetings with site counselors to promote consistency and continuous improvement.
    • Monitor state and national issues and trends related to mental health, academic, career, and social domains, and provide professional development to educate staff.
    • Provide individual training and onboarding support for newly assigned or hired counselors to ensure consistent processes across the district.
    • Coordinate with the Director of Mental Health to foster professional growth through training in trauma-informed practices, suicide prevention, and support for at-risk students.
    • Assist in providing updates to school sites regarding legislation related to graduation requirements or changes to Oklahoma Higher Learning Access Program (OK Promise).
  3. Great Culture (Systems Leaders):
    • Establish and chair a Counselor Advisory Committee to facilitate feedback loops, monitor implementation fidelity, and inform departmental policy.
    • Serve as a liaison between district leadership, community mental health partners, and post-secondary institutions to streamline support services for students.
    • Strengthen collaboration with families, community organizations, and mental health providers.
    • Ensure consistent implementation of crisis intervention, suicide prevention, and postvention protocols.
    • Promote inclusive and transparent systems to support the holistic development of all students.
    • Represent OKCPS in local, state, and national forums to remain current in the fields of mental health, counseling, and career readiness.
    • Maintain high levels of communication with site leaders to ensure alignment with district goals and emerging needs.
  4. Great Systems (Support & Accountability):
    • Respond to inquiries and provide assistance to staff, students, and the public; schedule counseling appointments; answer telephone calls; and provide information to callers, visitors, staff, and students.
    • Prepare all routine correspondence as requested by the guidance department and/or administration.
    • Receive and process student grades and grade changes; prepare and print report cards and progress reports; notify teachers, counselors and parents of academic issues.
    • Maintain and update all student records; updating with grades and other student information; transfer cumulative records to other schools for existing students; establish and maintain related filing systems.
    • Process student grade report data and maintain copies of accurate student/staff schedules.
    • Maintain and update all office files and a master calendar for guidance counselors and other coordinators.
    • Assist building administrators and guidance staff in processing forms, surveys, and other data as appropriate.
    • Monitor implementation, service access, grant deliverables, and student outcomes to guide continuous improvement.
    • Ensure compliance with grant requirements and develop plans to sustain effective practices beyond the grant period.
    • Facilitate training and successful utilization of the district's Student Information System (SIS) for scheduling and course enrollments.
    • Develop and maintain a guidance/counseling website/portal that contains update information related to the program serving both students and guidance counselors
    • Lead the development of guidance plans, policy recommendations, and digital resources, including a counseling and career readiness portal.
    • Perform other duties as assigned.

Job Specifications:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities required.

Preferred Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills and/or Abilities):

*Relevant experience may be substituted for formal education at a 2:1 ratio. Therefore for every 1 year of college lacking, 2 years

of directly relevant experience may be substituted.

Minimum Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills and/or Abilities):

  • Master’s degree in a counseling-related field.
  • Current Oklahoma School Counselor certification through the OSDE.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Previous experience and/or ability working with children or adolescents.
  • Proficiency with computer hardware. Google software applications, and Windows software applications.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and excellent organizational skills.

Physical/Mental Requirements:

  • Adequate manual dexterity to write legibly and perform required duties on a computer.
  • Adequate visual acuity to read, interpret, and transcribe written material and perform other required duties.
  • Normal range of hearing and clear speaking abilities to interact appropriately with others in person and via phone.
  • Ability to stoop, bend, stretch, and occasionally lift up to 25 pounds.
  • Sitting for prolonged periods of time.
  • May periodically require work outside of normal business hours, including weekends, under demanding conditions to meet business needs and deadlines.

Work Environment:

  • Frequent use of personal vehicle for travel within and outside the district to attend meetings with community partners, advisory boards, trainings, outreach and engagement events, and other community meetings essential to grant success.
  • Office duties will be performed in a well-lighted, climate-controlled environment.
  • Requires time in the office as well as external meeting locations with community partners or school sites throughout the OKC metro area.
  • Must be available in the office during standard work hours and on call for in-person school site needs.
  • May require participation in meetings and activities outside of normal business hours, including weekends and holidays.
  • Ability to bend, stoop, lift up to 25 lbs, and stand or sit for extended periods.

title: Oracle Cloud ERP Lead (1656)
description:
Oracle Cloud ERP Lead

Functional Leadership | Full Lifecycle Oracle Cloud Implementation

Role Focus: Lead the end-to-end Oracle Cloud ERP functional workstream across Financials, Procurement, Project Portfolio Management, and Enterprise Performance Management, aligning the solution across HCM, Payroll, integrations, reporting, data conversion, testing, and deployment.

Overview

The Oracle Cloud ERP Lead provides functional leadership for a full-lifecycle Oracle Cloud implementation. The role owns the overall ERP solution across core Financials, Procurement, Project Portfolio Management, and Enterprise Performance Management, while coordinating cross-functional dependencies with HCM, Payroll, data conversion, integrations, reporting, security, testing, and change management.

This is a senior, client-facing delivery role responsible for translating business objectives into an integrated Oracle Cloud ERP solution. The lead guides discovery, future-state process design, requirements, configuration, validation, deployment, and post-production stabilization, while directing onshore and offshore functional resources and serving as the primary ERP escalation point.

Key Responsibilities

ERP Functional Leadership

  • Lead the ERP functional workstream from discovery through deployment and stabilization.
  • Own the integrated solution design across General Ledger, Payables, Receivables, Cash Management, Fixed Assets, Expenses, Procurement, Self Service Procurement, Sourcing, Supplier Management, Project Financial Management, Grants where applicable, and Planning and Budgeting.
  • Ensure functional decisions support enterprise-wide business processes, reporting, controls, security, integrations, and data requirements.
  • Provide direction to module leads and coordinate work across onshore and offshore functional teams.
  • Serve as the first point of escalation for ERP functional issues, design decisions, and client concerns.

Discovery, Design & Requirements

  • Lead client discovery workshops and document current-state processes, requirements, pain points, and desired outcomes.
  • Design future-state business processes using Oracle Cloud capabilities and industry leading practices.
  • Lead fit-to-standard and fit-gap analysis, identify solution options, and document design decisions and approved exceptions.
  • Maintain functional requirements, process flows, configuration workbooks, decision logs, and traceability to testing and deployment.
  • Identify cross-functional dependencies and facilitate decisions across ERP, HCM, Payroll, data, reporting, integrations, and security.

Configuration & Solution Delivery

  • Provide hands-on configuration leadership and quality review across the Oracle Cloud ERP solution.
  • Assign and oversee configuration activities completed by module leads and offshore resources.
  • Partner with technical teams to define, review, and unit test extensions, integrations, conversions, reports, and workflows.
  • Confirm configurations are consistent across business units, ledgers, legal entities, charts of accounts, approval structures, and related enterprise structures.
  • Promote reusable standards, templates, and delivery practices that improve quality and speed.

Testing, Validation & Deployment

  • Lead Conference Room Pilots, solution validation sessions, System Integration Testing, User Acceptance Testing, regression testing, and production-readiness reviews.
  • Ensure test scenarios cover end-to-end business processes, cross-module dependencies, integrations, reporting, security, and converted data.
  • Drive resolution of defects and design issues identified during CRPs and testing cycles.
  • Lead functional readiness, cutover planning, deployment support, and business validation activities.
  • Provide post-production stabilization and issue-resolution support for approximately 30 days after deployment.

Client, Project & Team Management

  • Communicate ERP status, risks, issues, decisions, dependencies, and milestones to the Project Manager and project governance teams.
  • Lead client knowledge-transfer, solution walkthrough, and validation sessions.
  • Partner with business process owners to obtain timely decisions, approvals, and functional sign-offs.
  • Mentor functional consultants, review deliverables, and ensure adherence to project methods and quality standards.
  • Work effectively with globally distributed clients, onshore, and offshore resources.

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of Oracle ERP experience, including extensive experience with Oracle Cloud ERP applications.
  • Participation in at least three full-lifecycle Oracle Cloud ERP implementations with hands-on functional configuration responsibility.
  • Lead responsibility on at least one full-lifecycle Oracle Cloud ERP implementation.
  • Demonstrated functional depth across multiple ERP areas, including Financials and at least one of Procurement, Project Portfolio Management, or Enterprise Performance Management.
  • Experience gathering and documenting business requirements, facilitating fit-to-standard or fit-gap analysis, leading CRPs, configuring the solution, supporting testing, and delivering client training and knowledge transfer.
  • Understanding of ERP integrations, data conversions, reporting, security, workflows, and enterprise structures sufficient to lead an integrated solution.
  • Strong business communication, facilitation, presentation, issue-resolution, and customer-management skills.
  • Ability to lead and collaborate with onshore and offshore functional and technical teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Oracle Cloud Financials, Procurement, Project Portfolio Management, and Planning or Budgeting.
  • Experience leading ERP delivery for public-sector or education is preferred.
  • Knowledge of Oracle implementation methods, quarterly update impacts, role-based security, and Oracle Cloud reporting tools.
  • Oracle Cloud certification in one or more applicable ERP functional areas.

Expected Outcomes

  • An integrated Oracle Cloud ERP solution that meets approved business, control, reporting, and operational requirements.
  • Consistent solution design and delivery across ERP modules and related workstreams.
  • Completed configuration, validation, testing, knowledge transfer, deployment, and stabilization activities on schedule.
  • Timely resolution of functional risks, defects, and cross-workstream dependencies.
  • Client process owners prepared to operate and support the implemented solution.

title: Shelter Services Specialist (Full-time)
description:
Foothills Animal Shelter seeks a shelter services specialist to provide quality, compassionate customer service to patrons visiting Foothills Animal Shelter. This full-time position will be scheduled approximately 30 hours per week with the opportunity to pick up additional hours when available.

Who We Are

As an open admissions shelter, we are committed to being here for families and their pets in Jefferson County, Colorado. We identify as a socially conscious shelter, caring for over 9,000 dogs, cats, and small animals every year with a compassionate team of staff and volunteers who are committed to the physical and emotional wellbeing of every pet and person we serve.

What You Bring

  • You are a people person. You enjoy working with individuals of all ages, backgrounds, personalities, and abilities – and you enjoy working with them on their best days as well as their worst. You are friendly, outgoing, and have a way of putting people at ease.

title: Groundwater Modeler - Part Time
description:
Matrix New World Engineering, a part of True Environmental and its partner firms, have united their strengths to establish the nation's premier environmental and engineering services consulting firm. This powerhouse organization offers an extensive range of services aimed at revolutionizing the built environment and preserving the natural one. Its diverse expertise encompasses environmental remediation, urban planning, engineering iconic coastal and marine structures, developing sustainable energy sources, and pioneering resource extraction methods. Explore further at and to discover the full scope of our capabilities.

Matrix New World Engineering, a part of True Environmental and its partner firms, is seeking a Groundwater Modeler to join our team in Phoenix, AZ. The position will be a part-time position for up to 25 hours per week, with flexibility to work in our Phoenix office or remotely. Matrix is an equal opportunity employer.

Our Arizona Water Services group focuses on hydrogeological and environmental consulting with offices in Phoenix and Prescott, and remote staff located in North and South America. The ideal candidate will participate in groundwater flow and contaminant transport modeling and support hydrogeologic investigations for water resources and environmental consulting projects.

As a Groundwater Modeler, you will support the team by assisting with numerical groundwater model development, data analysis, and technical reporting, gaining hands-on experience in groundwater flow modeling.

What You'll Do

  • Assist in building, calibrating, and running numerical groundwater flow and transport models using the Modular Finite-Difference Flow Model (MODFLOW), Model Transport in 3 Dimensional (MT3D) and Finite Element Subsurface Flow System (FEFLOW) suites of software or similar platforms
  • Support collection, organization, and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) of large hydrogeologic datasets such as water levels, aquifer parameters, pumping rates, etc.
  • Help prepare model input datasets, grid construction, and boundary condition assignments under senior staff guidance
  • Assist with pre-processing of model inputs and post-processing/visualization of model outputs using tools such as Groundwater Vistas processing applications and Groundwater Modeling Systems (GMS) or ModelMuse graphical user interfaces and Geographic Information Systems (ArcGIS Pro)
  • Assist with sensitivity analyses and predictive scenario runs
  • Support preparation of technical memoranda, model reports, and figures documenting modeling methods and results
  • Participate in literature review and data acquisition of site geology, hydrogeology, and regulatory framework considerations
  • Collaborate with project teams on groundwater resources projects
  • Ensure all work is performed in accordance with project quality assurance and safety protocols

Minimum Requirements

  • Education: Working on Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Hydrogeology, Geology, Civil/Environmental Engineering, or a closely related field
  • Academic Experience: Coursework in groundwater hydrology, hydrogeology, fluid mechanics, or numerical methods
  • Hydrogeologic Experience: Familiarity with groundwater modeling concepts such as Darcy’s Law and the Theis non-equilibrium equation
  • Modeling Experience: Basic exposure to modeling software such as Modular Finite-Difference Flow Model (MODFLOW) suites of software, Groundwater Vistas processing applications or other graphical user interfaces through coursework or self-study
  • Support Software: Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; experience with data processing applications such as Python, R, or Matrix Laboratory (MATLAB)

Preferred Requirements

  • Master’s degree in Hydrogeology, Geology, or Environmental/Civil Engineering
  • Previous experience with MODFLOW-family of codes or commercial groundwater modeling graphical user interfaces (GUIs) such as Groundwater Modeling Systems (GMS), Groundwater Vistas and ModelMuse
  • Experience with ArcGIS software for spatial data management and figure preparation
  • Prior internship or research experience at an environmental consulting firm or regulatory agency
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary project team
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills for managing model files and datasets
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

This role requires basic skills in reading and interpreting design drawings and design specifications. This role may include detailed inspections of machinery and processes to identify potential issues with condition or performance and recommend solutions. This role involves collaborating with internal and external clients to understand their specific needs and tailor solutions accordingly. This role involves a basic understanding of a wide variety of unit process operations, control systems, maintenance requirements and procedures and staff required to operate and maintain these systems.

  • Plan and execute start-up and commissioning on construction projects.

  • Develop and facilitate operator training sessions.
  • Conduct QA/QC oversight of staff activities related to data collection and in development of O&M related work products.
  • Develop and present recommendations to improve efficiency and effectiveness.

  • Conduct operability and maintainability reviews of designs and operating facilities.

title: Softlines Processor (63716)
company: GOODWILL INDUSTRIES OF NORTH LOUISIANA INC
description:
SUMMARY:

The Softlines Processor evaluates, sorts, prepares, and processes donated apparel, linens, and other textiles for sale or appropriate disposition. The position works efficiently to meet established production and quality expectations while identifying merchandise with potential for higher value and ensuring sellable items are properly prepared for the sales floor.

This role supports Goodwill NLA's mission of Improving People's Lives Through the Power of Work by responsibly stewarding donated goods and helping maximize the value of each donation to generate revenue that supports workforce programs and community services.

REPORTS TO:

DGR Store Manager / DGR Store Assistant Manager

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Softlines Processing & Stewardship

  1. Inspects donated apparel, linens, and textiles for condition, quality, salability, and appropriate disposition.
  2. Sorts merchandise to the appropriate sales, e-commerce, higher-value, outlet, salvage, recycling, or disposal stream in accordance with established procedures.
  3. Identifies merchandise that may have increased value based on brand, condition, age, origin, collectability, or other established criteria and routes it appropriately.
  4. Hangs apparel using the appropriate hangers, categories, and rack organization standards.
  5. Tags merchandise in the correct location and according to established rotation and color procedures without damaging the item.
  6. Meets established production expectations while maintaining required quality standards.
  7. Accurately records required production information.

Merchandise Flow & Operational Support

  1. Maintains organized Z-racks, containers, workstations, and merchandise flow to support efficient production and movement to the sales floor.
  2. Safely moves merchandise and uses authorized material-handling equipment as required.
  3. Assists in other store operational areas, including hardlines processing, donations, merchandise movement, and sales-floor support, as assigned and trained.

Safety & Stewardship

  1. Maintains a clean, organized, and safe processing area and follows required PPE, lifting, material-handling, and equipment procedures.
  2. Protects donated goods and agency assets and promptly reports suspected theft, misuse, hazardous materials, prohibited items, or safety concerns.
  3. Attends required meetings and trainings.
  4. Performs other duties as assigned in support of store operations and the agency mission.

title: Design Manager
description:
The Boldt Company, a subsidiary of the Boldt Group
Location: Appleton, WI, Remote

At Boldt, we build more than complex projects, and we build strong relationships, great teams, and lasting impact.

As a Design Manager, you'll be at the center of those decisions, leading the planning, design, and preconstruction efforts that set complex projects up for success.

title: Landscape Supervisor
location: The Lodge at Ventana Canyon - Tucson, AZ 85750
description:
SUMMARY

The Landscape Supervisor is responsible for the care and maintenance of the turf area, ornamental trees, shrubs, and flowers around the facility buildings, resort grounds, and other related areas (par course & practice facility maintenance). Supervise and training of staff, scheduling, irrigation management and installation. Application of fertilizers and pesticides. Accurate record keeping.

  • Attend staff meetings.

title: Analyst, Business Systems - HR
description:
WHO WE ARE:


Exemplar Luxury Group, formerly Saks Global, is the luxury collective uniting coveted brands with unrivaled customer experiences across Neiman Marcus, Saks Fifth Avenue and Bergdorf Goodman. Driven by a relentless devotion to our customers and powered by our talented colleagues, we offer expertly curated product assortments, unparalleled service and personalized experiences across our integrated retail model. Through strong partnerships with the world's most desired luxury brands and deep customer relationships enhanced by data-rich insights, Exemplar Luxury Group is committed to setting the standard of excellence for luxury retail.

Job Description:


YOU WILL BE:

Reporting directly to the People Squad Lead, the Workday Functional Analyst (HCM) translates complex HR business needs into scalable technical solutions across our Workday ecosystem following our recent go-live. In this role, you will partner directly with HR business partners, squad peers, and senior analysts to assess operational gaps, design functional enhancements, and execute configuration changes across multiple HCM functional areas—including Recruiting, Compensation, Talent, and Core HCM—while supporting biannual release testing to ensure system stability.


WHAT YOU WILL DO:

  • Requirements Gathering & Solution Design: Lead functional discovery sessions with HR process owners to capture user stories and requirements, translating business challenges into clean technical specifications and scalable Workday solutions.
  • Cross-Functional HCM Configuration: Design, configure, and maintain business processes, validation rules, condition rules, and custom notifications across multiple modules, including Core HCM, Recruiting, Compensation, and Talent/Performance.
  • End-to-End Functional Optimization: Evaluate existing tenant configuration across HR streams to eliminate operational friction, improve process flow, and ensure consistent configuration practices across modules.
  • Biannual Release Testing & Quality Assurance: Drive functional release readiness by creating comprehensive test scenarios, conducting user acceptance testing (UAT), and executing regression testing during Workday's R1 and R2 feature updates.
  • Agile Delivery & Production Support: Investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve complex functional tickets across various Workday modules, identifying root causes and configuring durable fixes in sprint delivery cycles.

WHAT YOU WILL BRING:

Experience: 3–5 years of hands-on functional Workday configuration experience in a multi-module environment.

Multi-Module Functional Expertise:

  • Demonstrated track record configuring and supporting Core HCM alongside at least two secondary functional modules (e.g., Recruiting, Compensation, or Talent & Performance).
  • Deep expertise in Business Process (BP) framework architecture, condition rules, validation rules, and custom notifications.
  • Strong ability to translate complex HR policies into actionable, hands-on Workday functional setups.
  • Proficiency utilizing calculated fields to drive functional business logic and conditional routing.

Testing & Quality Assurance: Extensive experience defining test strategy, writing scenario-based test scripts, and coordinating end-to-end UAT across cross-functional HR teams.

Agile & Soft Skills: Strong analytical mindset with proven experience operating within an agile team structure and collaborating with diverse HR stakeholders.

Certifications (Optional): Workday HCM Certifications



YOUR LIFE AND CAREER AT EXEMPLAR LUXURY GROUP:


  • Opportunity to work in a dynamic fast paced environment at a company experiencing growth and transformation
  • Exposure to rewarding career advancement opportunities across the largest multi-brand luxury retailer from retail to distribution, to digital or corporate
  • Comprehensive benefits package for all eligible full-time employees (including medical, vision and dental)

Benefits: We offer the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan, basic life insurance, supplemental life insurance, disability insurance, and a variety of additional voluntary benefits (such as critical illness, hospital and accident insurance).

title: Director of Project AWARE
description:
Director of Project AWARE

Position Summary:

The Project AWARE project director is responsible for leading the planning and execution of the SAMHSA-funded Project AWARE federal grant program. The project director will be responsible for developing contracts for services, coordinate grant advisory team, and provide leadership in all facets of the OKC AWARE development and ensure alignment with Oklahoma City Public Schools’ multi-tiered system of supports (MTSS) framework for mental health, EmbraceOKC. Oversee the AWARE grant to ensure goals are met, with all reports filed on time, and all rules are followed.

Essential Duties:

  1. Great Teaching & Learning (Instructional Infrastructure):
    • Oversee access to and/or facilitate mental health awareness and suicide prevention training for all project staff and school personnel.
    • Coordinates and supports evidence-based training programs to expand mental health literacy across participating school sites.
  2. Great People (Talent Management):
    • Collaborate with project staff on day-to-day management of the grant program implementation.
    • Provide leadership, guidance, and support to school-based personnel and community service providers.
  3. Great Culture (Systems Leaders):
    • Coordinate with the grant’s required advisory team and engage formal and informal partners to effectively implement the initiative.
    • Take part in regular meetings, planning groups, and related activities with community partners.
    • Promote positive school climate and safety strategies by supporting trauma-informed practices and alignment with EmbraceOKC.
  4. Great Systems (Support & Accountability):
    • Liaise with the SAMHSA project officer to ensure all grant requirements and deadlines are met.
    • Develop and monitor contracts for services required under the grant program, including community-based organizations providing children’s services.
    • Coordinate with the district evaluator and monitor key performance indicators and progress towards the grant program.
    • Develop a strategic plan for implementation of all required grant activities and provide program leadership.
    • Other tasks, duties, or services consistent with this position assigned.

Job Specifications:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities required.

Minimum Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills and/or Abilities):

  • Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in public administration, social work, psychology, education, school counseling or related field.
  • Minimum of two (2) years' experience in project management, community-and/or education-based settings and mental health programs and services.
  • Must have a working knowledge of grant coordination, community-and/or school-based mental health services and delivery and applying a three-tiered public health framework.
  • Considerable knowledge and experience of children’s mental health and social service systems and best practices in K-12 and/or higher education settings is preferred.
  • Ability to provide strong leadership and knowledge of project management methodology; knowledge and experience in K-12 and/or higher education settings preferred.
  • Proven ability to manage tasks, resources, vendors, analyze complex concepts/ideas and assess risks.
  • Ability to work on fast-paced projects of varying complexity with tight deadlines, continually adapting to changing priorities.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to build and maintain effective partnerships and work collaboratively with various stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills and/or Abilities):

  • Master’s degree in public administration, social work, psychology, education, school counseling or related field.
  • Preferred credential in mental health services, such as an LPC, LMSW, LCSW, or School Counseling.

Physical/Mental Requirements:

  • Able to sit and/or stand for extended periods of time.
  • Exhibit manual dexterity to enter data into a computer.
  • Ability to see and read a computer screen and printed material with or without vision aids.
  • Hear and understand speech at normal classroom levels, outdoors and on the telephone.
  • Speak in audible tones so that others may understand clearly in normal classrooms, outdoors and on the telephone.
  • Physical agility, able to bend, stoop, sit on the floor, climb stairs, walk and reach.
  • Ability to lift, push, pull up to 25 pounds.

Work Environment:

  • Frequent use of personal vehicle for travel within and outside the district to meetings with community partners, advisory board meetings, trainings, outreach and engagement events, and other community-based meetings that are needed to ensure the success of the grant.
  • Office duties will be performed in a well-lighted, climate-controlled environment.
  • Must maintain a consistent daily in-office presence during designated work hours and remain available to respond to school-site needs requiring in-person support.
  • Must be able to work in the office each day during work hours, and be on call for in person school site needs.
  • May require participation in meetings and activities outside of normal business hours, including weekends and holidays.
  • Able to bend and stoop, lift 25lbs, stand and/or sit for extended periods of time.

description:

title: CDC Badged Professionals - Talent Pipeline
description:
The World at Abt

Solving the world's most pressing issues and improving the quality of life for people worldwide is what we do every day at Abt. Advancing data-driven innovations is no small task, but we are driven by big challenges.

We are a team of 2,000+ people in over 40 countries working in unison and focused on the bigger picture. Only by sharing our commitment, energy, and innovation do we affect change and push the boundaries of what is possible. We welcome representative ideas, backgrounds, and viewpoints - joining Abt means access to exceptional thinkers at the top of their game.

To thrive at Abt is to embrace flexibility and collaboration. Our open culture allows you to balance your work and personal life as needed to optimize personal well-being. We create value driven partnerships around the world, but our greatest focus is on empowering our employees to advance our mission.

Ready to embrace rewarding and meaningful work? Now's your chance.

The Opportunity

If you currently hold or previously held a CDC-issued badge, PIV card, or other documented access credential while supporting CDC project work, Abt wants to connect with you. Your firsthand knowledge of CDC environments can help future teams mobilize quickly and advance work that protects health and improves public health systems. We are building a pipeline across career levels for anticipated opportunities in epidemiology, surveillance, laboratory and scientific support, data modernization, digital health, communications, preparedness, program management, and mission operations. By joining this pipeline, you can be considered for future roles aligned with your documented CDC experience, technical expertise, and career interests. Please identify the project or office, contractor/employer, dates of support, and whether the credential is active or expired.

  • Ability to comply with role-specific background investigation, suitability, credentialing, confidentiality, and security requirements.

  • Preferred: federal contracting experience, knowledge of the agency operating environment, or experience transitioning rapidly onto a federal health project.

When You Apply

Please submit a current resume that clearly identifies:

  • The CDC project, program, center, institute, office, or division you supported

  • Your employer and, if applicable, your prime/subcontractor relationship, dates of support, role, and major responsibilities

  • The status and type of your CDC badge or access credential, if known

  • Your preferred functional area, career level, work location, and remote/hybrid availability

What We Offer

We foster an environment where you can Thrive Your Way. Our innovative total rewards programs are designed to help balance your work and personal life. The approach toward your wellbeing centers around comprehensive benefits, flexible schedules, and professional development.

title: 2027 Summer Intern - Translational Pharmacokinetics & Pharmacodynamics (tPKPD): QSP Modeling in Cardiovascular, Renal and Metabolic Diseases
description:
The Position

2027 Summer Intern - Translational Pharmacokinetics & Pharmacodynamics (tPKPD): QSP Modeling in Cardiovascular, Renal and Metabolic Diseases


Department Summary

This intern position is in the Translational Pharmacokinetics & Pharmacodynamics (tPKPD) Department within Development Sciences. The tPKPD department applies preclinical and computational models (in silico, in vitro, or in vivo) to determine the pharmacokinetics (what the body does to the drug) and pharmacodynamics (what the drug does to the body) of therapeutics. This work informs the selection of lead molecules, the optimization of dosing regimens, and the translation of molecules from research into early clinical development, across oncology, immunology, ophthalmology, neuroscience, and cardiovascular, renal and metabolic (CVRM) diseases. Within tPKPD, the Modeling and Simulation group builds mechanistic, quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models that link drug pharmacology to patient outcomes.


This internship position is located in South San Francisco, on-site.


The Opportunity

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to join the Modeling and Simulation group and apply QSP modeling to cardiovascular, renal and metabolic diseases, including obesity, using modern AI-assisted workflows.


The intern will:

  • Develop, extend, or integrate mechanistic QSP models of CVRM physiology and disease in MATLAB/SimBiology.
  • Represent drug pharmacology and its links to physiological and clinical outcomes in these models.
  • Calibrate and validate models against published preclinical and clinical data.
  • Use simulation, sensitivity analysis and virtual populations to address questions from drug development teams.
  • Leverage the latest agentic AI coding tools to accelerate model development, testing and documentation, with rigorous verification of the results.
  • Present results to project teams and the department, at the intern poster session, and in a written report.

Program Highlights

  • Intensive 12-weeks, full-time (40 hours per week) paid internship.
  • Program start dates are in May/June (Summer).
  • A stipend, based on location, will be provided to help alleviate costs associated with the internship.
  • Ownership of challenging and impactful business-critical projects.
  • Work with some of the most talented people in the biotechnology industry.

Who You Are


Required Education:

  • Must be pursuing a PhD (enrolled student).

Required Majors: Bioengineering / Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences / Pharmacometrics, Applied Mathematics, Computational or Systems Biology, AI and machine learning, or related quantitative fields.


Required Skills

  • Experience building and analyzing ordinary differential equation (ODE) models of biological or pharmacological systems.
  • Proficiency in MATLAB (SimBiology preferred), R, or Python.
  • Experience fitting models to data (parameter estimation) and interpreting the results.

Preferred Knowledge, Skills, and Qualifications

  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and interpersonal skills.
  • Complements our culture and the standards that guide our daily behavior & decisions: Integrity, Courage, and Passion.
  • Experience with QSP, PK/PD or physiologically based modeling.
  • Knowledge of cardiovascular, renal or metabolic physiology, including obesity.
  • Experience with sensitivity analysis, virtual populations, or uncertainty quantification.
  • Familiarity with version control (Git) and reproducible code.
  • Interest or experience in using AI coding assistants and agentic AI tools in scientific work.

Relocation benefits are not available for this job posting.


The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of California is $52.00 per hour. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. This position also qualifies for paid holiday time off benefits.

title: Senior Product Manager, Agent Growth
description:
Lone Wolf builds the software real estate runs on. Brokerages, agents, MLSs, and associations across North America use our products for forms and transaction management (zipForm, Transaction Desk, Transact), e-signature (Authentisign), comparative market analysis (Cloud CMA), listing advertising (Boost), and brokerage back office.

A large share of North American real estate agents use Lone Wolf products, and many of them buy on their own with a credit card: an e-signature plan, a forms upgrade, a CMA subscription, an ad for a new listing. You’ll be the owner that runs it as one system, with one dashboard and a steady stream of experiments along the way.

You’ll wear two hats:

  1. Product manager for Brand Management (Boost). Boost automates listing and brand advertising on Facebook, Instagram, and Google for agents and brokerages. You’ll own its roadmap, its metrics, and the priorities of its engineering team.
  2. Growth lead for every agent-purchased product. You’ll own the path from first touch to purchase to expansion across Boost, Cloud CMA, Authentisign, zipForm and Transaction Desk upgrades, and more.

This is your business to run. You’ll report to the Chief Innovation Officer, who sets direction, holds the number with the executive team, clears cross-functional blockers, and makes the calls that need executive weight: major pricing changes, tradeoffs across product pillars, and scale-or-stop decisions. Everything else is yours: the backlog, the experiments, the funnels, the roadmap, and the weekly review. You won’t be executing someone else’s plan. You’ll write it.

This is a builder’s role with a wide surface. Most of the funnel runs through teams you won’t manage: marketing’s website and SEO, CX’s in-app messaging and onboarding, other product teams’ engineering time, and sales conversations with brokerages. Your leverage is data, speed, and the ability to bring people with you.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the agent revenue number. Build the dashboard yourself (SQL, Metabase), run the weekly review, and make it what everyone else looks at. Bring a monthly readout to the executive team alongside the CIO.
  • Find and fix funnel leaks in landing pages, pricing pages, checkout, trials, and in-product upgrade prompts.
  • Run lifecycle email as a growth channel. Iterable triggers at listing events, onboarding, upgrade, and win-back. Write the copy, set up the tests, and read the results.
  • Ship your own variants. Build landing pages and messaging variants yourself with AI tools. Work hand in hand with Marketing’s website lead on lwolf.com agent pages and SEO, where Boost now sits alongside our other agent products.
  • Run experiments end to end: hypothesis, instrumentation, launch, readout, and decision, at a high tempo.
  • Own agent pricing and packaging: bundles, trials, annual plans, auto-renewal, and cross-product offers. Bring recommendations to the CIO for the big moves.
  • Shape how agents buy Transact. As agents move from zipForm and Transaction Desk to Transact, make sure the products they pay for today, like Authentisign and forms upgrades, still have a clear path to purchase.
  • Run the Boost roadmap. Balance growth work against reliability and commitments to brokerage and partner customers. Sales owns brokerage Boost deals; you make sure the product and the team behind it support them.
  • Test paid acquisition on a small budget, and scale only what pays back.
  • Get things done across the business. Win engineering time from other product teams, in-app placements from CX, page changes from Marketing, and agent offers in Sales conversations, without owning any of them.
  • Stand up lean product analytics that don’t require hand-instrumenting every event.

Requirements:

  • A track record of growing a purchase funnel with a product-led mindset. Bring the before-and-after numbers and explain what you personally did to move them.
  • Range across disciplines. You might come up through product management, growth marketing, or e-commerce. Either way, you’ve done the work of all three: shaping product, writing and testing messaging, and optimizing checkout and pricing.
  • You build things yourself. Landing pages, email variants, dashboards, prototypes. You use AI tools to build what used to take a team, and you can show us.
  • Data self-sufficiency. You write your own SQL, build your own dashboards, and design and read your own experiments without waiting on an analyst.
  • Ownership. You’ve run a number, not just a backlog. You set your own priorities, make the calls in front of you, and bring your manager decisions rather than questions.
  • Influence without authority. Concrete examples of getting important work done through teams you didn’t manage.
  • Experience: typically 7+ years across product, growth, or e-commerce roles, with direct ownership of revenue or conversion metrics.

Nice to have:

  • Real estate or proptech experience, or SaaS sold to independent professionals and small businesses.
  • Lifecycle platforms and paid social or search (Meta, Google Ads).
  • Pricing and packaging work on self-serve subscriptions, including e-commerce or billing migrations when products are replaced.
  • Setting up product analytics from scratch on a budget.
  • Working across multiple product lines, legacy systems, or a post-acquisition portfolio.

Compensation:

  • Base salary
  • A meaningful performance incentive tied to agent revenue growth

title: Regional Manager - Vancouver - Portland
description:
About Us:

Cambridge Management, Inc. (CMI) began in 1987 as a small team managing a portfolio of communities in Tacoma, Washington. Our focus soon shifted to providing quality management for affordable housing communities. These affordable communities provide homes for those with limited incomes including families, senior citizens, and people with disabilities. Today, our team has grown to nearly 500 employees managing 164 communities and more than 14,600 apartment homes. Our portfolio includes market rate, Low Income Housing Tax Credit, and Project-Based Section-8 communities that range in size from 6 to 344 units. We currently manage communities in California, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, North Carolina, Tennessee, Washington State, and Virginia.

Why work for us:

Cambridge Management, Inc. offers the following Compensation and Benefits package for full time employees:

Position Salary Range: $75,000 - $85,000 Salary

Paid time off:

  • An accrual of 80 hours of Vacation.
  • Up to 6 paid sick days per year. (varies based on state sick leave laws)
  • 8 paid holidays
  • 2 paid floating holidays.

Benefits offered:

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Long Term Disability, AD&D & EAP
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Voluntary benefits available

Job Summary:

The Regional Manager will report directly to the Director of Property Management. The Regional Manager is responsible for overall management and operations of each community in the assigned portfolio. This position supports and executes Company and Owner expectations set forth for an assigned portfolio of communities for profitability and superior performance by directing and leading team members in achieving and exceeding operational goals and expectations by enforcing policy, procedures, and practices. The Regional Manager will have contact with the public conducting relationships in a manner that will enhance the overall marketing effort of Cambridge Management. The Regional Manager will be called upon and be expected to participate with local community and industry related organizations to attend functions, seminars, meetings, and classes to further the reputation of Cambridge Management and to maintain knowledge of the industry. Incumbent is expected to have excellent attendance and communication skills, possess the ability to build lasting business relationships, and exhibit professionalism.

Essential Functions

The primary functions for this position are:

  • Effectively monitor and manage all communities to achieve financial and operational targets.
  • Monitor employee performance: consult Human Resources and act as necessary to improve portfolio or asset performance.
  • Ensure all CMI community procedures are being accomplished; monitor community performance at both the micro level (following procedures, practices) and macro level (occupancy, income, collections).
  • Work with Community Managers to prepare annual budgets and community plans.
  • Perform regular community inspections (physical, operational, file review).
  • Recruit, interview and hire community managers and lead maintenance technicians; approve all community new hires; ensure new hire paperwork is processed and delivered to Human Resources.
  • Coordinate, manage and monitor community audits by Syndicators, state agencies, etc.
  • Act as portfolio representative to coordinate activities and resolve issues with the Director and Owner Representatives.

Roles & Responsibilities

This position has responsibility for:

  • Provide feedback on capital needs and other asset plan items; complete asset plan items as required.
  • Complete annual performance reviews and regularly communicate employee performance expectations and achievement.
  • Seek to develop teams and provide motivation and direction as required.
  • Ensure integrity of application and file approval process at communities.
  • Monitor community financials; review variance reports; review financials with Community Managers regularly.
  • Approve community vendors.
  • Approve community purchase orders and expenditures.
  • Manage portfolio rents; propose adjustments as necessary.
  • Manage portfolio resident selection criteria; monitor and make adjustments as necessary.
  • Monitor portfolio collections and collection procedures; ensure all collections activities are accomplished.
  • Manage portfolio vendors such as collections agencies, legal representation, etc.; monitor performance and notify Managing Director of any issues.
  • Support Community Managers as necessary on resident issues, supportive services issues, vendor issues, compliance approvals and other operational duties.
  • Regularly meet with community staff.
  • Coordinate portfolio training, Marketing, Compliance, Accounting, IT and HR activities.
  • Prepare and deliver Regional Portfolio reports as required.
  • Initiate new programs, procedures or practices in portfolio as directed.
  • Represent portfolio to local PHA’s, state agencies, etc. as required.
  • Coordinate pre-lease set up of new communities; hire and train staff.
  • Participate in senior level management meetings as required; participate in regional team meetings as required.

Key Deliverables/Objectives

  • Achieve best possible financial success from the portfolio within the guidelines set by the Director and Owner Representatives.
  • Seek to maximize income and minimize expenses; ensure Community Managers are actively operating communities at or above budgeted income and at or below budgeted expenses.
  • Maintain appropriate staffing levels while achieving the financial goals for each community
  • Deliver accurate and timely regional reports.
  • Ensure every new employee completes the training within 30 days of employment.
  • Ensure all re-certifications are current.
  • Achieve at least 95% occupancy and 95% portfolio rent collections with minimal approved write-offs.
  • Maximize credit delivery on new project lease ups; complete all lease-ups in 12 months or less
  • Qualify all units prior to the qualification deadline.
  • Perform a thorough community inspection on each community at least twice per calendar year.
  • Perform other duties as required.

Knowledge, Skill, and Competency Requirements

  • Competency is based in part on education, training, skills, and experience. In order to perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following knowledge, skills and competencies:
  • Strong understanding of financial statements (budget, financial reports, P&L statement, general ledger, etc.).
  • Strong understanding of federal, state, and local fair housing laws and provisions.
  • Superior customer service skills including the ability to manage difficult customers and/or situations.
  • Professional verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong leadership and management skills; ability to direct a team.
  • Strong adherence to ethical standards including, but not limited to, the ability to maintain confidentiality and fiduciary responsibility.
  • Ability to exercise independent judgment.
  • Detail oriented; ability to manage conflicting priorities and to adjust priorities daily.
  • Ability to travel and work a flexible schedule to include weekends, evenings, and holidays.
  • Ability to draw data driven insights from systems-driven reporting and communicate in business and financial terms to various stakeholders.
  • Computer Skills:
  • Working knowledge of Office 365, Microsoft Office with advanced knowledge of Excel.
  • Must have excellent computer skills and have industry software experience. RealPage’s OneSite competency will be required following specific CMI training
  • Must be willing and able to utilize tablet/mobile devices and software efficiently.

Physical Requirements:

  • Requires sitting, standing, and walking for prolonged periods.
  • Position requires frequent/daily reaching, pushing, pulling, and lifting up to 20 pounds.
  • Position includes communication mastery in the form of electronic mail, writing letters, memos, documents, and any other correspondence in written form including reports. This position must also be proficient in face-to-face, telephone, and other median of conversation styles for prolonged periods, up to 6 hours per workday. This position also requires contact with external customers and others (face-to-face, telephone, or otherwise).
  • Requires competition or awareness of competitive pressures and the ability to meet strict deadlines.
  • Position can include conflict situations. Requires the ability to deal with unpleasant, angry, or discourteous people in a professional manner.
  • Requires making decisions that impact the results of co-workers, clients, or the company.
  • Requires being exact or highly accurate. May include freedom to determine tasks, priorities, make decisions in a timely manner and make goals. Requires repeating the same physical or mental activities over and over.
  • Pace and Scheduling Requires meeting strict deadlines.
  • Personal Interaction Requires working with others in a group or team. Requires coordinating or leading others in accomplishing work activities.
  • Requires working in a vehicle or golf cart. Requires working outdoors, exposed to all weather conditions. Requires working indoors in environmentally controlled conditions. Job tasks are performed in close physical proximity to other people.

Experience/Education:

  • Minimum High School Graduate, Bachelor’s degree preferred
  • 5+ years of experience in property management with recent experience as a Regional Property Manager
  • Experience in managing LIHTC and HUD multifamily properties.
  • Related Management Certification (ARM, CAM, CAPS, CPM, etc.).
  • Related Affordable Certification (HCCP, COS, SHCM, CPO, etc.).
  • Working knowledge of applicable Landlord Tenant Laws, Fair Housing Regulations, LIHTC/HUD Programs, and other laws as they relate to property specific guidelines and occupancy standards.
  • Experience managing up to 1,500 units within a multi-site region.

Travel requirements:

  • Up to 80% travel within assigned region.
  • Up to 10% travel outside of assigned region.

Driving:

  • Must be able to travel to and from a bank, other communities, and other off-site locations as a requirement of this position, without advance notice. A valid drivers license is required.

Must be able to complete all required training within thirty (30) days of hire date.

This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the team member incumbent in this position. Further, this document does not create an employment contract implied or otherwise, other than an “at will” relationship.

Additional Notes:

  • Offers contingent upon successful completion of background check, drug screen, and MVR check (if required by position)

title: Leasing Specialist
description:
About Waterton

At Waterton, we believe in finding the good and leaving it better. For over 30 years, we’ve been passionate about delivering incredible resident experiences, made possible by offering an extraordinary experience for our talented associates. We value adaptability, curiosity, accountability, and commitment to excellence. If this sounds like you, we’d love to meet you.

Job Summary

As a Leasing Specialist, you will drive occupancy by delivering exceptional resident and prospect experiences. The ideal candidate is customer-focused, sales-driven, adaptable, proactive, and thrives in a collaborative team environment.

What You Need to Succeed

Performance and Business Drive (Get It Done)

Success in this role requires effectively managing high-volume prospect outreach, tour scheduling, and resident priorities. By maintaining a sales-focused mindset and a strong sense of urgency, you convert leads into residents and maximize occupancy.
