From our crown jewel, The Empire State Building, to incredible buildings modernized for the 21st century, to outstanding customer service, and our decade-long leadership position in sustainability and energy efficient portfolio that is 100% fully powered by renewable wind electricity, we take pride in our work. ESRT seeks an equally passionate colleague to join the team, understand the vision and help achieve that vision.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Applied AI Engineer I supports, maintains, and enhances ESRT’s portfolio of AI-enabled enterprise applications. This early-career role offers recent graduates hands-on experience with large language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, and intelligent automation, and helps them develop software engineering skills for production applications.

The role works closely with senior engineers and technical leadership to learn the application portfolio and codebase and complete well-defined tasks, such as bug fixes, small enhancements, tests, and documentation. Regular mentorship and code review support skill development and greater responsibility over time.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support software design, development, tests, and deployment under senior guidance, and help build applications that incorporate large language models and other AI capabilities
  • Support retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows, such as document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, indexing, and retrieval
  • Help develop AI agents, agent tools, and tool-calling workflows, and convert approved prototypes into production-ready features under senior guidance
  • Implement small, well-defined features and components under close guidance, with code review by senior engineers
  • Learn the architecture and codebase of AI applications, such as model integrations, RAG pipelines, agent workflows, evaluation systems, and observability, through structured orientation, documentation, and work with experienced engineers
  • Write unit and integration tests and help develop automated tests and application monitoring
  • Learn and apply safeguards for data privacy, access control, and responsible AI practices
  • Help build APIs, backend services, and data processing workflows that connect AI solutions with internal systems, with support for data ingestion and extract, transform, and load (ETL) processes
  • Write clean, well-documented code, use Git for version control, participate in peer code reviews, and follow the team’s continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) practices
  • Maintain technical documentation, communicate progress and blockers clearly, and collaborate with internal teams, vendors, and business stakeholders in an agile environment

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • Complete orientation within the first 3 months, demonstrate familiarity with the team’s tools and development processes, and help resolve small, well-defined bugs and tasks under close supervision
  • Complete assigned tasks and small features within the first 6 months, incorporate regular feedback from senior engineers, and contribute reliably to team sprints
  • Handle well-scoped tasks with greater independence within the first year, apply foundational AI engineering practices, and take on greater ownership with continued mentorship

REQUIRED TECHNICAL SKILLS / ABILITIES

  • Solid foundation in Python; exposure to at least one additional language (e.g., C#, Java, TypeScript) through coursework or projects
  • Exposure to large language models, APIs, or other AI services through coursework, internships, or personal projects
  • Basic knowledge of software engineering fundamentals: version control (Git), tests, and code review
  • Familiarity with API development or use, databases, and data models
  • Willingness to learn about AI application risks, such as prompt injection and sensitive-data exposure, and responsible AI practices
  • Strong problem resolution skills, ability to learn new tools and technologies quickly, and clear written and verbal communication
  • Ability to collaborate, take direction from senior engineers, and show initiative on assigned tasks

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related field (recent graduates welcome), or equivalent hands-on experience through internships, bootcamps, or personal/academic projects
  • No prior professional experience required; internship, co-op, or project experience is a plus
  • Coursework or project exposure to RAG concepts (embeddings, vector search), Azure OpenAI or comparable AI platforms, cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, or GCP), or traditional machine learning

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

At ESRT, like our tenants, our employees come from everywhere. We foster a collaborative work environment that captures top talent and cultivates the best ideas. As a Great Place to Work® Certified employer, we are committed to maintaining our positive work culture where employees are engaged and can grow and develop.   • Adaptable – you are a self-starter who’s able to quickly digest and execute new processes to work both collaboratively and independently
  • Dynamic – you are solutions-oriented, aim to improve processes and implement efficiency, and offer insightful feedback to improve ESRT
  • Dependable – you take a strong sense of ownership and accountability over your work
  • Passionate – you keep up with industry trends and are excited about the potential to propel the industry forward with a “roll-up-your-sleeves” attitude
  • Curious – you consistently look for new ways to work smarter, not just harder
  • Ethical – you treat others with respect, act with integrity in how you perform your work, and embrace our collaborative culture
  • Positive – you possess a service-oriented attitude with excellent follow through

title: Principal (Interim) - Spanish/English Bilingual Required
description:
REDWOOD CITY SCHOOL DISTRICT

Principal

RCSD takes pride in our dedicated workforce and strong connection with our students, families, and community. Our highly dedicated and skilled team of professionals provides a safe and supportive, inspirational and rigorous, joyful and inclusive environment for all learners. We are looking to build our workforce with a staff who share this vision and want to instill passion in learning emphasizing student strengths and gifts for all learners: all abilities, all ethnicities and cultural identities, LGBTQ+ youth, and multilingual learners.

DEFINITION
Under direction, serve as the chief administrative officer of an elementary school to facilitate the development of a professional learning community; use data to guide decisions and improve student learning; direct the formulation and implementation of operational procedures and practices; plan, develop, and implement instructional objectives; design and implement procedures to evaluate instructional program effectiveness; assist in planning and conducting staff development opportunities; plan, develop, and carry out public and community relations activities; perform other related functions as directed.

EXAMPLES OF DUTIES
Serve as the instructional leader and operational manager of an elementary school.


Support the curriculum development and instructional implementation of a standards-based educational program designed to meet the unique needs of students and community.


Work closely with school staff and School Site Council to identify instructional goals in conjunction with Major District Objectives; develop long- and short-range plans to improve the instructional process.


Maintain and utilize student and staff performance evaluation information to insure site goals and objectives are achieved.


Work to establish a results-based school culture through the continuous collection, examination and use of data; initiate ongoing opportunities for teachers, students, and parents to understand and utilize data as a means to improve instruction and learning.


Plan, develop, organize, and administer support systems and intervention programs which optimize the learning opportunities for all elementary age pupils (regular, EL, and special education students).


Review, evaluate, requisition, purchase, and allocate instructional resources, supplies, and equipment to enhance programs and support schoolwide goals.


Confer and consult with school and District personnel, parents, and pupils pertaining to academic and behavioral issues and establish alternative interventions.


Direct, supervise, observe, assess, and evaluate site personnel performance. Ensure that all levels of staff adhere to District, state, and national educational and professional standards.


Establish and maintain teamwork, collaboration, and a collegial working environment.


Confer with instructional and support personnel in developing alternative solutions to unusual or unforeseen problems.


Participate in budget planning activities, and develop expenditure review and control procedures to insure a cost beneficial and cost effective operational mode.


Assume a leadership role in the functions and activities of site and District advisory committees and groups.


Assist the educational community in understanding the site, District and state goals and objectives, and the strategies utilized for achieving them.


Participate in the planning, development, implementation, interpretation, and administration of policies, rules, and regulations, and negotiated employee agreements.


Supervise, direct, and coordinate the assignment of instructional personnel and student classroom assignments in accordance with CSR mandates and District staffing allocations.


Coordinate student and family assistance programs with local service agencies.


Plan, develop, and provide management reports pertaining to the functions, activities, and general educational climate of the school facility.


Confer with site personnel in resolving rights disputes which may include the conduct of formal hearings.


Assist in the conduct of effective and efficient personnel management systems, including the recruitment, selection, retention, and separation of personnel.


May be responsible for managing, monitoring, and evaluating specially funded programs to insure compliance with funding agency standards and guidelines.

QUALIFICATIONS
Knowledge of:
Principles, techniques, strategies, goals, and objectives of public education; philosophical, economic, and legal aspects of public education; procedures, methods, and strategies of organization, management, and supervision; modern innovative and creative curriculum and instructional trends regarding the elementary age child; curriculum development, instructional program delivery strategies and program supervision, assessment, and evaluation; result and performance evaluation techniques pertaining to program and personnel performance effectiveness; human relations strategies, conflict resolution strategies, and team building principles and techniques.

Ability to:
Direct, lead, and coordinate the multifaceted functions and activities of an elementary school facility; demonstrate effective instructional, organizational, and administrative leadership; analyze problems, determine alternative solutions, and make appropriate and effective decisions; communicate effectively in oral and written form; plan, develop, and maintain effective organizational and community relationships; comply with the District’s customer service standards, as outlined in Board Policy.

Experience:
Five years of successful teaching experience or equivalent, and a minimum of three years in an administrative or leadership capacity.

Education:
Equivalent to the completion of a Master of Arts or higher degree in educational administration, instructional technology, or a closely related field.

AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

The Redwood City School District (RCSD) is an equal-opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. title: Lead Geospatial Analyst
description:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.


Roles & Responsibilities:


The Intelligence Mission Enablement Department is seeking a Lead Geospatial Analyst / Engineer to develop and maintain global geospatial data models of critical infrastructure and adversary activity in support of intelligence analysis of threats to U.S. Government equities. Initial priorities include the lifeline sectors of Energy, Fuel/Chemical, Telecommunications, Water, and Transportation. Embedded on-site with the sponsor in Bethesda, MD, this individual will work directly with mission partners to translate intelligence questions into data requirements, establish canonical models, and develop repeatable methods to aggregate, transform, conflate, and validate disparate datasets into trusted global layers. Candidates with strong all-source analytic experience and GEOINT expertise or exposure are encouraged to apply; this role blends mission analysis, data engineering, and geospatial tradecraft.

Basic Qualifications:


  • Typically requires a minimum of 8 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 6 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 3 years’ experience; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.
  • Experience in all-source intelligence analysis, GEOINT, geospatial analysis, data engineering, or a closely related field; ability to interpret and integrate data from multiple sources and assess provenance, completeness, and uncertainty.
  • Experience developing geospatial data models, canonical schemas, global infrastructure datasets, or geospatial layers for intelligence or mission applications.
  • Ability to engage mission partners, define requirements, and communicate technical and analytic findings clearly to sponsor stakeholders.
  • Must have an active Top Secret/SCI with polygraph. U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.
  • This position has an on-site requirement of 5 days a week on-site.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience analyzing critical infrastructure and adversary activities, particularly Energy, Fuel/Chemical, Telecommunications, Water, or Transportation sectors.
  • Experience applying code-based automation, AI-assisted workflows, or agentic AI methods with appropriate human review, traceability, and validation; experience with entity resolution and cross-source geospatial conflation.
  • Familiarity with GIS tools, spatial databases, geospatial standards, Python, SQL, or automated data pipelines for ingestion, transformation, conflation, and quality validation.

This requisition requires the candidate to have a minimum of the following clearance(s):

Top Secret/SCI/Polygraph

This requisition requires the hired candidate to have or obtain, within one year from the date of hire, the following clearance(s):

Top Secret/SCI/Polygraph

$147,200 - $184,000 - $220,800 Annual

Onsite

title: Patching Engineer
description:
Salary: ₱90,000 – ₱130,000 per month

About the role

Lead vulnerability remediation and patch management initiatives across Windows servers, infrastructure, applications, cloud environments, and container platforms. In this role, you will assess security risks, coordinate remediation activities, improve security processes, and help strengthen the organisation's overall cyber resilience.

Key responsibilities

  • Patch Windows servers and ensure the timely remediation of identified vulnerabilities.

  • Lead complex remediation efforts across infrastructure, applications, and cloud environments.

  • Analyse vulnerability scan results, assess risk, and recommend or implement appropriate remediation actions.

  • Develop and maintain scripts or tools to automate remediation and patching tasks.

  • Work closely with system owners, patching teams, and application developers to coordinate and execute remediation activities.

  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and analysts.

  • Serve as a subject matter expert for vulnerability management tools and remediation processes.

  • Ensure remediation activities comply with internal policies, service-level agreements, and regulatory requirements.

  • Maintain accurate documentation of remediation actions, patching activities, and risk assessments.

  • Support audit and compliance efforts by providing evidence of remediation and patching.

  • Identify and address gaps in vulnerability and patch management processes.

  • Stay current with emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and security technologies.

  • Contribute to the development of remediation playbooks, patching standards, and knowledge base articles.

What we're looking for

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • At least five years of experience in vulnerability management, system administration, or cybersecurity engineering.

  • Strong hands-on experience with vulnerability scanning tools such as Qualys, Tenable, or Rapid7.

  • Proficiency in patch management and configuration tools such as SCCM, WSUS, or ConnectWise Automate.

  • Solid understanding of CVSS scoring, threat modelling, and risk prioritisation.

  • Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, as well as container security.

  • Excellent troubleshooting, scripting, and documentation skills, including PowerShell or Python.

  • CISSP, CISM, CEH, Security+, or an equivalent certification is advantageous.

  • Cloud security certifications, such as AWS Certified Security – Specialty or Azure Security Engineer Associate, are advantageous.

Position Summary: Electrical Test Technician 1s execute test and commissioning procedures on a variety of integrated power products developed by the company. They verify assemblies against schematics, specifications, and approved settings, control energization of equipment in the test bay, diagnose and correct electrical failures, and document results to IE and customer acceptance criteria.


Work Schedule: Monday - Friday 6:00 am - 3:30 pm (every other Friday off)



Essential Functions - Other Duties May Be Assigned

Testing/Quality

Test Execution and Commissioning

  1. Executes assigned factory acceptance test (FAT) and inspection and test plan (ITP) procedures on a variety of IE manufactured equipment, working under the direction of a Technician 2 or above on complex and first-of-kind sequences.
  2. Performs pre-energization verification, including insulation resistance (megger), dielectric withstand, contact and winding resistance, continuity, and point-to-point wire-match checks against single line, three line, and control schematics.
  3. Verifies CT and PT ratio and polarity, phase rotation, phasing, and grounding and bonding continuity across the integrated assembly.
  4. Tests and proves protective devices and control circuits, including pickup and dropout, trip and close circuit proving, interlocks, key interlocks, permissives, and EPO circuits, and confirms applied settings against the approved settings sheet; performs relay secondary injection under the direction of a Technician 2 or above.
  5. Serves as the controlling authority for energizing and de-energizing equipment in the test bay, and applies test power in support of OEM and subcontractor commissioning activities after verifying that source voltage, phase rotation, and capacity are correct for the equipment being served.
  6. Operates load banks to the assigned test sequence and load steps, monitors and records results, and directs Electrical Test Assistants in cable handling and connection.
  7. Executes transfer and failure-mode testing, including automatic and manual transfer, static and maintenance bypass operation, loss-of-source simulation, and return-to-normal sequences, and records transfer times and system response.
  8. Performs point-to-point verification of PLC and control system I/O and verifies indication, alarm annunciation, metering accuracy, and remote monitoring points to the customer’s power monitoring or building management system.

Safety and Energized Work Control

  1. Executes lockout/tagout for multi-source assemblies, including utility and generator sources, UPS DC and battery systems, and temporary test power, under IE energy control procedures and under a group LOTO plan established by a Technician 2 or above.
  2. Verifies absence of voltage, discharges stored energy including DC bus and capacitors, and applies protective grounds before contact.
  3. Selects and wears arc-flash and shock PPE appropriate to the equipment’s incident energy and the task performed, and verifies that PPE and insulated tools are inspected and in date.
  4. Establishes and maintains approach and arc-flash boundaries, barricading, signage, and controlled access around energized test bays and load bank cable runs.
  5. Participates in pre-test safety briefings covering test sequence, energy sources and isolation points, hazards, communication method, and emergency response, and leads the briefing for routine tests within own scope.
  6. Enforces IE safety requirements on customer representatives, third-party commissioning agents, and OEM field service personnel working in the test bay, including LOTO, PPE, and boundary compliance, and confirms that no outside party energizes equipment, operates breakers, or applies test power.
  7. Exercises stop-work authority whenever an unsafe condition is developing and does not resume work until the condition is corrected.
  8. Maintains a clean and controlled test area, routes cable and test leads to prevent trip and arc hazards, and reports near misses, incidents, and equipment damage immediately.

Troubleshooting and Technical Judgment

  1. Assists in diagnosing root cause of test failures across power, control, and instrumentation circuits using electrical theory, schematics, and systematic isolation.
  2. Distinguishes among design, manufacturing, component, OEM equipment, and test-setup causes of failure and routes each to the correct owner rather than reworking the symptom.
  3. Makes real-time decisions during testing that prevent equipment damage, personnel injury, or catastrophic failure, including aborting a test sequence in progress.
  4. Interprets manufacturer test data, timing curves, and industry acceptance criteria to determine pass or fail status, and refers marginal and disputed results to a Technician 2 or above.
  5. Performs corrective repairs, re-terminations, and settings changes within own scope, then re-tests to prove the correction and documents the retest.
  6. Uses power quality analyzers, oscilloscopes, thermal imaging, and data logging equipment to characterize harmonics, voltage distortion, load imbalance, hot connections, and intermittent conditions.
  7. Identifies drawing errors, field changes, and as-built deviations and submits redlines through proper channels for drawing update.
  8. Understands how PLC and monitoring systems interact with the assembly and verifies the electrical conditions those systems depend on; does not modify PLC programming or perform OEM proprietary test procedures, and escalates conditions that exceed own qualification or authority without delay.

Customer, Vendor, and Subcontractor Interface

  1. Supports customer and engineer witness testing, demonstrating test steps and results and answering technical questions within scope.
  2. Applies and controls power for OEM commissioning of vendor-supplied UPS and switchgear while the OEM performs its own test procedures, and maintains sufficient familiarity with those procedures, including UPS battery commissioning and discharge sequences, to recognize and prevent conditions that could damage equipment or injure personnel.
  3. Hosts and escorts third-party commissioning agents and OEM field service personnel working within IE-integrated products.
  4. Coordinates test bay access, scheduling, load bank availability, and equipment isolation with vendor and subcontractor personnel so their activities do not conflict with IE testing.
  5. Verifies that vendor and subcontractor activities remain within the scope of the approved procedure and reports scope changes and out-of-scope requests to the Lead Electrical Test Technician or Electrical Test Supervisor.
  6. Witnesses and records third-party test results affecting IE scope and confirms their documentation is turned over before the equipment ships.
  7. Represents IE professionally in front of customers, consultants, and commissioning agents, maintaining a courteous and composed manner when tests do not go as planned.

Documentation, Quality, and Coordination

  1. Completes test forms, data sheets, and checklists accurately and legibly at the time of test; results are never back-filled, estimated, or copied forward.
  2. Records test results and commissioning status in CxAlloy so progress is visible to project teams, commissioning agents, and customers.
  3. Writes nonconformance reports (NCRs) for failed or out-of-tolerance conditions with sufficient detail to support disposition and root-cause review.
  4. Verifies the assembly against the job traveler, bill of materials, approved submittals, and torque sheets before energization, and restores the equipment to shipping configuration after test.
  5. Assembles and turns over complete test packages, including data sheets, settings sheets, punch lists, redlines, and third-party reports, and closes punch list items within own scope.
  6. Confirms test instruments are within calibration and records instrument identification and calibration dates on test records.
  7. Logs time and job hours accurately to the correct job, phase, and cost code, and flags conditions that will affect test hours or the ship schedule.
  8. Coordinates daily with assembly, quality, engineering, and project management on test readiness, and provides hands-on direction to Electrical Test Assistants, verifying their work before results are recorded.

Other Essential Duties

  • Maintains regular and consistent job attendance, comes to work on time.
  • Follows and complies with IE Core Values.
  • Follow and comply with IE safety program. Must maintain a safe and clean work area at all times.
  • Complies with OSHA Arc Flash safety standards, always wears appropriate PPE.

INTERMOUNTAIN ELECTRONICS (IE)

title: Manager, Pharmacy Business Analysis
description:
Your Role

The Pharmacy Operations and Stabilization team provides end-to-end oversight of all Pharmacy benefit intent, quality assurance, testing, and production stabilization activities ensuring benefit changes are clearly defined, accurately validated, and effectively managed from issue identification through resolution within a matrixed environment. The Manager, Business Analysis will report to the Sr Manager, Operations and Stabilization. In this role you will manage the team who owns the end-to-end translation of pharmacy benefit intent into business requirements, operational frameworks, and quality validation strategies; provide consultative leadership across quality assurance (QA), testing, and production stabilization activities; and influence cross-functional decisions to resolve complex issues and improve benefit accuracy, operational performance, and governance across matrixed business, clinical, technical, and vendor teams.

Our leadership model is about developing great leaders at all levels and creating opportunities for our people to grow – personally, professionally, and financially. We are looking for leaders that are energized by creative and critical thinking, building and sustaining high-performing teams, getting results the right way, and fostering continuous learning.

Your Work

In this role, you will:

  • Provide analytical support through the analysis and interpretation of data in support of cross-functional business operations
  • Contribute to annual operating plans, capital budgets and forecasts, and build business cases for new business initiatives (cost/benefit analysis)
  • Develop, prepare and analyze reports for management review, and present to various levels of management
  • Define business requirements and provide analysis to increase operational efficiency
  • Analyze actual results against plan and forecast and recommend interventions where appropriate

  • Translate pharmacy benefit intent, business needs, and operational inputs into clear requirements, process flows, test scenarios, and supporting documentation

  • Support quality assurance and user acceptance testing by validating benefit configuration, documenting results, and coordinating defect resolution

  • Analyze production issues, trends, and root cause indicators to support timely triage, escalation, remediation, and prevention efforts

  • Partner with business, clinical, technical, and vendor teams to clarify requirements, resolve questions, and ensure alignment across implementation and stabilization activities

  • Maintain dashboards, trackers, reports, and issue documentation to support operational visibility, leadership updates, and decision-making

Your Knowledge and Experience

  • ​​Bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience

  • ​Requires at least 7 years prior relevant experience, including 3 years of management experience gained as a team leader, supervisoror project/program manager

  • Requires extensive experience with healthy plan pharmacy operations

  • Requires experience translating business intent into business requirements, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, and operational validation plans

  • Requires experience supporting quality assurance, user acceptance testing, regression testing, defect management, and post-implementation validation for pharmacy benefit or healthcare operations initiatives

  • Preferred experience supporting large-scale pharmacy benefit implementations, annual benefit changes, product launches, client implementations, or system migration efforts

Hybrid

This role requires employees to be in-office based on our hybrid workplace model, balancing purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility. For most teams, this means coming into the office two days each week.

Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need.

title: Packaging Improvement Engineer
description:
Position Summary

The Packaging Improvement Engineer partners with cross-functional teams, equipment manufacturers, and packaging suppliers to improve packaging-system performance across the company. The role focuses on protecting product quality, food safety, and regulatory compliance while making packaging operations safer, more reliable, more consistent, and less wasteful. To support these improvements, the engineer establishes and improves packaging standards, converts operating data and field observations into practical solutions, and supports plants in resolving critical packaging and equipment issues. The position will be based at one of our four manufacturing facilities but will support all sites.

At Daisy Brand, we are committed to delivering high performing packaging solutions for our customers, and safe, experience enhancing solutions for our consumers. As a Packaging Improvement Engineer, you will play a critical role in shaping the future of packaging at Daisy Brand while working in a collaborative and growth-oriented environment. Join us to contribute to exciting projects and help us achieve our company's goals.

Location and Travel Requirements

Travel Requirements: Up to 25%

This position operates under a hybrid work model, requiring onsite presence Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday, with Wednesday and Friday designated as remote workdays. While this schedule is typical, team or business needs may require additional onsite days.

Boone hires will initially work from a temporary office in Ames, IA, and have increased travel requirements until the new manufacturing plant in Boone, IA, opens, which is expected in 2028. Once construction is complete, the position will move onsite to the Boone plant.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Packaging Continuous Improvement Activities, Projects, and Processes by:

  • Scheduling, coordinating, communicating, and verifying packaging improvement activities from problem definition through sustained results.
  • Identifying and driving improvements in packaging equipment, materials, operating methods, changeovers, inspection systems, and sanitation.
  • Leading initiatives to improve line efficiency, equipment reliability, throughput, and labor effectiveness while reducing packaging waste, giveaway, rework, downtime, and defects.
  • Using structured problem-solving methods such as 6M, root-cause analysis, Pareto analysis, capability studies, statistical process control, and designed experiments.
  • Developing business cases, expected benefits, trial plans, acceptance criteria, and post-implementation verification for improvement projects.
  • Analyzing manufacturing and packaging data using Excel, Power BI, statistical software, historian/MES data, or visualization platforms to identify trends, quantify losses, determine root causes, and verify that improvements are sustained.

Lead Packaging Quality and Process Standardization by:

  • Auditing packaging lines to verify that approved equipment settings, centerlines, materials, inspection methods, sanitation requirements, and operating procedures are being followed.
  • Establishing and maintaining packaging standards for critical parameters such as fill accuracy, seal temperature, dwell time, pressure, cooling, package integrity, code quality, and package appearance.
  • Partnering with plants, cross-functional teams, and vendors to design and execute controlled trials that resolve packaging unknowns, confirm repeatable solutions, and support data-based recommendations for equipment, material, parameter, or procedural changes.
  • Driving adoption and sustainment of packaging improvements by engaging plant leadership, operators, maintenance, quality, sanitation, and engineering resources in the development, implementation, training, and ongoing verification of new standards.

Provide Technical Support and Capability Development by:

  • Responding to critical packaging, product-quality, food-safety, and equipment-performance issues, including defects, complaints, excessive waste, downtime, and performance gaps, by supporting plants in investigating causes and implementing corrective actions that meet current targets and specifications.
  • Collaborating with OEMs and material suppliers on equipment capability, packaging-material performance, specifications, testing, troubleshooting, and improvement opportunities.
  • Identifying recurring equipment failure modes, evaluating mechanical condition and process capability, and partnering with Maintenance and OEM resources to eliminate chronic losses rather than repeatedly adjusting around equipment deficiencies.
  • Creating practical technical documentation, including troubleshooting guides, centerline sheets, health checks, inspection standards, and training materials, that explains both the required standard and the engineering rationale behind it for operators, mechanics, engineers, and technical resources.
  • Sharing proven methods and lessons learned across sites to accelerate standardization and prevent repeat issues.

Support Equipment Projects and Commissioning by:

  • Participating in equipment FATs, SATs, commissioning, capability studies, startups, and performance acceptance activities to ensure new or modified packaging systems meet agreed-upon safety, quality, throughput, waste, reliability, and maintainability requirements.
  • Documenting proven operating settings once the line is running consistently and meeting these requirements.

Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements

Required Qualifications

  • Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Packaging Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field is preferred; equivalent packaging or manufacturing experience will be considered.
  • Experience: Five or more years of experience in packaging engineering, manufacturing engineering, or continuous improvement is preferred, with an emphasis on hands-on packaging equipment troubleshooting, process optimization, and sustained improvements in line efficiency, reliability, package quality, and waste reduction. Experience in food manufacturing is preferred.
  • Technical Skills:
    • Knowledge of food-packaging materials and how material properties such as thickness, coefficient of friction, sealant behavior, barrier properties, stiffness, dimensional variation, and supplier tolerances interact with packaging equipment, package integrity, and process capability.
    • Familiarity with applicable packaging test methods and standards, including ASTM and ISTA methods where relevant, and experience with package-integrity, seal-performance, material, and distribution testing.
    • Experience with packaging equipment and machinery in a manufacturing setting.
    • Proficiency in CAD software for packaging design is a plus.
  • Problem-Solving: Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with a focus on developing practical and cost-effective solutions.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: In-depth understanding of food packaging standards, including FDA, USDA, and global food safety regulations.
  • Project Management: Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, from concept to implementation, while meeting deadlines.
  • Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills to collaborate with internal teams and external suppliers, including the ability to lead and facilitate cross-functional continuous improvement meetings, guide structured problem-solving discussions, and establish clear action items, owners, and follow-up timelines.
  • Attention to Detail: High level of accuracy and detail orientation in material selection, testing, and reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Packaging Materials and Shelf Life: Experience with food-grade packaging materials and process- and material-based shelf-life extension techniques.
  • Dairy Experience: Experience in dairy manufacturing.
  • Automation and Controls: Working knowledge of PLC-controlled packaging equipment, HMI recipes, servo systems, VFDs, sensors, vision/inspection systems, temperature controls, pneumatics, and automated reject systems, with the ability to troubleshoot packaging-process interactions in partnership with controls and maintenance resources.

Company Overview

Daisy Brand is the market leader in two billion-dollar categories – sour cream and cottage cheese. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, we’ve earned the trust of Americans through consistency and quality across five generations as a family-owned company. Our success has been guided by a simple belief: good food, much like good work, starts with integrity. That mindset continues to shape how we make our products, run our business, and support the people behind the brand.

At Daisy Brand, tradition and innovation go hand in hand. We invest thoughtfully in advancements that strengthen our products and operations, supporting responsible, long-term growth. In 2025, we broke ground on a new manufacturing facility in Boone, Iowa, further strengthening our supply chain alongside our established plants in Garland, Texas; Casa Grande, Arizona; and Wooster, Ohio. Looking ahead, our state-of-the-art Innovation Center, opening in 2026, will bring together research, food science, culinary, and technology teams to shape the future of our products. Recent work from these teams includes the development of the squeeze pouch and new line of dips, reflecting an intentional approach to modernization while staying true to the quality our consumers expect.

At the heart of Daisy Brand is its people. The company is intentionally structured to be collaborative and accessible, with an entrepreneurial mindset encouraged at every level. We hire with the goal of building long-term careers and provide an environment where employees are trusted to think critically, take initiative, and continue learning. Growth here isn’t accidental; it’s actively supported and shared.

To support our employees and their families, Daisy Brand offers a people-first benefits package that includes:

  • A no deductible, $0 premium option for employee only medical coverage
  • Access to virtual healthcare and wellness programs
  • A 401(k) program with company match, plus weekly safe harbor and annual profit-sharing contributions
  • Company paid short and long-term disability coverage and 2x annual salary in life and AD&D insurance
  • Four weeks of paid time off, plus 20 hours of floating holidays in your first full year of employment
  • Annual rollover and payout options for any unused paid time off
  • Paid time for volunteering and community involvement
  • Tuition reimbursement and ongoing professional development opportunities
  • Fitness and wellness incentives
  • And more.

Daisy Brand is a nicotine-free company. Daisy Brand is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Veterans and disabled encouraged to apply.

title: Deli Bakery- Assistant Manager
location: Air Force Academy - USAF Academy, CO 80840
description:
ASSISTANT MANAGER/SHIFT LEAD

title: REGISTERED CLINICIAN-BILINGUAL PREFERRED
description:
PROGRAM

The Vista Hill Learning Assistance Center Program and Mental Health Contracts Program are teams of therapists, behavioral rehabilitation staff, and psychiatrists who provide comprehensive treatment and work in a seamless and integrated manner at school locations with teachers, school counselors and administrators. Clinical staff address school related issues and help students succeed with academics, social interactions, and improve family relationships.

POSITION

The Clinician is responsible for the clinical integrity, assessment, planning and delivery of mental health services to the student and family. She/he assures that all provided services, program documentation, and billing are consistent with company policies and various county and community contracts and any federal, state, county, and district requirements. Duties include:

  • Provide school based counseling/mental health services to school-age students.
  • Practice as a member of a multidisciplinary team
  • Provide clinical assessments, intervention and support to students.
  • Complete proper clinical documentation in a timely manner.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Master's Degree
  • ACSW/AMFT/APHA/APCC, registration or License in good standing with the CA Board of Behavioral Science.
  • Experience working in school-based mental health program, mental health clinic, day treatment facility or other behavioral health setting.
  • 2-4 years professional experience in working with high risk youth.
  • Experience and knowledge in assessment and treatment of children and adolescents.
  • Valid CA drivers license and reliable transportation required.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.
  • Must pass background check, drug test, TB test and COVID vaccine requirements.

HOURS

Monday- Friday, 40 hours per week, school hours.

PAY

$35.50 for Registered

$37.25 for Licensed

These are starting rates and may be adjusted up based on education and experience.

Current Vista Hill employees in these job titles for 2024 are paid:

$35.50 – $37.48 for Registered; and

$39.30- $42.60 for Licensed

BENEFITS

Employees working over 30 hours a week receive employer-paid benefits, including medical, dental, vision, paid time off (vacation and sick leave), paid holidays, employer-paid retirement contribution and clinical supervision (if applicable). Some programs qualify for student loan forgiveness programs.

Registered Clinicians will also receive 2 hours a week of Clinical Supervision time.

Employees who work less than 30 hours a week do not qualify for healthcare benefits.

ABOUT US

Vista Hill is all about serving people. As a dynamic community-based organization, we develop and maintain a diverse array of quality services and programs throughout San Diego County. Our programs range from brief early intervention and preventive work with youth experiencing challenges, to treatment with school age kids, to long-term special education and training for individuals with developmental disabilities. We can be found assisting families in very difficult situations in many of our communities large and small, rural and suburban. You will see our caring staff working with challenging populations that most other agencies shy away from in areas that are conveniently located to the people we serve.

At Vista Hill we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles. Vista Hill is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Pediatric Hematologist/Oncologist
description:
Goryeb Children’s Hospital at Morristown Medical Center, part of Atlantic Health System, is seeking a full-time, board-certified/board-eligible Pediatric Hematologist/Oncologist to join its Pediatric Hematology/Oncology Department. As the original Valerie Fund Children’s Center in New Jersey, the hospital is dedicated to providing high-quality care close to home for pediatric patients across Northern New Jersey. A full member of the Children’s Oncology Group, the center manages approximately 40-50 new oncology diagnoses and over 3000 clinic visits each year. The physician will handle both inpatient and outpatient responsibilities on a rotating basis and must be comfortable with lumbar punctures as well as bone marrow aspiration and biopsy.

The ideal candidate will be board-certified in pediatrics, fellowship-trained, and board-certified/ board-eligible in pediatric hematology/oncology, with a strong commitment to patient- and family-centered care. Specific interest in Pediatric Hematology is also desired. The Hematology team is supported by a Hematology nurse navigator as well as social worker. Goryeb Children’s Hospital hosts a 38-physician pediatric residency program and serves as a branch campus of Sidney Kimmel Medical College at Thomas Jefferson University, offering ample teaching and research opportunities. Quality improvement and clinical research, especially in collaboration with residents, are integral to the role.

Role and Responsibilities:

  • The physician will collaborate with pediatric surgery, pediatric intensive care, pediatric palliative care, pediatric neurosurgery, orthopedic oncology, and radiation oncology to provide comprehensive care.
  • The multidisciplinary team, currently in growth mode, includes 4 advanced nurse practitioners, a dedicated Hematology/Oncology pharmacist in clinic, a nurse manager, APHON-certified nurses, social workers, a psychologist, an educational liaison, a child life specialist, a dietitian, and CRAs. Patients also benefit from integrative meidicine and pet therapy opportunities.
  • Proton Beam center for adults and children planning to open in first quarter 2027.
  • The physician will ensure that the physical and psychosocial needs of patients and their families are met throughout treatment and will continue to provide care in the long-term follow-up program after the completion of therapies.

To learn more about this opportunity, please send your CV to Lori Velasco, Physician Recruiter, at Lori.Velasco@atlantichealth.org

Salary Range: $205,000 - $250,000 base salary (exclusive of quality and productivity incentives)

Benefits

  • Competitive salary

  • Robust benefits with health, dental, Rx and vision plans

  • 403b retirement plan with company match

  • Comprehensive Malpractice Policy

  • Non-Profit Health System – eligible for Federal Student Loan Forgiveness

  • Generous PTO, annual sick days, and paid holidays

  • CME allowance and reimbursement for CDS/DEA, licensing, and boards

  • Tuition reimbursement for advanced degrees

  • Outstanding growth & mentorship opportunities

Qualifications

  • Must be BE/BC in Pediatrics
  • Fellowship trained in Pediatric Hematology/Oncology
  • 3-5 years of post-fellowship experience is preferred but not mandatory
  • Must be licensed or eligible for licensure in the State of New Jersey

title: Mill Utility
description:
Mill Utility Operator

Employment Type: Full Time Permanent

Division: P&H Milling

Location: Cambridge, ON

Wage: $30.56

Who We Are

Parrish & Heimbecker, Limited (P&H) is a Canadian, family-owned company with over 115 years in agriculture. We operate across four divisions: Grain & Crop Inputs, Flour Milling, P&H Foods, and New-Life Mills, delivering trusted solutions from crop inputs and grain handling to flour milling, livestock nutrition, and egg production. By connecting Canadian farms to tables across the country and beyond, we’re committed to quality, innovation, and sustainability as we shape the future of food and agriculture.

Your Team

P&H Milling: P&H Milling is Canada’s largest Canadian-owned milling company, producing high-quality flour and cereal products for bakeries, food manufacturers, and consumers. From coast to coast, we transform Canadian wheat into trusted products that feed families at home and abroad.

Want to know more? Start here: P&H Milling Group | Parrish & Heimbecker

The Role

We are seeking a Mill Utility Operator to join our P&H Milling team. The Mill Utility Operator is responsible for cleaning and tempering the appropriate wheat for gristing, supporting the First and Second Millers with daily flour production activities, and completing required sanitation duties. This position is also responsible for loading bulk flour tankers for shipment.

Day to Day

  • Operate and monitor incoming wheat, wheat transfer and tempering systems, including silo levels, grist selection and tempering times.
  • Grind and test wheat samples for protein, moisture and falling number.
  • Monitor wheat cleaning, transfer and milling equipment, escalating equipment or production concerns to the First Miller and Maintenance.
  • Complete required inspections, magnet cleaning, re-feeding activities and operational records.
  • Load bulk flour tankers and coordinate with the shunting driver to meet scheduled shipments.
  • Conduct routine plant inspections and assist mill and maintenance teams with troubleshooting production issues.
  • Provide coverage in wheat receiving and perform related duties as required.
  • Follow all health and safety procedures, lockout requirements, GMPs and daily cleaning schedules.
  • Perform additional milling duties as assigned.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Grade 12 education or equivalent.
  • Mechanical aptitude and ability to troubleshoot milling equipment.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
  • Ability to work 12-hour continental or 8-hour rotating shifts and overtime as required.
  • Ability to perform the physical requirements of the position, including climbing stairs frequently throughout the shift.

Why Join Us

At P&H, our people are our priority. We’re committed to fostering a workplace that supports professional growth, well-being, and a strong sense of community. Join a team that shares your Passion & Heart for Canadian agriculture, and take advantage of benefits designed to help you thrive and succeed:

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage (Medical, Dental, and Vision)
  • RRSP Matching Program
  • Paid Time Off and Wellness Initiatives
  • Learning and Development Opportunities
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Employee Assistance Program

Apply Today!

We thank all applicants, however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

P&H does not use artificial intelligence or automated decision-making tools to screen, assess, or select applicants. All applications are reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team or hiring team.

Job Summary

The Surgical Technician collaborates with the surgeon and perioperative team to deliver high-quality patient care during surgical procedures. This role prepares and maintains sterile surgical fields, assists with procedures, and ensures instruments and supplies are used appropriately. The Surgical Technician adheres to infection prevention standards, regulatory requirements, and facility policies to support optimal patient outcomes.

Essential Functions

  • Prepares and maintains the operating room for surgical cases, ensuring all equipment, instruments, and supplies are properly organized and available by applying principles of Universal Precautions, asepsis, and sterile technique.
  • Assists the surgical team by anticipating the needs of the surgeon and passing instruments and supplies accurately and efficiently.
  • Handles surgical instruments according to their instructions for use and ensures proper sterilization, inspection, and assembly.
  • Performs point-of-use cleaning and carefully handles instruments in compliance with infection control and professional standards. Performs sponge, needle, and instrument counts with the circulating nurse to ensure patient safety.
  • Assists in patient positioning, draping, and transfer methods to ensure safety and comfort during procedures.
  • Maintains and updates physician preference cards, ensuring accurate supplies and instruments are available for procedures.
  • Cleans, reprocesses, and sterilizes surgical instruments and equipment following established protocols.
  • Contributes to perioperative team efficiency by restocking supplies, returning equipment to storage, and ensuring operating rooms are ready for subsequent cases.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Maintains regular and reliable attendance.
  • Complies with all policies and standards.

Qualifications

  • Technical School graduate of Surgical Technology or Practical Nursing program required or
  • Associate Degree in Surgical Technology or Applied Sciences required
  • 0-2 years of operating room surgical technician experience required

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Knowledge of surgical procedures, instrumentation, and aseptic techniques.
  • Strong understanding of sterilization methods and infection prevention practices.
  • Ability to anticipate the needs of the surgical team and respond quickly and effectively.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills to collaborate with the perioperative team.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills to ensure procedural accuracy and efficiency.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks in a high-pressure environment while maintaining professionalism.

Licenses and Certifications

  • BCLS - Basic Life Support required
  • CST - Certified Surgical Technologist preferred

Oro Valley Hospital (OVH) is a 176-bed hospital that also has a freestanding emergency center, Northwest Transitions Inpatient Rehabilitation, Skilled Nursing Unit, and large physician group. With these varied access points, you have your choice of settings in which to work. OVH's culture centers around providing safe, quality care to patients, but also to foster a work environment based on teamwork, commitment to a shared goal and recognizing employees for all they do to care for our patients. Often described as a “family,” the staff at OVH take pride in doing the best they can to care for their community. OVH is accredited by The Joint Commission and is an equal opportunity employer: race, gender, disability and Veteran status, and VEVRAA Federal Contractor – priority referral Protected Veterans requested.

title: Director, Clinical Quality - HEDIS
description:
Your Role

The Clinical Quality [Commercial Populations] team is accountable for the organization’s quality ratings, preventive and primary care outcomes for Blue Shield of California’s Commercial members, and financial risks associated with quality performance. The Director, Clinical Quality will report to the Senior Director, Clinical Quality. In this role you will be accountable for provider network quality performance within the capitated (HMO), fee-for-service (PPO), self-funded and specialty care networks. This includes accountability for designing and executing strategic roadmaps to achieve quality and financial targets, as well as managing a cross-functional, statewide team.

Our leadership model is about developing great leaders at all levels and creating opportunities for our people to grow – personally, professionally, and financially. We are looking for leaders that are energized by creative and critical thinking, building and sustaining high-performing teams, getting results the right way, and fostering continuous learning.

This person is required to live within 50 miles of the Oakland, Rancho Cordova, Woodland Hills or Long Beach office locations.

Your Work

In this role, you will:

  • Design, implement, and sustain enterprise quality programs aligned with the Quality Roadmap and Work Plan with specific accountability to drive quality outcomes performance with large medical systems, small physician practices and specialty care teams
  • Accountable for quality improvement and assurance across current and anticipated member populations, using data to design multi-year HEDIS and CAHPS improvement pathways and change management initiatives within complex systems
  • Build and maintain strategic partnerships across clinical, operational, technical, and legal teams in order to translate enterprise business strategy into actionable plans that support care teams across the state of California in medical, dental and vision care
  • Lead collaboration on integrated quality initiatives spanning care delivery, pharmacy, wellness, and technology at all levels, including directly with Chief Medical Officers, Chief Nursing Officers and Medical Directors by demonstrating HEDIS expertise and a variety of influence techniques
  • Serve in a leadership role with provider partners, ACOs, and enterprise quality governance bodies in order to lead and direct decisions about return-on-investment and provider investment tradeoffs
  • Own annual quality program planning, evaluation, and budget development with specific accountability for creating successful strategic plans for provider incentives, clinical innovation funding, and penalty risk management with three-year time horizons
  • Lead teams using data-driven insights, industry best practices, and continuous improvement methodologies including hiring, firing, onboarding, promotion and reward, as well as creating workforce and staffing plans
  • Adapt quality strategies and program design in response to evolving business and regulatory needs, including close partnership with Senior leadership to align Quality outcomes, technology and artificial intelligence strategies

Your Knowledge and Experience

  • Requires Bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree

  • Requires at least 10 years prior relevant experience achieving outcomes in HEDIS, CAHPS or other publicly reported quality ratings targets
  • Requires 6 years of prior people management experience with direct responsibility for supervising, coaching, and evaluating direct reports
  • This person is required to live within 50 miles of the Oakland, Rancho Cordova, Woodland Hills or Long Beach office locations.
  • Master’s degree or equivalent in healthcare administration, public health, or a related field and Lean Six Sigma, or a comparable planning, strategy, program, or improvement certification preferred

  • Requires experience within a California health plan or comparable regulated payer environment and applying structured change-management methodologies within the California healthcare system

  • Requires demonstrated experience leading annual or multi-year planning in a complex, matrixed organization

  • Requires at least 6 years’ experience implementing quality interventions for and with preventive care and behavioral health or dental providers
  • Experience with health equity interventions within clinics, practices or medical groups preferred
  • Physical Requirements: Office Environment - roles involving part to full time schedule in Office Environment as well as required travel within the state of California. Based in our physical offices and work from home office/deskwork – Activity level: Sedentary, frequency most of the workday

Hybrid

This role requires employees to be in-office based on our hybrid workplace model, balancing purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility. For most teams, this means coming into the office two days each week.

Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need.

title: Food Services Worker II
description:

Micron is looking for a highly motivated Chemical and Gas Technician to support the systems that deliver bulk and specialty gases and process chemicals to our manufacturing operations. In this critical role, you will be responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing this equipment. Your work will keep our facilities safe and running efficiently. You’ll work closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, and the Emergency Response Team to resolve equipment issues, support system changes, and give technical expertise during alarm and abnormal events. • Monitor system alarms and performance, and respond to abnormal conditions

• Follow Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), line-break, PPE, and hazardous materials safety requirements

• Document work orders, maintenance activity, and findings accurately

• Support installation, modification, and startup of new gas and chemical equipment

• Take part in continuous improvement, root cause analysis, and procedure updates

• High school diploma or equivalent

• Working knowledge of mechanical, pneumatic, and basic electrical/controls systems

Preferred Qualifications

• Associate’s degree in a technical field, or equivalent military/technical training

• Experience in a similar role in the semiconductor industry or a related field (e.g., pharmaceutical, chemical processing, solar)

• 3+ years of hands-on experience with gas cabinets, VMBs, bulk gas, or chemical distribution systems

• Interest in or experience with applying AI tools or agentic workflows to improve work processes

Work Environment & Requirements

• This is a shift-based role. Successful candidates may be assigned to day or night shift, including weekends and holidays according to the shift schedule.

• Must be able to wear a respirator, and/or self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA), when required. This includes passing a medical evaluation and fit test.

• Must be able to wear required PPE, including chemical-resistant suits, gloves, face shields, and safety glasses.

• Work is performed in manufacturing, cleanroom, and facilities support areas with exposure to hazardous gases and chemicals under controlled conditions.

title: Senior Private Cloud Security Engineer
description:
Azqore, a next-generation provider of Information Systems and banking operations services, is a subsidiary of Indosuez Wealth Management, the wealth management arm of the Crédit Agricole Group. As a global company, Azqore is committed to providing wealth managers with integrated, turnkey digital solutions.

With its headquarters in Switzerland and its Asia hub in Singapore, Azqore currently serves around thirty clients through its proprietary S2i platform, supporting approximately CHF 200 billion in assets under management.

At the heart of our strategy, we are looking for a Senior Private Cloud Security Engineer in charge of the security engineering of Azqore private-cloud platforms and their workloads, with a primary focus on Virtuozzo Application Platform and Virtuozzo Hybrid Infrastructure. The engineer will establish secure platform patterns, hardening, segmentation, secrets management, observability and audit-ready evidence for regulated workloads..

👨‍🔧 Your responsibilities

  • Private-cloud security architecture - Design and maintain the security baseline for VAP/VHI, virtualization or OpenStack-like components. Translate threats and regulatory expectations into practical controls.

  • Environment isolation - Define secure patterns for DEV, SIM, UAT, EXP and sandbox environments, including tenant separation, administrative boundaries and controlled connectivity.

  • Network security - Specify and review segmentation, firewall rules, bastion and jump-host access, TLS, DNS and restricted-egress patterns. Apply least connectivity and produce traceable flow documentation.

  • Platform hardening - Establish CIS-aligned hardening, secure configuration, follow-up of patching, vulnerability management and configuration-drift controls and platform services.

  • Secrets and service access - Participate in designing Vault namespaces, policies, authentication methods, rotation, TTL and revocation. Secure GitLab JWT and production AppRole patterns. Prevent clear-text secrets in Terraform/Ansible and deployment tooling.

  • Secure automation - Review and harden centralized Ansible content and IaC. Define code-review, testing, promotion, inventory and credential-handling practices.

  • Registry and image security - Participate in governance of internal Docker and Nexus registries, approved base images, scanning, SBOM, provenance and promotion of trusted images into private-cloud environments.

  • Observability and detection - Define security logging and telemetry with ELK/EFK, Open Telemetry and Splunk. Ensure key administrative and security events are detectable and retained.

  • Operational readiness - Create runbooks, exception handling, incident support, evidence packs and knowledge transfer. Establish ownership with Infrastructure, Network, SOC, IAM, DevOps and application teams.

🧙‍♂️ Your core competencies

  • Bachelor Degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science or equivalent

  • Minimum 8 years delivery and hands-on security experience with:

    1. Private cloud, Kubernetes, OpenStack, OpenShift, VMware or an equivalent platform.

    2. Linux and container hardening, vulnerability management and secure administration.

    3. Network segmentation, firewalling, bastion patterns, TLS and DNS fundamentals.

    4. HashiCorp Vault or comparable enterprise secrets-management implementation.

    5. GitLab CI/CD and Ansible security, including secure credential patterns.

    6. Container image, registry, SBOM and trusted-base-image governance.

    7. Security logging, SIEM integration and operational evidence.

    8. Ability to create a baseline and drive implementation across several infrastructure owners.

  • Proven achievements as a hands-on architect-builder who can turn an incomplete requirement into a clear security design, working implementation, evidence, documentation and an operational handover.

  • Keen to roll up sleeve and do beyond advisory work but also involved in deployment and production support work.

  • Understands availability, recoverability, change control, audit evidence, operational ownership and supportability.

  • You are autonomous, tenacious and rigorous. Boredom won't be part of your day, but you need to know how to organize yourself to manage the multiple issues underway.

title: Scientist 3, Translational Oncology
description:
The Position

Bold thinkers, breakthrough makers: Join a team of curious minds who challenge the status quo, create what’s next in science and technology, and have the freedom to turn daring ideas into real breakthroughs.


The Opportunity


Join our Translational Oncology department as a Scientist 3, where your technical precision and deep immunological expertise will bridge the gap between early discovery and life-changing clinical therapies. In this pivotal, lab-based role, you will serve as our go-to flow cytometry expert, thriving in a collaborative, fast-paced environment that empowers bold scientific inquiry.


  • Advance Oncology Pipelines: Generate robust, reproducible data to propel novel oncology targets from exploratory discovery straight into clinical development.
  • Lead Flow Cytometry Execution: Design, execute, and analyze highly complex flow cytometry experiments, acting as the primary technical subject matter expert for the team.
  • Innovate Multicolor Panels: Build, optimize, and troubleshoot large, high-parameter multicolor flow cytometry panels to enable deep immunophenotyping.
  • Master Low-Input Samples: Perform rigorous, meticulous analysis on challenging, scarce samples, specializing in low cell count workflows.
  • Drive Cross-Functional Strategy: Partner seamlessly with diverse project teams, translating and presenting complex data insights to influence key strategic decisions.
  • Execute In Vitro Assays: Maintain and manipulate both primary human/murine cells and established cell lines using rigorous cell culture techniques.

Who you are


  • You hold a PhD in Immunology, Oncology, or a closely related scientific discipline.
  • You bring exceptional, hands-on mastery of advanced flow cytometry, with a proven track record of building and troubleshooting large multicolor panels.
  • You possess demonstrated expertise in analyzing challenging, low-input/low cell count biological samples.
  • You have a deep, foundational understanding of immunology and tumor biology.
  • You are proficient in sterile cell culture techniques involving both primary cells and established cell lines.
  • You are an adaptable, detail-oriented team player with strong communication skills who thrives when navigating shifting priorities.
  • You have experience or are willing to develop in-vivo models.
  • Documented record of professional achievement in the form of high-quality publications.

Preferred

Job Summary

The Patient Care Technician (PCT) provides high-quality, patient-centered care by performing delegated tasks in alignment with the PCT's training and the department's needs. Under the direct supervision of a Registered Nurse (RN) or Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) (LVN at Texas facilities), the PCT supports patient care by assisting with activities of daily living, maintaining a safe and organized care environment, and ensuring effective communication within the healthcare team.

Essential Functions

  • Assists nursing staff in delivering care, performing delegated basic patient care services, and ensuring a clean, safe, and well-organized environment.
  • Collects and records patient data, including vital signs, height, weight, oxygen saturation, intake/output, and calorie counts, reporting findings to the RN/LPN/LVN.
