title: Wastewater Systems Specialist - (Employbridge)
description:
Job Summary:

The Wastewater Systems Specialist is responsible for the operation, performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of the wastewater pretreatment system supporting Powder Coat Manufacturing. The position serves as the designated Operator in Responsible Charge (ORC) and primary technical resource for wastewater treatment operations, including system monitoring, chemical management, process optimization, sampling, documentation, and routine operator-level maintenance.

As a member of the Powder Coat Manufacturing team, this position supports
manufacturing operations by ensuring the wastewater treatment system remains reliable, operational, and capable of meeting production demands. The role also provides limited support to powder coat pretreatment processes as they relate to wastewater generation, treatment performance, and process chemistry.

The position works closely with Operations, Environmental, Maintenance, Engineering, and Quality personnel to support safe, efficient, and compliant operations. Environmental retains responsibility for regulatory compliance assurance, permit management, and reporting activities, while Maintenance retains responsibility for major repairs, equipment reliability programs, and preventative maintenance execution. The successful candidate will help improve system performance, reduce downtime, maintain accurate operational records, and minimize single-point-of-failure knowledge risks through documentation, training, and standardized work practices.

Minimum Qualifications: (Education, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills):

  • Minimum HS diploma, GED, or equivalent Required.
  • Minimum 3 years’ experience in manufacturing, industrial maintenance, process equipment, utilities, wastewater treatment, powder coat systems, or related industrial operations.
  • Strong mechanical troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to understand process flow, cause-and-effect relationships, and root cause analysis principles.
  • Ability to safely work around industrial equipment and hazardous chemicals.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications.
  • Ability to read technical manuals, control logic diagrams, equipment documentation, schematics, and procedures.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • NCDEQ Wastewater Physical/Chemical Grade I certification or ability to obtain
    certification within a timeframe established by PowerSecure.

Preferred Qualifications: (Education, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills):

  • Associate’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering Technology, Mechatronics,
    Manufacturing/Industrial Systems Technology, Chemical Process Technology, Water and Wastewater Technology, or related field.
  • Experience with powder coat systems and water treatment processes.
  • Experience operating/maintaining industrial wastewater treatment systems.
  • Experience with preventative maintenance systems and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • NCDEQ Wastewater Physical/Chemical Grade I or II certification

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Wastewater Treatment System Ownership

  • Serve as the designated Operator in Responsible Charge (ORC) for the
    wastewater pretreatment system.
  • Operate, monitor, and optimize wastewater treatment processes to support uninterrupted manufacturing operations.
  • Conduct routine inspections of treatment equipment, tanks, pumps, piping, valves, instrumentation, chemical feed systems, and associated infrastructure.
  • Monitor treatment system performance and make routine operational
    adjustments as necessary.
  • Manage wastewater treatment chemical inventories and coordinate chemical deliveries.
  • Monitor and maintain treatment system operating parameters.
  • Develops and maintains preventative maintenance programs for wastewater equipment.
  • Coordinates maintenance activities with Production and Maintenance teams.
  • Establishes critical spare parts recommendations and inventory requirements.
  • Identify operational issues and implement corrective actions within established operating procedures.
  • Evaluate treatment process performance and recommend improvements to efficiency, reliability, and operational effectiveness.
  • Coordinate wastewater treatment activities with production schedules and changing manufacturing demands.
  • Respond in a timely manner to treatment system upset, assist with spill
    response, and coordinate contingency actions during equipment failures.
  • Troubleshoots mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and process-related equipment issues.
  • Assists with installation, startup, testing, and commissioning of new equipment.

Sampling, Monitoring and Documentation

  • Collect wastewater samples in accordance with established procedures and schedules.
  • Maintain chain-of-custody documentation and sampling records as required.
  • Maintain operating logs, inspection records, calibration records, chemical usage records, and treatment system documentation.
  • Perform routine monitoring activities and document operational observations.
  • Track treatment system performance metrics and operating trends.
  • Maintain wastewater treatment operating procedures, inspection forms, and supporting documentation.
  • Support Environmental personnel by providing operational data, documentation, and treatment system information required for compliance programs and regulatory reporting.
  • Ensure records are accurate, complete, and readily available for review.

Training and Knowledge Management

  • Maintains Grade I or higher Physical/Chemical Wastewater ORC licensure in good standing with the State board.
  • Complete continuing education and training requirements to maintain certification
  • Develop and maintains procedures and work instructions, such as SOPs, guides, instructions, and training materials for powdercoat and wastewater treatment systems.
  • Trains production operators and backup ORCs on safe and effective operation of equipment.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

Must be capable of working in a fast-paced environment around automated equipment, industrial machines, moving conveyors, ovens, and chemicals.

This position will require standing, stooping, bending, and limited lifting/manipulation of up to 60lbs. Manual dexterity required to manipulate tools, operate digital equipment, which includes computers, HMIs, and other such equipment with small fine buttons and small parts of machines.

General manufacturing environment which may include working near hot equipment. Must be capable of wearing personal protective equipment (TYVEK, mask, booties, face shield, steel-toe boots, etc.).

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of the position. All employees may have other duties assigned at any time.

About Us

PowerSecure, a Southern Company subsidiary, is a leading provider of innovative energy solutions to electric utilities and their industrial, institutional, and commercial customers.

Join Our Power Team!

We invest in high-value and cost-effective benefits for our employees. Our benefits package includes:

title: Tønsberg kommune - Næringssjef

Du har relevant erfaring fra næringsutvikling, næringsliv, innovasjon eller gründerarbeid, og kan vise til gode resultater. Du har erfaring fra ledelse, prosjekt- eller utviklingsarbeid, og forstår næringslivets dynamikk. Utdanning på bachelor- eller masternivå innen samfunnsutvikling, økonomi, innovasjon eller tilsvarende er ønskelig. Relevant erfaring kan veie opp for formell utdanning. Eget nettverk i næringslivet i regionen er en fordel, og det samme er kjennskap til kommunal sektor.

  • Samfunnsorientert med god rolleforståelse: Du forstår samspillet mellom næringsliv, administrasjon og politikk, og navigerer klokt i en kompleks organisasjon.

En sentral og synlig rolle med reell påvirkningskraft i en kommune med store ambisjoner. Du får en variert og fleksibel arbeidshverdag, med dyktige, engasjerte og inkluderende kolleger som spiller hverandre gode og ønsker å skape resultater sammen. Som Næringssjef får du sette ditt preg på utviklingen av Tønsberg og bidra til å skape gode rammevilkår for fremtidens næringsliv.

  • Working outside on job sites for long hours in all seasons including summer months.

title: Transportation Computer Scientist, Senior Principal
description:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

The Center for Integration Transportation, Surface Transportation, has an opening for a Senior Principal Transportation Computer Scientist starting immediately. MITRE CIT offers candidates an exciting opportunity to influence and integrate efforts across world class professionals addressing the nation’s most challenging transportation problems. As a member of our Transportation leadership team, you will have an opportunity to develop and execute transportation research and development programs and accelerate innovation for stakeholder benefits. You will lead and participate in large, complex efforts to understand intelligent transportation system needs, address development challenges, identify strategic opportunities, and develop new prospects to have increased impact. Interested candidates will work with a multi-disciplinary group of researchers, engineers, business analysts, and strategists across all transportation modes, including highways and automotive, rail and transit, and aviation.


Job Responsibilities:

The Senior Principal Transportation Computer Scientist will apply knowledge and skills to growing MITRE’s capabilities and business opportunities as part of our Surface Transportation team, with a focus on automotive, rail, and transit modes, with an emphasis on Digital Infrastructure and Intelligent Transportation Systems. An ability to understand our sponsors’ needs, effectively communicate these to our technical teams, and help to solve our sponsors most difficult problems is required. Candidates are expected to build partnerships with external organizations, and to help guide and shape the work for our sponsors throughout the planning, execution, and delivery process.


The Computer Scientist will be working with individuals that are experts in data analytics, computer science, modeling and simulation, mathematics/statistics, operations research, policy analysis, and safety management systems. Problems are often ambiguous and challenging. The ability to interface and collaborate with sponsors is required. Other responsibilities include business development, strategic planning, technical quality reviews, capability development, collaboration, and communications across department and organizational boundaries. An ability to foster state/local/federal government relationships and university and industry association relationships, and an ability to leverage external skill sets from other stakeholders is also an expectation.

  • Drive MITRE’s effort to advise the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT), state and local agencies, professional associations, and commercial organizations on appropriate modal strategies and solutions and their safe integration into the broader transportation system-of-systems.
  • Contribute to a vision for an integrated, seamless, equitable, and resilient US transportation system and how to evolve toward that vision over time.
  • Shape long-term, strategic view of MITRE’s modal activities; to include participating in the broader Surface Transportation planning efforts, consistently scanning the horizon for new opportunities, collaborating with the relevant MITRE Labs as they periodically refresh their transportation research strategies and plans, and exploring improvements in program operations.
  • Engage with government sponsors, industry partners, and universities to understand and shape desired outcomes and associated work activities in the rail and transit fields.
  • Build partnerships with personnel representing relevant manufacturers, suppliers, USDOT officials, state and local transportation planners and system operators, and other stakeholders to develop collaborative solutions for adoption in the modal industries.
  • Provide thought leadership as input to a comprehensive policy framework or other work products that aim to guide USDOT and other relevant stakeholders in ensuring the safe development and operation of modal systems and the broader transportation system-of-systems.
  • Provide thought leadership to sponsor and MITRE strategies within the modal administrations and across the broader surface transportation domain by analyzing and tracking emerging trends in transportation including, automation, connectivity, and electrification, and developing balanced approaches to anticipate and incorporate these shifts into operations.
  • Develop an understanding of stakeholder challenges, develop, and execute proposals that identify where MITRE can provide differentiated value to address the challenges directly while also bringing broader value for a safer world.
  • Represent MITRE on select committees/boards/working groups.



Basic Qualifications:

  • Typically requires a minimum of 10 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 8 years and a Master’s degree; or 5 years and a PhD
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in surface transportation, including substantial work with federal or state transportation agencies, in roles requiring both technical depth and strategic advisory responsibility.
  • Proven ability to advise senior government clients—shaping research direction, translating technical findings, and communicating complex material to executive, policy, and technical audiences.
  • Working knowledge of data-driven approaches, modeling, and analytics applied to transportation problems, with the ability to identify where AI/ML or advanced analytics can add genuine value.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce polished, high-impact deliverables under deadline.
  • Bachelor’s degree in transportation engineering, systems engineering, computer science, public policy, or a related discipline.

  • This position requires a minimum of 3 days a week on-site.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Graduate degree in a relevant field (transportation, systems engineering, data science, public policy, or related).
  • Direct experience with U.S. DOT programs, FHWA, NHTSA, or OST-R, including familiarity with federal research program structures, funding mechanisms, and policy development processes.
  • Hands-on experience with transportation data standards (e.g., WZDx, GTFS, CV pilot data, connected infrastructure data) or national data-sharing platforms and governance frameworks.
  • Applied fluency in AI/ML, data science, or advanced analytics—including the ability to evaluate technical approaches, interpret results, and communicate findings to non-technical audiences.
  • Experience leading or contributing to business development efforts, including sponsor cultivation, proposal development, and strategic positioning of research capabilities.
  • Familiarity with MITRE’s FFRDC model and experience working in a public-interest, sponsor-facing research environment.
  • Active engagement in relevant professional communities (TRB, ITS America, AASHTO, SAE, or equivalent).

The role translates Australian and relevant/aligned State Government health policy, funding and system reform into actionable strategies aligned with WAPHA’s commissioning, capacity building, coordination and compliance outcomes.

title: Packaging Improvement Engineer
description:
Position Summary

The Packaging Improvement Engineer partners with cross-functional teams, equipment manufacturers, and packaging suppliers to improve packaging-system performance across the company. The role focuses on protecting product quality, food safety, and regulatory compliance while making packaging operations safer, more reliable, more consistent, and less wasteful. To support these improvements, the engineer establishes and improves packaging standards, converts operating data and field observations into practical solutions, and supports plants in resolving critical packaging and equipment issues. The position will be based at one of our four manufacturing facilities but will support all sites.

At Daisy Brand, we are committed to delivering high performing packaging solutions for our customers, and safe, experience enhancing solutions for our consumers. As a Packaging Improvement Engineer, you will play a critical role in shaping the future of packaging at Daisy Brand while working in a collaborative and growth-oriented environment. Join us to contribute to exciting projects and help us achieve our company's goals.

Location and Travel Requirements

Travel Requirements: Up to 25%

This position operates under a hybrid work model, requiring onsite presence Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday, with Wednesday and Friday designated as remote workdays. While this schedule is typical, team or business needs may require additional onsite days.

Boone hires will initially work from a temporary office in Ames, IA, and have increased travel requirements until the new manufacturing plant in Boone, IA, opens, which is expected in 2028. Once construction is complete, the position will move onsite to the Boone plant.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Packaging Continuous Improvement Activities, Projects, and Processes by:

  • Scheduling, coordinating, communicating, and verifying packaging improvement activities from problem definition through sustained results.
  • Identifying and driving improvements in packaging equipment, materials, operating methods, changeovers, inspection systems, and sanitation.
  • Leading initiatives to improve line efficiency, equipment reliability, throughput, and labor effectiveness while reducing packaging waste, giveaway, rework, downtime, and defects.
  • Using structured problem-solving methods such as 6M, root-cause analysis, Pareto analysis, capability studies, statistical process control, and designed experiments.
  • Developing business cases, expected benefits, trial plans, acceptance criteria, and post-implementation verification for improvement projects.
  • Analyzing manufacturing and packaging data using Excel, Power BI, statistical software, historian/MES data, or visualization platforms to identify trends, quantify losses, determine root causes, and verify that improvements are sustained.

Lead Packaging Quality and Process Standardization by:

  • Auditing packaging lines to verify that approved equipment settings, centerlines, materials, inspection methods, sanitation requirements, and operating procedures are being followed.
  • Establishing and maintaining packaging standards for critical parameters such as fill accuracy, seal temperature, dwell time, pressure, cooling, package integrity, code quality, and package appearance.
  • Partnering with plants, cross-functional teams, and vendors to design and execute controlled trials that resolve packaging unknowns, confirm repeatable solutions, and support data-based recommendations for equipment, material, parameter, or procedural changes.
  • Driving adoption and sustainment of packaging improvements by engaging plant leadership, operators, maintenance, quality, sanitation, and engineering resources in the development, implementation, training, and ongoing verification of new standards.

Provide Technical Support and Capability Development by:

  • Responding to critical packaging, product-quality, food-safety, and equipment-performance issues, including defects, complaints, excessive waste, downtime, and performance gaps, by supporting plants in investigating causes and implementing corrective actions that meet current targets and specifications.
  • Collaborating with OEMs and material suppliers on equipment capability, packaging-material performance, specifications, testing, troubleshooting, and improvement opportunities.
  • Identifying recurring equipment failure modes, evaluating mechanical condition and process capability, and partnering with Maintenance and OEM resources to eliminate chronic losses rather than repeatedly adjusting around equipment deficiencies.
  • Creating practical technical documentation, including troubleshooting guides, centerline sheets, health checks, inspection standards, and training materials, that explains both the required standard and the engineering rationale behind it for operators, mechanics, engineers, and technical resources.
  • Sharing proven methods and lessons learned across sites to accelerate standardization and prevent repeat issues.

Support Equipment Projects and Commissioning by:

  • Participating in equipment FATs, SATs, commissioning, capability studies, startups, and performance acceptance activities to ensure new or modified packaging systems meet agreed-upon safety, quality, throughput, waste, reliability, and maintainability requirements.
  • Documenting proven operating settings once the line is running consistently and meeting these requirements.

Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements

Required Qualifications

  • Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Packaging Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field is preferred; equivalent packaging or manufacturing experience will be considered.
  • Experience: Five or more years of experience in packaging engineering, manufacturing engineering, or continuous improvement is preferred, with an emphasis on hands-on packaging equipment troubleshooting, process optimization, and sustained improvements in line efficiency, reliability, package quality, and waste reduction. Experience in food manufacturing is preferred.
  • Technical Skills:
    • Knowledge of food-packaging materials and how material properties such as thickness, coefficient of friction, sealant behavior, barrier properties, stiffness, dimensional variation, and supplier tolerances interact with packaging equipment, package integrity, and process capability.
    • Familiarity with applicable packaging test methods and standards, including ASTM and ISTA methods where relevant, and experience with package-integrity, seal-performance, material, and distribution testing.
    • Experience with packaging equipment and machinery in a manufacturing setting.
    • Proficiency in CAD software for packaging design is a plus.
  • Problem-Solving: Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with a focus on developing practical and cost-effective solutions.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: In-depth understanding of food packaging standards, including FDA, USDA, and global food safety regulations.
  • Project Management: Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, from concept to implementation, while meeting deadlines.
  • Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills to collaborate with internal teams and external suppliers, including the ability to lead and facilitate cross-functional continuous improvement meetings, guide structured problem-solving discussions, and establish clear action items, owners, and follow-up timelines.
  • Attention to Detail: High level of accuracy and detail orientation in material selection, testing, and reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Packaging Materials and Shelf Life: Experience with food-grade packaging materials and process- and material-based shelf-life extension techniques.
  • Dairy Experience: Experience in dairy manufacturing.
  • Automation and Controls: Working knowledge of PLC-controlled packaging equipment, HMI recipes, servo systems, VFDs, sensors, vision/inspection systems, temperature controls, pneumatics, and automated reject systems, with the ability to troubleshoot packaging-process interactions in partnership with controls and maintenance resources.

Company Overview

Daisy Brand is the market leader in two billion-dollar categories – sour cream and cottage cheese. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, we’ve earned the trust of Americans through consistency and quality across five generations as a family-owned company. Our success has been guided by a simple belief: good food, much like good work, starts with integrity. That mindset continues to shape how we make our products, run our business, and support the people behind the brand.

At Daisy Brand, tradition and innovation go hand in hand. We invest thoughtfully in advancements that strengthen our products and operations, supporting responsible, long-term growth. In 2025, we broke ground on a new manufacturing facility in Boone, Iowa, further strengthening our supply chain alongside our established plants in Garland, Texas; Casa Grande, Arizona; and Wooster, Ohio. Looking ahead, our state-of-the-art Innovation Center, opening in 2026, will bring together research, food science, culinary, and technology teams to shape the future of our products. Recent work from these teams includes the development of the squeeze pouch and new line of dips, reflecting an intentional approach to modernization while staying true to the quality our consumers expect.

At the heart of Daisy Brand is its people. The company is intentionally structured to be collaborative and accessible, with an entrepreneurial mindset encouraged at every level. We hire with the goal of building long-term careers and provide an environment where employees are trusted to think critically, take initiative, and continue learning. Growth here isn’t accidental; it’s actively supported and shared.

To support our employees and their families, Daisy Brand offers a people-first benefits package that includes:

title: Service Manager
description:

  • Analytical thinking: Able to identify patterns, understand operational challenges and approach problems systematically.

title: [Job-32675] Dynamics 365 CRM Senior Software Developer, Colombia
description:
At CI&T, we help large enterprises transform the potential of AI into real business impact with AI Deployment, AI-native execution, and tech-integrated business solutions.

With 30 years of experience in technological transformation, we accelerate innovation with expertise in Agentic SDLC, Application modernization, Data & AI, Martech and Business strategy.

We are 8,000 CI&Ters across more than 25 countries, collaborating to build solutions with real impact. AI is already part of how we work, evolve, and innovate every day.


We’re looking for a Dynamics 365 CRM Software Developer to join a dedicated nearshore team building a placement management platform for a US education client. The CRM core runs on Dynamics 365 and Dataverse, integrated with Azure services and a React frontend. You’ll build and extend the CRM layer and the Azure components around it.

What you’ll do

  • Customize Dynamics 365 and Dataverse: tables (entities), forms, views, business rules and Power Automate flows.
  • Develop C# plugins and custom workflow logic, following Dynamics best practices for performance and upgrades.
  • Configure Dataverse security, including security roles, business units, teams and field-level security.
  • Build Azure Function Apps that integrate with Dataverse, managed in Azure DevOps repos and deployed through Azure DevOps pipelines.
  • Work in an Agile team, overlapping with US Central Time.

What we’re looking for

  • Hands-on experience with Dynamics 365 CE / Dataverse development, with production delivery.
  • Strong C# / .NET skills, including plugin development and the Dataverse SDK or Web API.
  • Practical experience with core Azure resources and concepts, especially Function Apps, plus CI/CD in Azure DevOps.
  • Experience managing solutions and moving them across environments (ALM).
  • Upper-intermediate or advanced English for daily communication with US stakeholders.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Dynamics 365 Customer Service, Customer Insights – Journeys or Contact Center.
  • PCF components or Power Apps portals / Power Pages.
  • Certifications such as PL-400 (Power Platform Developer), MB-910 or AZ-204.

title: Post Fab Technician (Day Shift 2)
description:
onsemi is seeking a Post‑Fab Technician in Hopewell Junction, NY. This is a multi‑skilled, hands‑on role responsible for supporting semiconductor manufacturing through equipment maintenance, process execution, and day‑to‑day operations. This position requires a strong willingness to learn semiconductor processes, troubleshoot and maintain manufacturing equipment, and support smooth production flow while adhering to all safety, quality, and cleanroom standards.

This role is ideal for a technician who enjoys hands‑on technical work, problem‑solving, and working in a high‑precision manufacturing environment. Application Technicians work 12‑hour compressed shifts in a cleanroom environment.

Day 2 Schedule: Thursday, Friday, Saturday every other Wednesday 6:30 AM – 7:00 PM

Sign on Bonus: $5,000

Employees in this role may be required to participate in the site Emergency Response Brigade and support emergency preparedness activities. Participation includes maintaining required training, certifications, and response readiness in accordance with site policies and business needs.

Operations Support

  • Operate production tools safely and efficiently within a cleanroom environment
  • Load/unload wafers, materials, and tools in accordance with operating procedures
  • Monitor equipment performance, alarms, and system statuses
  • Support production goals by maintaining equipment uptime and tool availability
  • Follow all safety, ESD, and contamination control guidelines

Process Support

  • Learn and monitor semiconductor manufacturing processes according to documented procedures
  • Assist with process setup, recipe changes, and process optimization under engineering guidance
  • Perform inspections, measurements, and basic data collection to ensure process stability
  • Identify process deviations and escalate issues to engineering or leadership as required

Equipment Maintenance

  • Perform preventative maintenance (PM) on semiconductor manufacturing equipment
  • Diagnose and troubleshoot equipment issues to minimize downtime
  • Assist with equipment repairs, part replacements, and system calibrations
  • Maintain maintenance logs and documentation in accordance with company standards
  • Support equipment startups, shutdowns, and qualification activities

Continuous Improvement & Team Collaboration

  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives for process, equipment, and operations
  • Work closely with engineers, technicians, and operators across shifts
  • Assist with training new team members and documenting procedures
  • Maintain a high standard of housekeeping and organization in work areas
  • Perform all job duties in a safe and responsible manner, supporting all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security (EHS&S) programs
  • High school diploma or GED with 1-2 years of technical manufacturing experience
  • Ability to stand and walk for up to 10-hours per day in a cleanroom environment while wearing coveralls, hoods, booties, safety glasses, and gloves.
  • Basic computer literacy, including the use of email, web-based systems, and common office productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Office applications) to document work, create reports, and communicate with team members.
  • Must be self-motivated, showing initiative and drive to exceed performance expectations.
  • Analytical problem-solving and troubleshooting skills with close attention to detail.
  • Ability to work well in a diverse team environment.
  • Ability to work with minimal supervision and adjust to rapidly changing priorities.
  • Able to speak and write fluently in English.
  • Must be able to lift up to 35 lbs.

Preferred

  • Vocational High School, Technical training, or technical trade certificate.
  • Proficient in working with hand tools, meters, and calibration tools
  • Knowledge of and ability to follow 5S, LEAN is a plus.

Hourly: onsemi is excited to share the base salary range for this position is $18.46 to $32.26 exclusive of fringe benefits or potential bonuses. The final pay rate for the successful candidate will depend on geographic location, skills, education, experience, and/or consideration of internal equity of our current team members. We also offer a competitive benefits package. https://www.onsemi.com/site/pdf/Benefits-Summary-USA.pdf

title: Director of Security & Safety
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Manages security/loss prevention operations on a daily basis. Areas of responsibilities include protection of property assets, employees, guests and property, accident and fire prevention and response. Ensures that all areas of the property are safe and secure. Maintains logs, certifications and documents required by law and Standard Operating Procedures. Strives to continually improve guest and employee satisfaction while maximizing the financial performance of the department.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 4 years experience in the security/loss prevention or related professional area.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Criminal Justice or related major; 2 years experience in the security/loss prevention or related professional area.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Managing Security/Loss Prevention Operations

• Assists in the development and implementation of emergency procedures.

• Conducts investigation of all losses of property assets and refers to proper management for disposition.

• Deploys security staff to effectively monitor and protect property assets.

• Comply with all Corporate Loss Prevention safety and security management guidelines and procedures.

• Conduct periodic patrols of entire property and parking areas.

• Recognize success across areas of responsibility.

• Handles complaints, settling disputes, and resolving grievances and conflicts, or otherwise negotiating with others.

• Identifies and makes recommendations for minimizing physical hazards and unsafe work practices.

• Implements action plans to monitor and control risk.

• Maintains required reports and documentation regarding patrols of property and parking areas.

• Provides means for obtaining necessary medical attention on a timely basis.

Leading Security/Loss Prevention Teams

• Attends pre- and post-convention and weekly forecast meetings to understand group needs and gather critical information to communicate to Loss Prevention officers.

• Celebrates successes by publicly recognizing the contributions of team members.

• Communicates the importance of safety procedures, detailing procedure codes, ensuring employee understanding of safety codes, monitoring processes and procedures related to safety.

• Encourages and builds mutual trust, respect, and cooperation among team members.

• Identifies the developmental needs of others and coaching, mentoring, or otherwise helping others to improve their knowledge or skills.

• Provides guidance and direction to subordinates, including setting performance standards and monitoring performance.

• Provides personal assistance, medical attention, emotional support, or other personal care to others such as coworkers, customers, or patients.

• Serves as a role model to demonstrate appropriate behaviors.

• Solicits employee feedback, utilizes an "open door" policy and reviews employee satisfaction results to identify and address employee problems or concerns.

• Strives to improve service performance.

• Utilizes interpersonal and communication skills to lead, influence, and encourage others; advocates sound financial/business decision making; demonstrates honesty/integrity; leads by example.

Ensuring Exceptional Customer Service

• Displays leadership in guest hospitality, exemplifies excellent customer service and creates a positive atmosphere for guest relations.

• Empowers employees to provide excellent customer service.

• Meet quality standards and customer expectations on a daily basis.

• Incorporates guest safety and satisfaction as a component of departmental meetings with a focus on continuous improvement.

Conducting Human Resources Activities

• Assists in minimizing cost of accident claims through aggressive claims management.

• Brings issues to the attention of Human Resources as necessary.

• Completes proper documentation and reports all employee accident and general liability incidents to Claims Reporting Service.

• Conducts hourly employee performance appraisals according to Standard Operating Procedures.

• Complete disciplinary procedures and documentation according to Standard and Local Operating Procedures (SOPs and LSOPs) and support the Peer Review Process.

• Administer property policies fairly and consistently.

• Maintain first aid and CPR certifications required for Loss Prevention officers.

• Handles guest problems and complaints.

• Identifies the educational needs of others, developing formal educational or training programs or classes, and teaching or instructing others.

• Provides services that are above and beyond for customer satisfaction and retention.

Additional Responsibilities

• Analyzes information and evaluating results to choose the best solution and solve problems.

• Develops and maintains a working relationship with local law enforcement authorities.

• Informs and/or updates the executives, the peers and the subordinates on relevant information in a timely manner.

• Provides information to supervisors, co-workers, and subordinates by telephone, in written form, e-mail, or in person.

title: Senior Product Manager, Rights & Royalties Modernization
description:
At Warner Music Group, we’re a global collective of music makers and music lovers, tech innovators and inspired entrepreneurs, game-changing creatives and passionate team members. Here, we turn dreams into stardom and audiences into fans. We are guided by three core values that underpin everything we do across all our diverse businesses:
• Curiosity: We do our best work when we’re immersing ourselves in culture and breaking through barriers. Curiosity is the driving force behind creativity and ingenuity. It fuels innovation, and innovation is the key to our future.
• Collaboration: Making music and bringing it to the world is all about the power of originality amplified by teamwork. A great idea, like a great song, travels globally. We ignite passions and build connections across our diverse community of artists, songwriters, partners, and fans.
• Commitment: We pursue excellence for our team and our talent. Everything in music starts with a leap into the unknown, and we’re committed to keeping the faith, acting with integrity, and delivering on our promises.
Technology is one of the most important parts of our business. Whether it’s supporting our songwriters, ensuring we provide the right royalty data to global partners, or helping our creative teams use the latest AI tools to discover new talent—technology plays an invaluable role in our success. Product Managers help turn vision into reality. Check out first-hand accounts from the WMG engineering, product, design, infrastructure and data teams in our blog!
WMG is home to a wide range of artists, musicians, and songwriters that fuel our success. That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone. We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences.
Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.

Your Role

As a Product Manager for Rights & Royalties Modernization at WMG, you will own new platforms that define who owns what, and who is owed what, across one of the largest music catalogs in the world. Every stream, sync deal, and payout depends on accurate rights data and deal performance calculation. In this role, you will use modern, AI-enabled platforms to replace legacy royalty and accounting processes and to improve how we manage our global rights portfolio and pay our artists. You will shape the strategy, roadmap, and organizational change needed for how WMG captures, validates, and activates rights across our recorded music catalog, so music reaches fans and everyone gets paid accurately and on time.

What you'll do

  • Product Ownership: Own the roadmap, both tactical and strategic, for your area. Communicate priorities clearly to engineering, business stakeholders, and leadership.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with engineering, UX design, finance, accounting, legal, business affairs, and label operations stakeholders to turn complex contractual rules into clear, scalable software.

  • Rights & Royalties Data Management: Build new products that capture and maintain ownership splits, territorial rights, terms, and more at a global scale, and then use these contractual terms to automate financial tracking and artist payouts, replacing legacy tools and processes with scalable, auditable systems.

  • User Understanding: Develop a deep understanding of your users across business affairs, copyright administration, A&R, and finance, then design tools that remove manual work from their day.

  • Data-Driven Decisions: Define and track KPIs around rights (e.g. data accuracy, completeness) and royalties (e.g. time-to-pay, calculation accuracy).

Who you are

  • Product Experience: At least 7 years of product management or equivalent experience, including building technical products from idea to launch.

  • Music, Rights or Royalties Expertise: You have hands-on experience with music rights and royalties (e.g. royalty accounting, licensing, rights management). We'll also consider strong candidates with deep experience in music, or in accounting and finance systems.

  • Technical Fluency: Comfortable working with engineers on data models, APIs, and system integrations. You understand the software development lifecycle and can go deep on complex data problems.

  • Navigating Ambiguity: Proven ability to simplify complex business rules and competing stakeholder needs into clear product decisions.

  • Communication: Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to explain rights concepts to technical teams and technical tradeoffs to business partners and executives.

  • Passion: A genuine love for music and a respect for the artists and songwriters behind it.

We'd love it if you also had

• Experience with rights or royalty systems at a label, publisher, collecting society, or DSP

• Experience interfacing with ERP systems like SAP or Oracle

• Experience building master data or source-of-truth platforms

• Experience using AI tools in a hands-on way to rapidly iterate and build products

• Knowledge of key industry concepts (e.g. identifiers like ISRCs, common recording deal structures, neighboring rights and digital performance royalties)

As the home to 10K Projects, Asylum, Atlantic Music Group, East West, FFRR, Fueled by Ramen, Nonesuch, Parlophone, Rhino, Roadrunner, Sire, Warner Records, Warner Classics, and several other of the world’s premier recording labels, Warner Music Group champions emerging artists and global superstars alike. And our renowned publishing company, Warner Chappell Music, represents genre-spanning songwriters and producers through a catalog of more than one million copyrights worldwide. Warner Music Group is also home to ADA, which supports the independent community, as well as artist services division WMX. In addition, WMG counts film and television storytelling powerhouse Warner Music Entertainment among its many brands.
Together, we are Warner Music Group: Independent Minds. Major Sound.
Love this job and want to apply?
Click the “Apply” link at the top of the page, or apply directly with your LinkedIn. Applying with LinkedIn will import all of the information you put in your profile, but will still allow you to upload a resume and cover letter.
Don’t be discouraged if you don’t hear from us right away. We’re taking our time to review all resumes, and to find the best people for WMG.
Thanks for your interest in working for WMG. We love it here, and think you will, too.
WMG is committed to inclusion and diversity in all aspects of our business. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and will evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, religious creed, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, ancestry, marital status, medical condition as defined by state law (genetic characteristics or cancer), physical or mental disability, military service or veteran status, pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

title: Senior Counsel, Patent Litigation
description:
The Position

Genentech is hiring a Senior Counsel, Patent Litigation in Global Legal Pharma, based at Roche’s Genentech campus in South San Francisco, California. This role reports directly to the Senior Director of Global Patent Litigation. It is a high-impact role with significant visibility across the business, leading and supporting patent litigation matters globally, with an emphasis on US matters.

THE OPPORTUNITY

  • Manage and coordinate an active and varied caseload of litigations, appeals, and other adversarial proceedings while advising on substantive legal strategy with foresight and appropriate risk tolerance
  • We are looking for candidates specializing in patent litigations in the life sciences. Experience with ANDA and/or biosimilar matters, both in court and at the PTAB, is preferred. Additional experience with investigations, commercial contract disputes, product liability cases, and/or experience in an in-house setting is also preferred, but not required.
  • Partnering closely with business clients and legal department colleagues to advise on strategic issues while using a practical and business-minded approach.
  • Developing strategies to avoid or resolve regional, national, and international disputes, including directly negotiating license agreements and settlements.
  • Counseling on multi-jurisdictional litigations or other proceedings, including coordinating with counterparts in the U.S. and around the world.
  • Serving as a thought leader for the litigation group in one or more substantive areas.
  • Contributing to cross-functional or departmental projects and teams.
  • Working effectively in teams and with a cross-section of stakeholders within the organization.
  • The successful candidate must be able to work closely and independently with internal domestic/international research & development, commercial, manufacturing, partnering, finance and tax units, among other business units.
  • This position requires being in the office three days a week when not away.
  • Business stakeholders and partners are based in both South San Francisco and Basel, Switzerland; working across cultures and time zones is essential to success.

WHO YOU ARE

  • Education & Legal Bar License: Must have an advanced law degree (i.e. JD) and must be currently licensed to practice law, in good standing, in at least one U.S. state, and must be registered or currently eligible as a Registered In-House Counsel in California.
  • Experience: Minimum 7-10+ years of experience in patent litigation, with significant experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, or life sciences matters. Trial experience required.
  • Subject Matter Expertise: Deep familiarity with US patent litigation practice. Experience in coordinating complex, multi-jurisdictional patent litigation.
  • Critical Competencies: Strong analytical, written, and oral communication skills. Creative problem-solver with a business mindset. Knowledgeable and committed to deploying emerging AI-enabled technologies to increase productivity, speed and efficiency in litigation management.
    • Strategic Litigation Expert:
      • Demonstrated experience in resolving challenging legal issues and proven ability to deliver sound, clear, practical legal advice in a business setting.
      • Superior negotiation skills.
      • Ability to approach complex problems with a creative mindset.
    • Influential Communicator:
      • Excellent judgment and interpersonal skills.
      • Outstanding communication skills, both verbal and written.
      • Superior client-relations skills.
      • An awareness and ability to engage with others of diverse backgrounds.
    • Adaptive and Results-Oriented Performer:
      • Ability to prioritize and work with agility across multiple projects.
      • Ability to work both in a team and independently.
      • Aptitude and interest to learn the scientific/technical side of the business.
      • Comfortable with getting outside of one’s comfort zone and stepping into new areas of practice or business.

  • Global Operating Model and Travel: Requires adaptability for possible early morning/late evening calls to accommodate global time zones and a willingness to undertake necessary domestic and international travel to ensure effective global support and alignment.
  • Other: A degree (undergraduate or graduate) in a biological science or chemistry preferred but not required.

Location

  • This role is located at Roche’s Genentech campus in South San Francisco, California.
  • Relocation benefits are not available for this position.
  • This role is NOT allowable for a remote working arrangement.

The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of California is $203,800 to $378,400. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below.

title: Leasing Specialist (Part-time)
description:
About Waterton

At Waterton, we believe in finding the good and leaving it better. For over 30 years, we’ve been passionate about delivering incredible resident experiences, made possible by offering an extraordinary experience for our talented associates. We value adaptability, curiosity, accountability, and commitment to excellence. If this sounds like you, we’d love to meet you.

Job Summary

As a Leasing Specialist, you will drive occupancy by delivering exceptional resident and prospect experiences. The ideal candidate is customer-focused, sales-driven, adaptable, proactive, and thrives in a collaborative team environment.

What You Need to Succeed

Performance and Business Drive (Get It Done)

Success in this role requires effectively managing high-volume prospect outreach, tour scheduling, and resident priorities. By maintaining a sales-focused mindset and a strong sense of urgency, you convert leads into residents and maximize occupancy.

  • Drive occupancy by conducting engaging community tours, executing effective closing techniques, following up with prospective residents, and managing the leasing process from application through move-in.

Customer Service (Be Kind)

Exceptional service is at the heart of our Resitality® philosophy, creating memorable experiences that go above and beyond resident expectations. By demonstrating Resitality®, you help create a community where residents feel valued, supported, and truly at home.

  • Deliver exceptional service to prospects and residents by responding promptly to inquiries, addressing concerns, and creating positive experiences in every interaction.

Initiative (Own It)

Great associates don't wait for opportunities, they create them. By anticipating needs, taking ownership, and proactively solving challenges, you contribute to community success.

  • Identify opportunities to increase community visibility and traffic through outreach marketing, referrals, competitor analysis, and local market knowledge.

Adaptability (Listen & Talk)

Change is constant and adaptable associates keep communities competitive. By listening, learning, and pivoting quickly, you ensure success in a dynamic environment.

  • Adjust priorities and respond effectively to changing prospect, resident, and community needs in a fast-paced environment.

Teamwork (Have Fun)

High performing communities are built through collaboration and shared accountability. By working as a team, you help create an environment that drives resident satisfaction and operational excellence.

  • Partner closely with office and service team members to deliver a seamless resident experience and ensure compliance with company policies and Fair Housing requirements.

What You’ll Bring – Desired Skills and Experience

  • Minimum of one-year of sales experience.
  • Multifamily property management experience is strongly preferred.
  • Ability to multi-task and adapt in a fast-paced work environment.
  • Excellent communication, conflict resolution, and customer service abilities.
  • Yardi experience preferred.
  • High school diploma or equivalent relevant experience.

At Waterton, we recognize that compensation and benefits are important not only to our associates but to their families as well. We offer a variety of benefits to part-time associates including:

  • Competitive compensation and incentive program participation
  • 401K + match
  • Generous paid time off, volunteer time off, and paid holidays
  • Commitment to job and career advancement

Waterton welcomes all.

Waterton is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Waterton will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

title: Parent Educator/Outreach Specialist
description:
PHMC serves as both a direct service provider to individuals, families, and communities across the region and an intermediary agent—managing large-scale contracts, government and philanthropic partnerships, and multidisciplinary initiatives that require operational sophistication, strategic leadership, and deep mission alignment.

Position Type: Exempt Annual Salary

Accountability: Reports to Program Manager

Location: 1500 Market Street; some travel required throughout Pennsylvania

Job Overview:

Position Type: Full-time, Non-Exempt

The Parent Educator/ Outreach Specialist (PE/OS) maintains weekly contact with participants through meetings (in-person or virtual) or phone calls. This person is responsible for intake assessments, identifying and setting goals with participants, connecting participants to supportive services, and completing periodic progress assessments, including a closing assessment, to document participant progress for HPC’s fatherhood initiatives. The PE/OS provides parenting education sessions for fathers, couples, co-parents, and other child caretakers. The PE/OS a also leads the social media for the Focus on Fathers program and attends outreach events to help to market the program. This person will also be responsible for promoting and conducting outreach activities to recruit fathers who are part of the target populations for participation in services through the Health Promotion Council's Focus on Fathers program and other fatherhood initiatives. A special emphasis will be placed on engaging fathers in the Focus on Fathers program's virtual and in-person classes, through the development of program promotional materials and activities, and creating a strong social media presence. These activities may include, but are not limited to, participation in online, virtual community, and public events as well as in-person community events, such as health fairs, community days, and events held at key organizations that attract and serve community members (e.g., churches, grocery stores, barbershops, etc.). Other activities may also include engaging in direct outreach to organizations and businesses in targeted communities. This position reports to the Program Manager.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide ongoing parenting skills education groups for fathers, couples, and co-parents at various community-based sites, using established curricula.
  • Assist with tracking participant progress to ensure course completion.
  • Assist in identifying, recruiting, and engaging clients for the program.
  • Complete program reports and other written documentation as required.
  • Work closely with partner sites to ensure participant retention through follow-up calls and in-person engagements.
  • Administers evaluation instruments, including intake and closing assessments, and maintains contact notes aligning with program and evaluation requirements across fatherhood programs.
  • Utilizes a variety of contact methods to reach participants.
  • Meets participants in a variety of settings, including online (virtually), participants' homes, and the community.
  • Actively supports and facilitates the ongoing recruitment and retention of parent graduates (fathers) to participate in the Focus on Fathers Alumni Parent groups.
  • Participates in case conferences, trainings, and weekly team meetings.
  • Actively participates in evaluation activities by attending/contributing to CQI team meetings.
  • Works with the program team to assist in the delivery of other program activities.
  • Assists with program evaluation by entering participant data via web-based application.
  • Complete program reports and other written documentation as required.
  • Maintain data tracking sheets of all program contacts, including dates and types of events, number of individuals reached through group or one-on-one communication, and referrals made.
  • Identify and execute ongoing outreach to community organizations and businesses in targeted communities.
  • Establish relationships with leadership at various community organizations as outlined in the marketing and recruitment plan.
  • Provide community education about services available through HPC, the Focus on Fathers program, and other fatherhood initiatives.
  • Provide oversight of recruitment partners and work closely with the Program Manager and Assistant Director to monitor benchmarking goals.

Skills:

  • Excellent oral communication skills.
  • Ability to engage underserved and hard-to-reach populations.
  • Strong organizational skills, including the ability to prioritize multiple assignments.
  • Knowledge of issues related to child development, family life skills, child abuse prevention, healthy relationships, and healthy parenting.
  • Availability during daytime and some evening and weekend hours.
  • Willingness to travel.

Experience:

  • At least one year of direct service experience working with men and families.
  • Experience with clients facing substance abuse, mental health, employment, criminal justice, and other issues.
  • Strong experience with adult education and/or group facilitation.
  • Comfortable working with adults in low-income communities.
  • Knowledge of positive parenting principles and practices.
  • Personal commitment to promoting and being a role model for fathers, couples/co-parents.
  • Must be willing to work a flexible schedule, including some evening/weekend hours as requested.
  • Must successfully pass child abuse clearance; and
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office and web-based data collection applications.

Education Requirement:

High School Diploma or equivalency

PHMC is an Equal Opportunity and E-Verify Employer.

title: Back Office Operations Intern
description:
Azqore is a leader in outsourced banking services. One of the entities under Credit Agricole Indosuez Wealth Management, it provides integrated solutions and quality services to our clients.

Asia Operations provide operational capabilities to Azqore’s client banks, allowing them to focus on executing their strategy, while reducing operational cost and improving operational risk. Commitment to quality and continuous process improvement is at the heart of all Asia Operations activities. It is thus one of the key functions to facilitate and drive Azqore to reach its ambitious growth target, by putting the clients at the center of its activity, being attentive to their needs, bringing them value and increasing their satisfaction.

Within Asia Operations, the intern may be assigned to one of the following teams:

  • Cash Operations: supporting the processing and monitoring of cash transactions and related operational activities.

  • Securities Operations: supporting activities relating to securities and derivatives, which may include settlements, transfers, corporate actions, and asset creation and maintenance.

  • Reconciliation & Investigation: supporting account reconciliations, the identification of discrepancies and the follow-up of operational investigations.

👨‍🔧 Your role


As an Operations Intern, you will support the day-to-day activities of your assigned team. Working under the guidance of experienced colleagues, you will contribute to the accurate and timely processing of operational tasks, while developing an understanding of banking operations, control procedures and client service standards.

Depending on your team assignment, your responsibilities may include:

  • Supporting the processing and monitoring of operational transactions in accordance with procedures and service standards.

  • Assisting with reconciliations and the identification, analysis and follow-up of discrepancies.

  • Helping to handle operational queries and investigations, escalating issues to the appropriate colleagues when required.

  • Performing assigned checks and maintaining accurate, complete operational records.

  • Working with colleagues and relevant stakeholders to support timely and reliable service delivery.

  • Contributing to process documentation and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Following internal procedures and maintaining awareness of operational risk, confidentiality and data protection requirements.

🧙‍♂️ Your core competencies

  • Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Banking, Finance, Business, Economics or a related field. Candidates in their final year of study will be preferred.

  • Strong interest in banking operations and financial services.

  • Careful and organised, with good attention to detail.

  • Proactive, dependable and willing to learn in a team environment.

  • Comfortable working with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.

  • Good written and spoken English.

  • Knowledge of French or Mandarin would be an advantage.

🧠 What you will gain

  • Practical exposure to banking operations in an international environment.

  • An opportunity to learn about Cash, Securities or Reconciliation & Investigation processes.

  • Experience working with operational procedures, controls and client service standards.

  • Support and guidance from experienced Operations colleagues.

title: Sleep Technologist Registered - Nights
description:
Registered Sleep Technologist

  • Full-Time, 36 hours per week
  • Nights, 6:00pm-6:30am
  • Sunday, Monday, Tuesday or Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday

Benefits

  • Health Insurance (Medical, Dental, Vision)
  • 401(k) with matching
  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.

Job Summary

The Sleep Technologist is responsible for administering sleep studies under the direction of a physician to diagnose the type and extent of sleep disorders. This role involves conducting routine patient assessments, scoring sleep records accurately, documenting results, and collecting and transmitting biological specimens for analysis.

Essential Functions

  • Conducts sleep studies in accordance with established protocols and under the direction of a Medical Director, ensuring patient safety and comfort throughout the procedure.
  • Performs and documents comprehensive patient assessments prior to and during sleep studies, addressing patient needs and monitoring physiological data.
  • Scores sleep records accurately, adhering to guidelines and standards, and communicates findings to physicians for diagnostic evaluation.
  • Collects and transmits biological specimens for analysis, following proper procedures and maintaining sample integrity.
  • Documents test results and patient data thoroughly, ensuring compliance with departmental policies and regulatory standards.
  • Maintains and calibrates sleep study equipment, troubleshooting and reporting any malfunctions to ensure effective operation.
  • Provides patient education about sleep studies and explains procedures, promoting understanding and comfort.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Maintains regular and reliable attendance.
  • Complies with all policies and standards.

Qualifications

  • 1-3 years of experience in sleep technology or a related field required

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Proficient in scoring sleep studies and interpreting physiological data.
  • Strong patient care and assessment skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational abilities.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Knowledge of sleep study equipment and maintenance procedures.

Licenses and Certifications

  • RPSGT - Registered Polysomnographic Technologist required or
  • CPSGT - Certified Polysomnographic Technician required
  • BCLS - Basic Life Support required

title: Ultrasound Technologist - Evenings
description:
Ultrasound Technologist
Full time, Evenings: 3 pm - 11 pm, Monday - Friday

Benefits:

  • Comprehensive Health Insurance (Medical, Dental, Vision)
  • 401(k) with matching
  • Student Loan Repayment
  • Educational Assistance
  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package
  • Paid Time Off Available


Job Summary

The Ultrasound Technologist performs high-quality diagnostic ultrasound examinations to assist physicians in the evaluation and treatment of patients. This role requires independent judgment, technical expertise, and a commitment to patient safety and comfort. The Ultrasound Technologist ensures all procedures are appropriately ordered, patient identification is verified, and imaging protocols are followed to produce accurate and reproducible results.

Essential Functions

  • Performs all ultrasound procedures independently, adhering to department protocols and ensuring high-quality, diagnostic imaging results.
  • Verifies patient identification and ensures the appropriate procedures are ordered and acknowledged prior to conducting imaging.
  • Recognizes and documents pathologies during scanning for interpretation by the radiologist, following established protocols.
  • Assumes responsibility for patient care, safety, and comfort during all imaging procedures.
  • Maintains a clean, safe, and organized work environment, ensuring compliance with safety and infection control guidelines.
  • Operates ultrasound equipment safely and effectively, following departmental policies and manufacturer guidelines.
  • Accurately documents imaging procedures and patient information in the electronic health record system, ensuring all associated documents are scanned into PACS for radiologist interpretation.
  • Monitors and maintains an adequate supply of imaging materials and coordinates inventory replenishment as needed.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Maintains regular and reliable attendance.
  • Complies with all policies and standards.

Qualifications

  • 1-3 years of clinical experience as an Ultrasound Technologist required
  • 2-4 years of clinical experience as an Ultrasound Technologist preferred

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Proficiency in ultrasound imaging techniques and equipment operation.
  • Knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and pathology relevant to diagnostic sonography.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively with patients and healthcare teams.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills to ensure accurate imaging and documentation.
  • Ability to work independently and make informed decisions within the scope of practice.
  • Commitment to maintaining patient confidentiality and adhering to ethical standards.

Licenses and Certifications

  • (S) - ARDMS or ARRT - Sonography certification or registry eligible required
  • BCLS - Basic Life Support obtained within the 7 days of employment required
