title: Scheduler, PMO
description:
Who We Are

ATCO Frontec is a leading provider of facilities management, infrastructure, construction, defence and operational support services. We work in complex and remote environments, delivering practical solutions that help our clients and communities thrive.

The Opportunity

We are looking for an experienced Project Scheduler to join our Project Management Office. In this role, you will develop, maintain and analyze project and portfolio schedules to support successful project delivery.

Working closely with Project Managers, Project Controllers, functional leaders and other stakeholders, you will provide schedule visibility, identify critical path impacts and forecast milestone performance. Your analysis and recommendations will help project teams manage risks, address schedule challenges and make informed decisions.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop and maintain detailed project schedules using approved scheduling tools.

  • Establish work breakdown structures, project activities, milestones, dependencies and schedule baselines.

  • Ensure schedules accurately reflect project scope, execution plans and resource requirements.

  • Update schedules based on actual project progress and approved changes.

  • Monitor critical path activities, schedule variance, float consumption and milestone performance.

  • Develop schedule forecasts, what-if scenarios and impact assessments.

  • Identify schedule risks, constraints and cross-project dependencies.

  • Recommend corrective actions and support the development of schedule recovery and contingency plans.

  • Support integrated master schedules and consolidate scheduling information across multiple projects.

  • Produce weekly and monthly schedule reports, dashboards and executive summaries.

  • Report schedule variances and forecast completion dates to project teams and leadership.

  • Support resource loading, utilization planning and the identification of resource conflicts.

  • Participate in project reviews, gate reviews and planning sessions.

  • Ensure scheduling practices align with PMO standards and governance requirements.

What You Bring

  • A bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Construction Management, Project Management or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.

  • Five or more years of project scheduling experience.

  • Experience developing, maintaining and analyzing detailed project schedules.

  • Experience supporting multiple concurrent projects and managing competing scheduling priorities.

  • Strong knowledge of critical path analysis, schedule forecasting, variance analysis and milestone tracking.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Project and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex scheduling information into practical recommendations.

  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively with project teams, functional leaders and senior stakeholders.

Assets

  • Experience working within a PMO, project controls, construction, engineering, utilities, infrastructure or capital projects environment.

  • Experience developing integrated master or portfolio schedules.

  • Experience using Procore, Power BI, SharePoint or Project Online.

  • PMI Scheduling Professional (PMI-SP), AACE Planning and Scheduling Professional (PSP), Project Management Professional (PMP) or a related certification.

Who You Are

You are a detail-oriented scheduling professional who can bring structure and clarity to complex project information. You take a proactive approach to identifying schedule risks, dependencies and emerging challenges, and you work collaboratively with project teams to develop practical solutions.

You are comfortable managing schedules across multiple projects and communicating schedule impacts clearly to both operational and executive audiences.

What Success Looks Like

  • Project schedules are accurate, current and aligned with project scope and execution plans.

  • Critical activities, milestones and dependencies are clearly identified and actively monitored.

  • Schedule risks and potential delays are identified early.

  • Forecasts and schedule reports provide reliable information for decision-making.

  • Project teams receive practical recommendations to support schedule recovery and on-time delivery.

  • Scheduling practices are consistent across the project portfolio.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the country where this position is located before starting work and must maintain any legally required work authorization during employment.

We would like to thank everyone for their application; however, only those being considered for an interview will be contacted.

Final candidates will be required to undergo a Security Clearance Check.

Collection, use, and retention of personal information will be in accordance with ATCO Group privacy policies and practices.

By submitting your resume and personal information to the ATCO Group of Companies, and/or participating in a personal interview, you acknowledge and consent to the collection, use and disclosure of your personal information by the ATCO Group of Companies to determine your suitability for employment opportunities within the ATCO Group of Companies.

title: Regional Program Specialist
company: YOUNG MENS CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION OF METROPOLITAN LOS ANGELES
description:
YMCA OF METROPOLITAN LOS ANGELES

The LA Y is the Center for Community Well-Being in Los Angeles, committed to building stronger communities by providing equitable programs and services to empower all. We are focused on fighting food insecurity, providing equity in education, making sure every child has the opportunity to experience the joy of sports, ensuring kids and teens have a safe place to grow, learn and live a healthy lifestyle. The LA Y’s health and wellness initiatives offer medical and mental health resources to ensure everyone has access to basic health needs. Our mission is to provide services and resources that contribute to the well-being of our community. The LA Y operates 29 Centers and over 200 program sites across LA County.

*This position is grant funded, and continued employment is contingent upon the availability and renewal of funding and compliance with grant requirements. Positions may be modified or eliminated if funding is reduced, discontinued, or not renewed.*

POSITION SUMMARY

  • Connect community members impacted by HR1 policy changes and new community engagement requirements to YMCA volunteer opportunities where they can complete required hours and support continued benefit eligibility.
  • Match individuals with appropriate YMCA volunteer opportunities based on required hours, location, availability, interests, and ability to participate.
  • Guide community members through the volunteer placement process, including identifying opportunities, completing onboarding, and preparing to begin service.
  • Work closely with Certified Enrollment Specialists (CES) to receive referrals and connect individuals who need volunteer hours to meet HR1 requirements with available YMCA placements.
  • Maintain an up-to-date pipeline of YMCA volunteer opportunities that can support HR1 community engagement requirements, including schedules, capacity, locations, and available hours.
  • Partner with YMCA centers to identify and develop volunteer opportunities and support registration, screening, background clearance, orientation, and onboarding.
  • Maintain communication with centers regarding volunteer capacity, placements, scheduling, and barriers that may prevent individuals from completing required hours.
  • Conduct proactive outreach through community events, resource fairs, schools, partner organizations, YMCA centers, and other trusted community spaces to reach populations impacted by HR1.
  • Educate community members on HR1 policy changes, community engagement requirements, potential impacts, required actions, and available YMCA support.
  • Stay informed of HR1 policy and implementation updates and share accurate, current information with YMCA centers, partners, and community members.
  • Connect individuals to CES enrollment and renewal assistance and additional YMCA programs and resources as needed.
  • Build relationships with community organizations and regional partners to strengthen HR1 outreach, referrals, and awareness of YMCA volunteer opportunities.
  • Track volunteer referrals, placements, service hours, outreach activities, and other program data to support reporting and follow-up.
  • Identify barriers, emerging community needs, and gaps in volunteer capacity and work with centers and program leadership to develop solutions.
  • Funding Contingent Position: Continued employment is contingent upon the availability of program funding, ongoing program needs, and satisfactory job performance. Funding beyond the current funding period is not guaranteed.

YMCA LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES

The Y’s Leadership Competency Model is comprised of multiple leadership competencies (leadership knowledge, skills, and behaviors required for success in the Y), organized by the four disciplines of cause driven leadership:

  • Advancing Our Mission & Cause: Provide visionary leadership to the organization and ensure that all resources are mobilized to adapt to new challenges and needs in the community.
    • Competencies Include: Change Leadership, Engaging Community, Philanthropy, & Volunteerism
  • Building Relationships: Connect people to the Y’s cause by developing inclusive relationships, partnerships and collaborations so that Ys can co-create solutions to pressing social needs.
    • Competencies Include: Collaboration, Communication & Influence, Inclusion
  • Leading Operations: ensure relevance, effectiveness, and sustainability of the organization so that we can continue to fulfill our promise to the community.
    • Competencies Include: Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Fiscal Management, Functional Expertise, Innovation, Program/Project Management
  • Developing & Inspiring Others: support the holistic development of self and others so that everyone can embrace the Y’s cause, sustain the Y’s culture, and inspire others to take individual and collective action to further our impact.
    • Competencies Include: Developing Self & Others, Emotional Maturity

While all competencies are significant the following are critical to success in this position:

  • Engaging Community: Builds relationships with YMCA centers, community members, and trusted community partners to expand outreach, connect individuals impacted by HR1 policy changes to volunteer opportunities, and increase access to YMCA resources and support.
  • Volunteerism: Connects community members impacted by HR1 community engagement requirements to meaningful YMCA volunteer opportunities and supports them through the placement and onboarding process.
  • Collaboration: Works closely with YMCA center staff, Certified Enrollment Specialists, community partners, and the Civic Engagement team to coordinate volunteer placements, outreach, and effective program implementation.

*This position is grant funded, and continued employment is contingent upon the availability and renewal of funding and compliance with grant requirements. Positions may be modified or eliminated if funding is reduced, discontinued, or not renewed.*

title: WMS & Business Systems Analyst (Exp in Warehousing/Logistics Co.)/East!
description:

title: Software Developer for Test Framework (Python)
description:
Are you a Python programmer? Are you driven by system-level challenges? Join the Software Test Solutions at Westermo as a Software Developer!

Are you our next Software Developer?

Software Test Solutions develops our in-house test framework, which is used to test our products, and plays a critical role in ensuring product quality and reliability. Many teams rely on the accuracy of our test results, which makes our work essential for validating our products against their specifications.

We are looking for a software developer who thrives in an agile environment and wants to be part of a team that builds and maintains this framework and its tools. The framework is used for system-level testing of our products in network solutions, running on dedicated test systems.

Our department is made up of two teams: the Test Framework team (the role described here), which schedules and runs tests, processes the test results and maintains the test systems, and the Test Developer team, which develops and maintains tests for our operating system WeOS. We promote close collaboration between the two teams, so your work won't necessarily stay limited to the framework – there's plenty of room to explore and contribute across both.

In your role, you will be:

  • Programming primarily in Python (and Go), working with tools such as Docker and Kubernetes.

  • Analysing test results and troubleshooting and refining the framework to keep it reliable.

  • Maintaining and developing the test systems, with the devices under test, that the framework relies on.

  • Extending the framework to support new WeOS functionality.

  • Developing the next generation of our test framework to meet future demands on scalability, including virtual testing, and reduced complexity for end users.

  • Working with both front-end and back-end development of the web interfaces for configuration and visualization of test results.

We think about automation in everything we do, and we are always trying out new technologies that help us meet current and future demands. We use Jira for planning and tracking work, and keep improving our Agile methods. AI is also a natural part of our daily software work, and we are exploring how to put it to even better use.

So, who are we looking for?

You have an academic background in computer science or similar, and you’re motivated by solving real problems with smart solutions. We value teamwork, and hope you do, too. You enjoy both technical development and team collaboration, and you share your knowledge just as readily as you ask for help. You are curious and innovative, comfortable in an agile environment, and like to try, test, and learn with colleagues.

Further, we want you to be:

  • Experienced in Python development and eager to deepen your skills.

  • Comfortable working in a Linux environment.

  • Familiar with software engineering tools such as source code management, CI/CD, containers, and web development (front-end and/or back-end).

  • Interested in networking technologies.

  • Fluent in English and Swedish.

Oh, and don't worry, if you're not an expert in all the things described – you'll learn.

In return, we offer: You will be working at the forefront of technology in a friendly, open culture where you get the opportunity to learn from skilled colleagues every day. A mature and caring leadership in a flat organization. Through our collective bargain agreement you will be covered in terms of insurance, pension and other benefits. We like to have fun together and we regularly enjoy sports and other social activities as a team. We believe that magic happens when people meet. We are a learning organization and we truly love to try new things, think outside the box and be innovative together!

Basic information:

  • Location: Kopparlunden, Västerås

  • Job type: Full time

  • Employment contract: Permanent

Don’t miss out on this opportunity – apply today! We look forward to meeting you!

For further information please contact:

Hiring Manager: Alexander Falk at alexander.falk@westermo.com

Recruiter: Elin Sandell at elin.sandell@westermo.com

About Westermo:

Welcome to a rapidly growing international company, thriving at the forefront of cutting edge technology. Westermo develops and manufactures advanced devices for industrial data communication, used in mission-critical installations and harsh industrial environments. The very robust and secure communication networks built with our products provide a high value for our customers.

We are focused on leveraging growth opportunities in our market and are devoted to delivering the world's best industrial networks. This is achieved through a very dynamic work environment where teamwork and loyalty are valued. Strong and honest relationships with colleagues, customers, and suppliers are important to us. We have an open culture where we share knowledge, learn from one another and explore new ideas, allowing us to constantly improve.

Westermo is a leading provider of Industrial Data Communications equipment to the global market. Sales are conducted through our own offices in key markets in Europe, North America, Australia and Asia, as well as through distributors and OEM customers worldwide. Development and manufacturing take place in Sweden, Ireland, Germany and Switzerland. Westermo was founded in 1975 and today has over 580 employees with a turnover of around 1.4 Billion SEK. The company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Ependion, listed on the Nasdaq OMX Nordic stock exchange.

title: Regional Program Specialist (5343)
location: Stuart M Ketchum Downtown YMCA - Los Angeles, CA 90071
description:
YMCA OF METROPOLITAN LOS ANGELES

The LA Y is the Center for Community Well-Being in Los Angeles, committed to building stronger communities by providing equitable programs and services to empower all. We are focused on fighting food insecurity, providing equity in education, making sure every child has the opportunity to experience the joy of sports, ensuring kids and teens have a safe place to grow, learn and live a healthy lifestyle. The LA Y’s health and wellness initiatives offer medical and mental health resources to ensure everyone has access to basic health needs. Our mission is to provide services and resources that contribute to the well-being of our community. The LA Y operates 29 Centers and over 200 program sites across LA County.

*This position is grant funded, and continued employment is contingent upon the availability and renewal of funding and compliance with grant requirements. Positions may be modified or eliminated if funding is reduced, discontinued, or not renewed.*

POSITION SUMMARY

  • Connect community members impacted by HR1 policy changes and new community engagement requirements to YMCA volunteer opportunities where they can complete required hours and support continued benefit eligibility.
  • Match individuals with appropriate YMCA volunteer opportunities based on required hours, location, availability, interests, and ability to participate.
  • Guide community members through the volunteer placement process, including identifying opportunities, completing onboarding, and preparing to begin service.
  • Work closely with Certified Enrollment Specialists (CES) to receive referrals and connect individuals who need volunteer hours to meet HR1 requirements with available YMCA placements.
  • Maintain an up-to-date pipeline of YMCA volunteer opportunities that can support HR1 community engagement requirements, including schedules, capacity, locations, and available hours.
  • Partner with YMCA centers to identify and develop volunteer opportunities and support registration, screening, background clearance, orientation, and onboarding.
  • Maintain communication with centers regarding volunteer capacity, placements, scheduling, and barriers that may prevent individuals from completing required hours.
  • Conduct proactive outreach through community events, resource fairs, schools, partner organizations, YMCA centers, and other trusted community spaces to reach populations impacted by HR1.
  • Educate community members on HR1 policy changes, community engagement requirements, potential impacts, required actions, and available YMCA support.
  • Stay informed of HR1 policy and implementation updates and share accurate, current information with YMCA centers, partners, and community members.
  • Connect individuals to CES enrollment and renewal assistance and additional YMCA programs and resources as needed.
  • Build relationships with community organizations and regional partners to strengthen HR1 outreach, referrals, and awareness of YMCA volunteer opportunities.
  • Track volunteer referrals, placements, service hours, outreach activities, and other program data to support reporting and follow-up.
  • Identify barriers, emerging community needs, and gaps in volunteer capacity and work with centers and program leadership to develop solutions.
  • Funding Contingent Position: Continued employment is contingent upon the availability of program funding, ongoing program needs, and satisfactory job performance. Funding beyond the current funding period is not guaranteed.

YMCA LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES

The Y’s Leadership Competency Model is comprised of multiple leadership competencies (leadership knowledge, skills, and behaviors required for success in the Y), organized by the four disciplines of cause driven leadership:

  • Advancing Our Mission & Cause: Provide visionary leadership to the organization and ensure that all resources are mobilized to adapt to new challenges and needs in the community.
    • Competencies Include: Change Leadership, Engaging Community, Philanthropy, & Volunteerism
  • Building Relationships: Connect people to the Y’s cause by developing inclusive relationships, partnerships and collaborations so that Ys can co-create solutions to pressing social needs.
    • Competencies Include: Collaboration, Communication & Influence, Inclusion
  • Leading Operations: ensure relevance, effectiveness, and sustainability of the organization so that we can continue to fulfill our promise to the community.
    • Competencies Include: Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Fiscal Management, Functional Expertise, Innovation, Program/Project Management
  • Developing & Inspiring Others: support the holistic development of self and others so that everyone can embrace the Y’s cause, sustain the Y’s culture, and inspire others to take individual and collective action to further our impact.
    • Competencies Include: Developing Self & Others, Emotional Maturity

While all competencies are significant the following are critical to success in this position:

  • Engaging Community: Builds relationships with YMCA centers, community members, and trusted community partners to expand outreach, connect individuals impacted by HR1 policy changes to volunteer opportunities, and increase access to YMCA resources and support.
  • Volunteerism: Connects community members impacted by HR1 community engagement requirements to meaningful YMCA volunteer opportunities and supports them through the placement and onboarding process.
  • Collaboration: Works closely with YMCA center staff, Certified Enrollment Specialists, community partners, and the Civic Engagement team to coordinate volunteer placements, outreach, and effective program implementation.

*This position is grant funded, and continued employment is contingent upon the availability and renewal of funding and compliance with grant requirements. Positions may be modified or eliminated if funding is reduced, discontinued, or not renewed.*

title: Project Coordinator-Supervisor
description:
Job Overview

Performs administrative and operational duties associated with coordinating assigned projects and related activities within a department.

Starting Salary $55,099- $67,225/ yearly

Ideal Candidate

The Project Coordinator Supervisor performs administrative and operational duties associated with coordinating assigned projects, work activities, and related functions within the Infrastructure Maintenance Division of the Water Resources Department. This is an in‑office working supervisory and operational coordination position. It is not a project management or construction project manager role.

The ideal candidate will also bring strong administrative and supervisory experience. Responsibilities include employee payroll and timekeeping oversight, recruitment and onboarding support, training coordination, records management, purchasing and requisition support, document preparation, data‑quality review, and other division‑level administrative functions. The Supervisor ensures consistent administrative processes and may contribute to procedure development or process improvements.

Strong leadership, communication, and customer‑service skills are essential. The ideal candidate sets clear expectations, supports employee development, communicates effectively with field personnel and leadership, resolves routine workflow issues, and exercises discretion when handling sensitive employee, payroll, financial, or operational information.

The ideal candidate is a highly organized, service‑oriented supervisor with experience supporting daily maintenance operations in a utility, field service, facilities, or similarly complex operational environment. The Supervisor oversees Project Coordinators who operate in a call center environment dispatching service calls, assigning work orders, and monitoring them through completion. The PCS will be responsible for handling call escalations and, during emergencies or staffing shortages, may be required to assist directly with call intake and dispatch functions.

The Supervisor ensures that Project Coordinators effectively review work requirements, prioritize assignments, coordinate labor, materials, equipment, and parts, and support daily and emergency operations for teams such as Meter Maintenance, Preventive Maintenance, and other infrastructure maintenance workgroups. This role requires sound judgment, attention to operational priorities, and the ability to adjust schedules when emergencies, staffing changes, material availability, or competing service needs affect planned work.

The successful candidate will be proficient with work management systems, databases, scheduling and timekeeping applications, document‑management platforms, and standard office software. Experience improving administrative or operational processes, maintaining accurate records, and using work‑order information to support operational decisions is highly desirable. The preferred candidate is adaptable, accountable, detail‑oriented, and committed to safety, regulatory compliance, reliable utility service, continuous improvement, and public service.

Core Competencies

  • Customer Commitment - Proactively seeks to understand the needs of the customers and provide the highest standards of service.
  • Dedication to Professionalism and Integrity - Demonstrates and promotes fair, honest, professional and ethical behaviors that establishes trust throughout the organization and with the public we serve.
  • Organizational Excellence - Takes ownership for excellence through one's personal effectiveness and dedication to the continuous improvement of our operations.
  • Success through Teamwork - Collaborates and builds partnerships through trust and the open exchange of diverse ideas and perspectives to achieve organizational goals.

Duties and Responsibilities

Note: The following duties are illustrative and not exhaustive. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position. Depending on assigned area of responsibility, incumbents in the position may perform one or more of the activities described below.

  • Performs project management work by coordinating small to moderate projects or elements of larger complex projects.
  • Directs and coordinates activities concerned with the implementation and completion of assigned projects.
  • Prepares or assists in the preparation of contract drafts, requests for proposal, and other related documents for review.
  • Manages project operations to ensure adherence to project plans and schedules.
  • Identifies, tracks, monitors and communicates project-related tasks, issues, scope changes, variances and contingencies that may arise during the project.
  • Monitors project budget, monitors status of allocated funds and controls expenses.
  • Prepares reports and maintains project documentation.
  • Performs other related duties as required.

Job Specifications

  • Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management.
  • Knowledge of the processes, activities, requirements and objectives of the functional area to which assigned.
  • Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and solve problems involving several variables or unique situations.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relations with others within and outside own organization.
  • Ability to manage the details of projects, track activities and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to collect, organize and analyze data and make logical decisions.

Physical Requirements

  • While performing duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear.
  • This position is primarily sedentary.

Work Category

  • Light work - Exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects. If the use of arm and/or leg control requires exertion of forces greater than that of sedentary work and if the worker sits most of the time, the job is considered light work.

​​​​​​​Minimum Qualifications Required

  • Graduation from an accredited four-year degree granting college or university; AND
  • One year of experience managing projects, programs or activities; OR
  • An equivalent combination of education (not less than possession of a High School diploma/GED), training and experience that would reasonably be expected to provide the job-related competencies noted above.

​​​​​​​Emergency Management Responsibilities

In the event of an emergency or disaster, an employee may be required to respond promptly to duties and responsibilities as assigned by the employee’s department, the County’s Office of Emergency Management, or County Administration. Such assignments may be for before, during or after the emergency/disaster.

Additional Job Requirements

A department, depending on the nature of its mission and operations, may require that employees in all or certain positions in this job classification:

  1. Maintain the ability to pass the background checks required for the position. These background checks may include but are not limited to:
  • Criminal History Background Check using Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS)
  • Level 1 and Level 2 Background screening (Ch. 435 Florida Statutes)
  • Child Abuse, Abandonment and Neglect Record Check using the State Automated Child Welfare Information System (SACWIS)

  1. Possess the necessary job-related license(s) or certification(s) that may include possession of a Florida Driver License (Class E) or an applicable Commercial Driver License (CDL)

title: RESOURCE CONSERVATIONIST
description:
Department: Conservation District

Job Title: Resource Conservationist

Starting Rate: $20.26 per hour

Dauphin County Conservation District is currently accepting applications for the full-time position of Resource Conservationist. The objective of the individual within this position is to administer the Erosion and Sediment Pollution Control (ESPC) and the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permitting program for the discharge of storm water associated with construction activities in accordance with the related delegation agreement with the PA Department of Environmental Protection (DEP).

The individual in this position is responsible for but not limited to performing the following essential functions: reviews ESPC plan and related NPDES permit applications in a fair and equitable manner to determine adequacy of content in accordance with program manual, checklists guidance documents and DEP training; completes ESPC plan technical reviews and NPDES administrative reviews in a timely manner that is in accordance with current program standards and requirements; keeps the program supervisor informed of project timelines that are not meeting standards and requirements; maintains all program-related files, charts and project documentation up-to-date and in an organized manner for timely retrieval of information.

He/she also performs the following essential duties: conducts site inspections where earth disturbance is occurring to meet permit requirements and as needed to verify that construction is proceeding in conformance with approved plans; and completes and distributes inspection reports for sites with severe or major violations within two (2) business days with attention to accuracy and detail as may be required for future enforcement actions; investigates field complaints within established program timelines; properly documents the findings of the investigation and to the extent practical moves the complaint toward resolution within either our program or another agency's requirements.

He/she performs a few other critical essential key functions which include: developing and conducting a minimum of two (2) educational programs for contractors, consultants, developers or municipal officials to keep them current in applicable aspect of program administration; initiates enforcement actions when voluntary compliance efforts fail or blatant violation of environmental laws has occurred; always conducts all activities and actions in a professional manner for all key essential functions; and performs all other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, AND TRAINING REQUIREMENTS:

  • Bachelor's degree in agronomy, engineering or related natural resource field or such practical experience as required to develop a technical knowledge of this work.
  • Computer training and valid PA driver's license required.
  • Experience in the preparation or reading of site plans and construction plans or the preparation of surveying documents is preferred.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF JOB:

1 . Reviews ESPC plan and related NPDES permit applications in a fair and equitable manner to determine

adequacy of content in accordance with program manual, checklists guidance documents and DEP

training.

2 . Completes ESPC plan technical reviews and NP DES administrative reviews in a timely manner that is in

accordance with current program standards and requirements; keeps the program supervisor informed of

project timelines that are not meeting standards and requirements.

3 . Maintains all program related files, charts and project documentation up-to-date and in an organized

manner that permits accurate and timely retrieval of information.

4 . Conducts site inspections where earth disturbance is occurring to meet permit requirements and as

needed to verify that construction is proceeding in conformance with approved plans.

5. Completes and distributes inspection reports for sites with severe or major violations within 2 business

days.

6. Completes inspection reports with attention to accuracy and detail as may be required for future

enforcement actions.

7. Investigates field complaints within established program timelines; properly documents the findings of the

investigation and to the extent practical moves the complaint toward resolution within our program

requirements or by another agency.

8 . Develops and conducts a minimum of 2 educational programs for contractors, consultants, developers or

municipal officials to keep them current in applicable aspect of program administration.

9. Initiates enforcement actions when voluntary compliance efforts fail or blatant violation of environmental

laws has occurred.

10 . Conducts all activities and actions in a professional manner.

OTHER DUTIES OF JOB:

1 .Attends meetings, training and in-services as required.

2 . Performs other job-related duties as required.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED:

1 . Receives occasional instruction and supervision from the program oversight supervisor in regard to daily

work duties.

SUPERVISION GIVEN:

1. None.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

1 . Works indoors in adequate workspace, lighting, temperatures and ventilation.

2 . Works with average indoor exposure to noise, stress and disruptions.

3 . Normal indoor exposure to dust/dirt.

4 . Subject to working outdoors at work sites and being subjected to heavy and/or dangerous equipment,

poor water, odors and natural elements.

5. Travels to work sites or other locations as required.

KNOWLEDGE. SKILLS AND ABILITIES REQUIRED:

1 . Must be able to speak and understand the English language in an understandable manner in order to

carry out essential job duties.

2 . Must possess effective communication skills.

3 . Must possess initiative and problem-solving skills in relation to environmental projects.

4 . Must possess ability to function independently, organize efficient work schedules, have flexibility and the

ability to work effectively with clients, co-workers and others.

5 . Must possess the technical knowledge of operating personal computers.

6 . Must possess the ability to deal with and resolve volatile situations.

7. Must possess a valid PA driver's license and a willingness to travel as needed to perform field

inspections and other projects.

8 . Must possess the ability to make independent decisions within stipulated bounds when circumstances

warrant such action.

9 . Must possess ability to work on large projects and to interact effectively with DEP and County officials.

10 . Must possess a thorough knowledge of engineering skills, practice and methods needed to carry out

quality environmental conservation programs.

11 . Must be able to traverse all kinds of outdoor terrain.

12 . Must possess a knowledge and appreciation of natural resources.

13 . Must be able to present factual information and documentation of site conditions where enforcement

actions are present.

PHYSICAL/MENTAL CONDITIONS:

1 . Must possess the ability to record, convey and present information, explain procedures and follow

instructions.

2 . Must be able to sit, stand, walk and drive intermittently throughout the workday, with occasional kneeling,

twisting, stooping, bending, climbing necessary to carry out work duties.

3 . Dexterity requirements range from simple coordinated movements of fingers/hands; feet/legs; torso

necessary to carry out duties of job.

4 . Sedentary work, with occasional lifting/carrying of objects with a maximum weight of ten pounds.

5 . Must be able to move frequently throughout the workday.

6 . Must be able to pay close attention to details and concentrate on work.

7 . Must be able to cope with the physical and mental stress of the position.

8 . Must be able to walk significant distances, over irregular terrain and traverse steep slopes in adverse weather conditions.

title: Director of Program Compliance and Reporting (5344)
location: Stuart M Ketchum Downtown YMCA - Los Angeles, CA 90071
description:
YMCA OF METROPOLITAN LOS ANGELES

The LA Y is the Center for Community Well-Being in Los Angeles, committed to building stronger communities by providing equitable programs and services to empower all. We are focused on fighting food insecurity, providing equity in education, making sure every child has the opportunity to experience the joy of sports, ensuring kids and teens have a safe place to grow, learn and live a healthy lifestyle. The LA Y’s health and wellness initiatives offer medical and mental health resources to ensure everyone has access to basic health needs. Our mission is to provide services and resources that contribute to the well-being of our community. The LA Y operates 29 Centers and over 200 program sites across LA County.

*This position is grant funded, and continued employment is contingent upon the availability and renewal of funding and compliance with grant requirements. Positions may be modified or eliminated if funding is reduced, discontinued, or not renewed.*

POSITION SUMMARY

  • Report to the Senior Director of Civic Engagement and provide ongoing updates on program performance, funding requirements, reporting deadlines, compliance needs, risks, and emerging issues.
  • Lead compliance, reporting, and funding accountability for the YMCA’s HR1 community response, ensuring program activities align with funding agreements, contracts, organizational policies, and applicable requirements.
  • Manage monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting to funders, County partners, and other stakeholders, ensuring reports are accurate, complete, and submitted on time.
  • Work closely with the HR1 program team, including Certified Enrollment Specialists (CES) and Regional Program Coordinators, to collect, review, and validate program data required for funder, County, and internal reporting.
  • Establish clear data collection, documentation, and reporting processes for HR1 program staff and provide ongoing guidance to ensure consistent and accurate reporting across locations.
  • Develop and manage surveys, data collection tools, and feedback processes to capture participant outcomes, community needs, program impact, and other information required for funder reporting and program evaluation.
  • Track and analyze program performance, including applications, enrollments, renewals, outreach, referrals, volunteer placements, service hours, and other required program outcomes.
  • Monitor funding agreements, contracts, deliverables, performance measures, reporting deadlines, and documentation requirements to ensure program commitments are met.
  • Develop and maintain reporting systems, dashboards, documentation standards, and internal processes to support program oversight and funder accountability.
  • Review program data for accuracy, completeness, trends, and discrepancies and work directly with HR1 program staff to address reporting or documentation gaps.
  • Serve as a key liaison with funders, County agencies, and external partners regarding funding agreements, reporting requirements, program performance, data, and documentation.
  • Coordinate across Civic Engagement, Finance, Legal, Risk Management, IT, and other internal departments to support funding compliance and effective program implementation.
  • Ensure appropriate collection, storage, access, and handling of sensitive participant and program information in accordance with privacy, confidentiality, and organizational requirements.
  • Develop and maintain compliance procedures, documentation protocols, staff guidance, and training related to data collection, confidentiality, reporting, and funding requirements.
  • Monitor HR1 implementation, funder requirements, County guidance, and other relevant updates and communicate operational impacts to the Senior Director and HR1 program team.
  • Support audits, monitoring visits, funder reviews, contract renewals, and requests program documentation, financial information, or performance data.
  • Prepare reports, dashboards, summaries, and recommendations for the Senior Director of Civic Engagement and organizational leadership to support program oversight and decision-making.
  • Identify reporting gaps, compliance risks, contractual concerns, and operational challenges and coordinate with program staff and appropriate stakeholders to develop solutions.
  • Maintain organized records of funding agreements, contracts, reports, policies, program documentation, and other required records.
  • Support additional cross-functional projects related to funding, reporting, data management, compliance, and overall HR1 program implementation.
  • Funding Contingent Position: Continued employment is contingent upon the availability of program funding, ongoing program needs, and satisfactory job performance. Funding beyond the current funding period is not guaranteed.

YMCA LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES

The Y’s Leadership Competency Model is comprised of multiple leadership competencies (leadership knowledge, skills, and behaviors required for success in the Y), organized by the four disciplines of cause driven leadership:

  • Advancing Our Mission & Cause: Provide visionary leadership to the organization and ensure that all resources are mobilized to adapt to new challenges and needs in the community.
    • Competencies Include: Change Leadership, Engaging Community, Philanthropy, & Volunteerism
  • Building Relationships: Connect people to the Y’s cause by developing inclusive relationships, partnerships and collaborations so that Ys can co-create solutions to pressing social needs.
    • Competencies Include: Collaboration, Communication & Influence, Inclusion
  • Leading Operations: ensure relevance, effectiveness, and sustainability of the organization so that we can continue to fulfill our promise to the community.
    • Competencies Include: Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Fiscal Management, Functional Expertise, Innovation, Program/Project Management
  • Developing & Inspiring Others: support the holistic development of self and others so that everyone can embrace the Y’s cause, sustain the Y’s culture, and inspire others to take individual and collective action to further our impact.
    • Competencies Include: Developing Self & Others, Emotional Maturity

While all competencies are significant the following are critical to success in this position:

  • Engaging Community: Builds relationships with YMCA centers, community members, and trusted community partners to expand outreach, connect individuals impacted by HR1 policy changes to volunteer opportunities, and increase access to YMCA resources and support.
  • Volunteerism: Connects community members impacted by HR1 community engagement requirements to meaningful YMCA volunteer opportunities and supports them through the placement and onboarding process.
  • Collaboration: Works closely with YMCA center staff, Certified Enrollment Specialists, community partners, and the Civic Engagement team to coordinate volunteer placements, outreach, and effective program implementation.

*This position is grant funded, and continued employment is contingent upon the availability and renewal of funding and compliance with grant requirements. Positions may be modified or eliminated if funding is reduced, discontinued, or not renewed.*

Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

MITRE’s Mission Engineering and System of Systems Engineering department within the Systems Engineering Technical Division is seeking driven, technically exceptional Lead Mission Systems Engineers to support various sponsor across the national security sector such as Department of War, Intelligence Community as well as the public sector to include DHS, HHS, and more. The candidates will support activities such as mission engineering, system of systems analysis, experimentation, and decision-support activities for complex operational missions.

Apply modeling, simulation, experimentation, sensitivity analysis, and comparative assessments to evaluate baseline and alternative mission approaches, system of systems performance, risks, and mission impacts.

Experience supporting defense, aerospace, intelligence, national security, or other mission-critical technical programs.

  • Ability to analyze complex missions, operational scenarios, system dependencies, system of systems interactions, or capability gaps.

  • Must have an active Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance and must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.

title: Senior DevSecOps Engineer
description:
Azqore, a next-generation provider of Information Systems and banking operations services, is a subsidiary of Indosuez Wealth Management, the wealth management arm of the Crédit Agricole Group. As a global company, Azqore is committed to providing wealth managers with integrated, turnkey digital solutions.

With its headquarters in Switzerland and its Asia hub in Singapore, Azqore currently serves around thirty clients through its proprietary S2i platform, supporting approximately CHF 200 billion in assets under management.

At the heart of our strategy, we are looking for a Senior DevSecOps Engineer in charge of design, build and industrialise security controls across the software development lifecycle and CI/CD supply chain. The engineer will create secure-by-default delivery patterns, integrate automated controls into GitLab pipelines, establish actionable vulnerability workflows and help application and platform teams adopt the controls at scale.

👨‍🔧 Your responsibilities

  • DevSecOps framework and governance - Assess the current delivery landscape; contribute to and implement the agreed DevSecOps control framework, ownership model and exception process across IWM / Azqore.

  • Risk-based security gates and vulnerability management - Create ownership, SLAs, triage, remediation, exception expiry and evidence workflows. Ensure findings become actionable work rather than dashboard-only alerts.

  • Secure CI/CD engineering - Design and maintain reusable GitLab CI/CD templates and golden pipelines (approved, reusable CI/CD templates) with protected branches, approvals, controlled runners, signed or trusted components and secure deployment patterns.

  • Automated security testing - Integrate and tune SAST, SCA, secret detection, IaC scanning, container-image scanning and, where applicable, DAST. Define risk-based blocking thresholds and prevent excessive false positives.

  • Software supply-chain security - Establish artefact governance, SBOM generation and retention, image provenance, trusted base images and lifecycle controls for Nexus and internal registries.

  • Infrastructure as Code - Secure Terraform and Ansible workflows, including module review, policy checks, secret handling and promotion between environments.

  • Secrets and identities - Promote no-secrets-in-repositories patterns and integrate HashiCorp Vault, workload identities, tokens and least-privilege service access into delivery workflows.

  • Enablement - Coach development and platform teams, contribute to Security Champion activities, publish practical standards and support pilot teams through adoption.

  • Metrics and assurance - Produce coverage, failure, remediation and exception KPIs; ensure evidence is available for management, risk, audit and regulatory reviews.

  • Operational improvement - Support incident analysis and recurring control failures; automate repetitive checks and progressively transfer mature capabilities into an agreed Run model.

🧙‍♂️ Your core competencies

  • Bachelor Degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science or equivalent

  • Minimum 8 years delivery and hands-on security experience with:

    1. GitLab CI/CD pipeline engineering and reusable component design.

    2. Practical implementation of SAST, SCA, secret, IaC and container scanning.

    3. Terraform and scripting in Python, Bash or PowerShell.

    4. Vulnerability triage, remediation workflows and risk-based security gates.

    5. Artefact repository, container registry and dependency governance.

    6. Solid application-security fundamentals.

    7. Ability to design controls that developers can adopt without bypassing them.

  • Proven achievements as a hands-on architect-builder who can turn an incomplete requirement into a clear security design, working implementation, evidence, documentation and an operational handover.

  • Keen to roll up sleeve and do beyond advisory work but also involved in deployment and production support work.

  • Understands availability, recoverability, change control, audit evidence, operational ownership and supportability.

  • You are autonomous, tenacious and rigorous. Boredom won't be part of your day, but you need to know how to organize yourself to manage the multiple issues underway.

title: Director of Program Compliance and Reporting
company: YOUNG MENS CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION OF METROPOLITAN LOS ANGELES
description:
YMCA OF METROPOLITAN LOS ANGELES

The LA Y is the Center for Community Well-Being in Los Angeles, committed to building stronger communities by providing equitable programs and services to empower all. We are focused on fighting food insecurity, providing equity in education, making sure every child has the opportunity to experience the joy of sports, ensuring kids and teens have a safe place to grow, learn and live a healthy lifestyle. The LA Y’s health and wellness initiatives offer medical and mental health resources to ensure everyone has access to basic health needs. Our mission is to provide services and resources that contribute to the well-being of our community. The LA Y operates 29 Centers and over 200 program sites across LA County.

*This position is grant funded, and continued employment is contingent upon the availability and renewal of funding and compliance with grant requirements. Positions may be modified or eliminated if funding is reduced, discontinued, or not renewed.*

POSITION SUMMARY

  • Report to the Senior Director of Civic Engagement and provide ongoing updates on program performance, funding requirements, reporting deadlines, compliance needs, risks, and emerging issues.
  • Lead compliance, reporting, and funding accountability for the YMCA’s HR1 community response, ensuring program activities align with funding agreements, contracts, organizational policies, and applicable requirements.
  • Manage monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting to funders, County partners, and other stakeholders, ensuring reports are accurate, complete, and submitted on time.
  • Work closely with the HR1 program team, including Certified Enrollment Specialists (CES) and Regional Program Coordinators, to collect, review, and validate program data required for funder, County, and internal reporting.
  • Establish clear data collection, documentation, and reporting processes for HR1 program staff and provide ongoing guidance to ensure consistent and accurate reporting across locations.
  • Develop and manage surveys, data collection tools, and feedback processes to capture participant outcomes, community needs, program impact, and other information required for funder reporting and program evaluation.
  • Track and analyze program performance, including applications, enrollments, renewals, outreach, referrals, volunteer placements, service hours, and other required program outcomes.
  • Monitor funding agreements, contracts, deliverables, performance measures, reporting deadlines, and documentation requirements to ensure program commitments are met.
  • Develop and maintain reporting systems, dashboards, documentation standards, and internal processes to support program oversight and funder accountability.
  • Review program data for accuracy, completeness, trends, and discrepancies and work directly with HR1 program staff to address reporting or documentation gaps.
  • Serve as a key liaison with funders, County agencies, and external partners regarding funding agreements, reporting requirements, program performance, data, and documentation.
  • Coordinate across Civic Engagement, Finance, Legal, Risk Management, IT, and other internal departments to support funding compliance and effective program implementation.
  • Ensure appropriate collection, storage, access, and handling of sensitive participant and program information in accordance with privacy, confidentiality, and organizational requirements.
  • Develop and maintain compliance procedures, documentation protocols, staff guidance, and training related to data collection, confidentiality, reporting, and funding requirements.
  • Monitor HR1 implementation, funder requirements, County guidance, and other relevant updates and communicate operational impacts to the Senior Director and HR1 program team.
  • Support audits, monitoring visits, funder reviews, contract renewals, and requests program documentation, financial information, or performance data.
  • Prepare reports, dashboards, summaries, and recommendations for the Senior Director of Civic Engagement and organizational leadership to support program oversight and decision-making.
  • Identify reporting gaps, compliance risks, contractual concerns, and operational challenges and coordinate with program staff and appropriate stakeholders to develop solutions.
  • Maintain organized records of funding agreements, contracts, reports, policies, program documentation, and other required records.
  • Support additional cross-functional projects related to funding, reporting, data management, compliance, and overall HR1 program implementation.
  • Funding Contingent Position: Continued employment is contingent upon the availability of program funding, ongoing program needs, and satisfactory job performance. Funding beyond the current funding period is not guaranteed.

YMCA LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES

The Y’s Leadership Competency Model is comprised of multiple leadership competencies (leadership knowledge, skills, and behaviors required for success in the Y), organized by the four disciplines of cause driven leadership:

  • Advancing Our Mission & Cause: Provide visionary leadership to the organization and ensure that all resources are mobilized to adapt to new challenges and needs in the community.

While all competencies are significant the following are critical to success in this position:

  • Engaging Community: Builds relationships with YMCA centers, community members, and trusted community partners to expand outreach, connect individuals impacted by HR1 policy changes to volunteer opportunities, and increase access to YMCA resources and support.

title: USP GMP Scientist/ Biotechnologist
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION


USP GMP Scientist/ Biotechnologist

Position summary

The USP GMP Biotechnologist performs hands-on upstream manufacturing activities for mammalian or microbial cell culture processes in a GMP-regulated CDMO environment. The role is primarily responsible for safe, compliant, and timely execution of seed train, bioreactor, harvest, equipment preparation, cleaning, and documentation activities. Strong practical GMP manufacturing experience is essential. Experience supporting cell line generation or cell line development is beneficial but is not required.

Position responsibilities

  • Execute upstream GMP manufacturing operations according to approved batch records, SOPs, work instructions, and production schedules.

  • Perform cell culture operations, including cell thaw, shake-flask expansion, seed train execution, inoculation, bioreactor operation, sampling, monitoring, and harvest.

  • Prepare media, feeds, buffers, reagents, and process solutions; complete required calculations, labels, status controls, and documentation.

  • Set up, operate, clean, and perform routine checks of upstream equipment such as biosafety cabinets, incubators, cell counters, pumps, balances, single-use bioreactors, controllers, and harvest systems.

  • Perform aseptic manipulations and closed or functionally closed processing using qualified techniques in controlled GMP areas.

  • Complete batch records, logbooks, forms, and electronic records accurately and contemporaneously in accordance with GDP and ALCOA+ principles.

  • Perform equipment and room preparation, line clearance, material staging, component verification, cleaning, disinfection, and post-operation closeout.

  • Follow gowning, environmental monitoring, contamination-control, biosafety, waste-handling, and controlled-area behavior requirements.

  • Monitor critical process parameters and cell culture performance, including viable cell density, viability, metabolites, pH, dissolved oxygen, temperature, agitation, gas flow, and process alarms.

  • Immediately escalate deviations, atypical observations, equipment issues, contamination risks, and documentation errors; support investigations and CAPA implementation as assigned.

  • Support material inventory, consumable readiness, equipment status tracking, and GMP suite scheduling to maintain manufacturing readiness.

  • Participate in shift handoffs, daily production meetings, pre-run readiness reviews, and cross-functional coordination with Manufacturing, QA, QC, MS&T/Process Development, Facilities, and Warehouse teams.

  • Support technology transfer, engineering runs, process qualification, and continuous-improvement activities under appropriate guidance.

  • Assist with training of new personnel after qualification and demonstrate consistent adherence to safety, quality, and data-integrity expectations.

  • When business needs require, support non-GMP upstream or cell line development activities such as routine cell culture, transfection support, clone handling, screening, or cell banking.

Position requirements

  • BS in Biotechnology, Biology, Biochemistry, Biochemical/Chemical Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Typically 6+ years of hands-on biopharmaceutical manufacturing experience, including at least 2 year working directly in a GMP-regulated manufacturing environment. Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.

  • Demonstrated experience executing GMP batch records and SOPs, including contemporaneous documentation, corrections, review, and adherence to Good Documentation Practices.

  • Hands-on experience with cell culture and upstream operations such as seed train expansion, shake flasks, bioreactors, sampling, process monitoring, and harvest.

  • Working knowledge of aseptic technique, contamination control, gowning, controlled-area behavior, and safe handling of biological materials.

  • Experience preparing media, buffers, feeds, and process solutions using controlled recipes and verified calculations.

  • Ability to recognize process or equipment abnormalities, respond appropriately, and escalate issues promptly.

  • Ability to work accurately in a fast-paced CDMO environment where client timelines, quality commitments, and operational priorities may change.

  • Ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams and communicate clearly during shift handoffs and manufacturing escalations.

  • Ability to lift and move materials up to 40 lb (18 kg), stand for extended periods, perform repetitive manipulations, and work in cleanroom garments, subject to applicable accommodation requirements.

  • Availability to support flexible schedules, including early starts, evenings, weekends, holidays, or on-call coverage as manufacturing campaigns require.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in a multi-product CDMO or clinical/commercial biologics manufacturing environment.

  • Experience with single-use bioreactor systems and associated controllers, tubing assemblies, sterile connectors, pumps, and in-process analytical equipment.

  • Experience supporting deviations, investigations, CAPAs, change controls, equipment qualification, or process validation activities.

  • Familiarity with electronic batch records, manufacturing execution systems, LIMS, or electronic document-management systems.

  • Experience with cell line generation or cell line development activities, including transfection, clone screening, cell banking, or cell line characterization. This experience is preferred but not required.

Core competencies

  • GMP discipline and strong attention to detail

  • Aseptic execution and contamination-control mindset

  • Reliable batch-record and data-integrity practices

  • Technical learning agility and practical troubleshooting

  • Clear communication, teamwork, and accountability

  • Safety focus and consistent procedural compliance

Working environment

The position involves work in laboratory and GMP manufacturing environments with biological materials, cleaning and disinfecting agents, process equipment, controlled access, and cleanroom gowning requirements. Work may be performed across multiple shifts to support manufacturing campaigns and client commitments.

Role emphasis

Primary requirement: hands-on GMP upstream manufacturing experience and reliable execution in a regulated environment. Nice to have: cell line generation or broader CLD experience.

title: Telemetry Technician (EKG) PRN
description:
Highpoint Health with Ascension Saint Thomas – Lawrenceburg

Job Title: Telemetry Technician

Job Type: PRN

Schedule: 4 Shifts per Month

Your experience matters

Highpoint Health – Lawrenceburg with Ascension Saint Thomas is part of Lifepoint Health, a diversified healthcare delivery network with facilities coast to coast. We are driven by a commitment to prioritize your well-being so you can provide exceptional care to others.

As a Telemetry Technician joining our team, you’ll play an important role in supporting safe, high-quality patient care. We are seeking candidates with healthcare experience who are comfortable monitoring patients, recognizing changes in cardiac rhythms, and communicating concerns promptly to the nursing team.

LPNs, experienced Telemetry Technicians, EMTs, and Paramedics are encouraged to apply.

Join us in our mission of Making Communities Healthier®, where your skills, compassion, and dedication can make a meaningful difference in the lives of those we serve.

How you'll contribute

A Telemetry Technician who excels in this role will:

  • Perform continuous monitoring of cardiac telemetry for multiple patients.
  • Identify and recognize abnormal heart rhythms and changes in cardiac patterns.
  • Observe for signs of patient distress and immediately communicate concerns to nursing staff.
  • Notify nursing staff of abnormal telemetry findings or changes in patient condition.
  • Identify and correct monitor artifacts to help ensure accurate readings.
  • Test telemetry equipment to ensure proper functioning.
  • Report equipment malfunctions or concerns to the appropriate supervisor.
  • Perform patient-care support duties as assigned and within the employee's training, credentials, and scope of practice.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision in a fast-paced healthcare environment.
  • Use critical thinking and sound judgment when responding to changes in patient status.

What we're looking for

Candidates should have healthcare experience appropriate for the responsibilities of the position. We especially welcome applicants with backgrounds or credentials such as:

  • Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)
  • Telemetry Technician / Monitor Technician
  • Emergency Medical Technician (EMT)
  • Advanced EMT (AEMT)
  • Paramedic (EMT-P)
  • Previous cardiac monitoring or arrhythmia-recognition experience is highly valued.

title: IAM Security IT Architect
description:
At Azqore, we understand that information security is more than a necessity – it’s a passion. That’s why we’re looking for an security architect who shares our commitment to excellence and the protection of our banking partners.

Role purpose

The IAM Security IT Architect defines and governs secure application architectures, with a strong focus on digital identity, authentication, federation, and authorization. The role translates business, regulatory, and cybersecurity requirements into scalable architecture patterns and guides delivery teams from design through implementation and operation.

Your main responsibilities:

  • Define target architectures, principles, standards, and reusable patterns for secure applications and APIs. Design authentication, federation, authorization, and session-management solutions across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments.

  • Assess the existing SSO federation landscape and propose a technical rationalisation programme, including target-state architecture, platform consolidation opportunities, migration priorities, dependencies, risks, and a phased implementation roadmap.

  • Define and govern authentication patterns for native and cross-platform mobile applications, including OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, secure system-browser or broker-based sign-in, deep-link and redirect URI protection, device binding, biometric re-authentication, and secure token storage using platform-provided keystores.

  • Support projects during early-stage architecture and solution design, helping teams assess options, define secure target designs, and address identity and application security requirements before implementation.

  • Lead architecture decisions for SSO using SAML 2.0, OpenID Connect, WS-Federation, and OAuth 2.0 and specify secure token lifecycles, claims models, trust relationships, certificate management, key rotation, and logout patterns.

  • Define, document, maintain, and promote enterprise authentication and federation standards, implementation guidelines, and reusable patterns for software developers.

  • Participate in troubleshooting sessions with production and operations teams responsible for API gateways, supporting the diagnosis and resolution of authentication, authorization, token, federation, and integration issues.

  • Participate in the IAM team’s on-call rotation, providing operational support beyond authentication services and contributing to incident diagnosis, escalation, and resolution across the team’s technology portfolio, including CyberArk Privileged Access Management (PAM), Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and Hardware Security Module/Key Management System (HSM/KMS) services.

  • Maintain architecture documentation, decision records, reference implementations, and technology roadmaps.

Profile:

Required Technical Expertise:

  • Advanced knowledge of SAML 2.0, OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, and WS-Federation, including protocol flows, assertions, tokens, scopes, claims, and trust models

  • Strong command of authentication methods, including phishing-resistant MFA, FIDO2-based passwordless authentication as well as Passkey, adaptive access, and step-up authentication.

  • Hands-on knowledge of identity and federation platforms, ideally including WSO2 Identity Server, Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS), Microsoft Entra ID (SSO and Conditional Accesses), and Keycloak. But other experiences in other solutions like Okta, Ping Identity or Forgerock will be considered.

  • Good understanding of SPA security architecture, including browser-based threat models, secure use of tokens, cross-origin controls, and the security benefits and trade-offs of the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern.

  • Optional Working knowledge of privileged access management, PKI, cryptographic key management, and hardware security technologies; exposure to CyberArk PAM and enterprise HSM/KMS platforms is highly desirable.

  • Familiarity with zero-trust principles, cloud security architecture, container platforms, CI/CD security, and infrastructure as code.

  • Ability to interpret regulatory, audit, and risk requirements and translate them into effective technical controls.

Qualifications and Experience :

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, information systems, engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

  • Typically ten or more years of experience in IT IAM architecture, application security, IAM, software engineering, or related fields.

  • Demonstrated experience designing and governing enterprise authentication and federation solutions.

  • Proven ability to influence multidisciplinary teams and communicate complex risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Certifications in the administration of authentication, identity, or federation platforms are considered an advantage.

  • Certifications in offensive web application security and web penetration testing are considered an advantage.

  • CISSP certification is considered an advantage; other relevant certifications such as Microsoft SC-300 or SC-100 are also desirable.

Benefits at Azqore:

  • Generous healthcare contribution (300 CHF/month).

  • 27 days of annual leave for work-life balance.

  • Attractive pension plan (“LPP”).

  • Extended paternity leave of 1 month.

  • Embrace flexibility with our flex office policy.

Who is Azqore ?

Azqore is a leader in outsourced banking services. We are one of the entities under Credit Agricole Indosuez Wealth Management, providing integrated solutions to our clients : with our core banking system and the solution of outsourcing of backoffice banking operations.

Backed up by the banking and financial strength of Crédit Agricole Group with its global presence and resources made available by Capgemini under our strategic agreement and positioned as the expert partner for the digital transformation of tomorrow's Wealth Managers with a single ambition: to make S2i the technology and banking operations platform of choice for the Wealth Managers in its international markets.

Our business has a single purpose : building partnerships with tomorrow's Private Bankers and Wealth Managers.

title: Structured Originator
description:
⚡️ What We Do

Flower is Flexible Power. We are a next-gen energy company leveraging AI and machine learning to make renewable energy stable and always available – even when the sun isn’t shining and the wind isn’t blowing.

Through smart optimization and trading of energy assets like wind and solar farms, battery systems, and EV chargers, we make renewable energy reliable and predictable, leading the charge towards the energy system of tomorrow.

🌟 Who We Are

Tech company at heart. Purpose-driven at core. Flower consists of a diverse group of innovative individuals with a strong desire to improve the state of the world.

At Flower, we believe trust, collaboration and diversity are essential to not only create an inclusive work environment, but also drive career growth. By embracing varying perspectives, we allow creativity and progress to flourish.

To accelerate towards our goal of becoming the pioneering force powering the energy system of tomorrow, we are now looking for an experienced Structured Originator to join us.

👩‍💻 About The Role

As Structured Originator, you’ll turn complex energy opportunities into carefully structured, executable transactions. You’ll understand how the words in a contract translate into value—and know how to negotiate an agreement that balances commercial opportunity with risk.

You’ll lead the structuring and valuation of bespoke, long-term deals, including flexibility purchase agreements (FPAs) for Flower-developed battery energy storage projects, buy- and sell-side power purchase agreements (PPAs), hedging contracts and non-standard optimization agreements.

Working closely with our origination team, you’ll help shape opportunities and take a leading role in negotiations. The lines aren’t rigid, though: you’ll also bring your own relationships and market insight, keep a finger on the pulse of the industry and help identify larger deals. You’ll be comfortable leading substantial contract negotiations independently, while bringing colleagues together to get the best outcome.

Your counterparties will include utilities, trading houses, independent power producers and infrastructure investors. Your work will help Flower secure contracted revenues and create long-term, risk-adjusted value across our portfolio.

What You’ll Do

  • Structure, value and execute complex energy transactions, partnering with origination and other teams from initial opportunity through to signing

  • Build and maintain relationships with sophisticated counterparties, using your network and market insight to help identify larger opportunities

  • Lead or co-lead negotiations, draft term sheets and work cross-functionally on long-form agreements that support project financing requirements

  • Develop pricing and valuation models, assess embedded optionality and transaction risks, and shape appropriate risk allocation, hedging and credit mitigation

  • Prepare transaction papers for investment and risk committees, and contribute to Flower’s valuation standards, contract frameworks and commercial strategy

Who You Are

You’re a strong negotiator who can see both the detail in a contract and the commercial opportunity behind it. You’re comfortable owning complex discussions with senior counterparties, but you know that the best deals also depend on close collaboration internally.

We believe you have:

  • Several years of experience in structuring, origination, trading or valuation, with a proven track record of executing complex energy transactions

  • Deep experience negotiating sophisticated contracts such as tolling agreements, buy- and sell-side PPAs, optimization agreements and hedging contracts

  • An established network in the energy industry and a good understanding of where larger opportunities may emerge

  • Advanced financial modelling and valuation skills, including long-dated and option-based structures, as well as a strong understanding of market, volume, credit and operational risk

  • Solid knowledge of Nordic and wider European power and flexibility markets, and experience with project-financed transactions

  • A degree in finance, economics, engineering, mathematics or another relevant quantitative field, and fluency in English

You may have gained your experience at a utility, IPP, trading house, investor or advisory firm, or in investment banking. Swedish language skills and a CFA, FRM or equivalent qualification are a plus.
